raw_facts.fact: Belgium host France on Monday, 28 September 2026 at 20:45 local time (18:45 UTC) at the King Baudouin Stadium in Brussels. It is matchday 2 of League A Group 1 in the 2026/27 UEFA Nations League.

France won 1-0 away to Turkey in their Nations League opener, Zinedine Zidane's first game as France coach. Kylian Mbappé scored the winner in the 55th minute, set up by Michael Olise, but hurt his left knee moments later.

Mbappé is leaving the France camp and will miss the rest of the international window, including the Belgium match. Real Madrid diagnosed an overstretching of the posterior capsule of his left knee. Zidane said: 'he is going to have to go home. We don't want to take any risks.'
Belgium won their opener 2-0 against Italy, with goals from Mika Godts and Dodi Lukebakio. It was Belgium's first clean sheet in five matches.
After matchday 1, Belgium and France both have 3 points. Belgium are 1st in the group and France 2nd.
Belgium have lost each of their last five meetings with France, a run going back to June 2015.
Belgium are unbeaten in 9 home games against all opponents since November 2024 (6 wins, 3 draws).
France have won 8 and drawn 1 of their last 9 away matches.
The all-time record, from Belgium's side, is 30 wins, 19 draws and 25 losses against France, with 160 goals scored and 128 conceded. In the last 6 meetings France won 5 and Belgium 1, with no draws.
Recent meetings include France 2-0 Belgium in the Nations League on 2024-09-09. The most recent meeting was a 3-2 France win over Belgium.
Belgium are without Leandro Trossard (heel injury). Apart from Mbappé, France have no reported absentees.

Both teams have new coaches. Mark van Bommel took over Belgium on 15 August, replacing Rudi Garcia, who had taken Belgium to the 2026 World Cup quarter-finals. Zidane replaced Didier Deschamps as France coach after 14 years, and the Belgium match is his second game in charge.
Only the result after 90 minutes plus stoppage time counts. A draw resolves both the France and Belgium questions as 'No'.

A first-round win requires more than 50% of valid votes; blank and null votes are excluded. Otherwise the top two meet in the Oct 25 runoff, and the question counts the runoff result.

Since re-election was allowed in 1997, 3 of 4 sitting presidents who ran again won: Cardoso in 1998, Lula in 2006 and Rousseff in 2014. Jair Bolsonaro lost to Lula in 2022, 50.9% to 49.1% in the runoff.

The newest item on the White House presidential actions page is the Gold Star Mother's and Family's Day proclamation of Sept 25, 2026. None of the actions listed from Sept 16–25 (including H-1B, angling, hunting and procurement orders) mentions artificial intelligence, super intelligence or renaming AI.

In his Sept 22, 2026 UN General Assembly speech, Trump said the federal government would rename AI 'super intelligence.' He said that 'from this point forward, all of United States documents' would use 'super' instead of 'artificial.'

Breaking Defense reported that Trump gave the directive verbally at the UN, citing no signed executive order or formal memo, and said 'As of yet, there is no official announcement from the White House on how this is to be implemented.'

Michael Drager, a Deputy Assistant Secretary in the State Department's international organizations bureau, sent staff an email titled 'Change in Nomenclature AI to SI.' Citing 'the president's remarks at the GA today,' it told them to replace 'Artificial Intelligence' with 'Super Intelligence' in all remarks, positions and press elements. It was an agency email, not a presidential document.

US representatives had already started using 'SI' at UN Security Council meetings. Euronews said it was unclear whether the directive applied beyond the State Department's international organizations bureau.

This explainer said no executive order or Federal Register filing had yet made the 'Super Intelligence' switch binding. It said existing federal orders and the AI Action Plan still use 'Artificial Intelligence.'

Before the speech, Trump posted a social media poll offering 'superior intelligence,' 'extreme intelligence' and 'supreme intelligence' as new names for AI. 'Super intelligence,' the name he announced, was not one of the poll options.
According to Gizmodo's headline, the White House said Trump got China's Xi Jinping to agree to call AI 'super intelligence.' Trump posted that Xi 'seemed to like' the idea.

Trump's earlier renamings in his second term included changing the Gulf of Mexico to 'Gulf of America' by executive order and renaming Lake Ontario 'Lake America' in August 2026 during a trade dispute with Canada.
Breaking Defense noted that Trump appointees have pushed earlier terminology changes, such as 'War Department' for 'Defense Department,' and that those changes have not always gained legal status.

Only a signed executive order, proclamation or presidential memorandum counts, and it must be signed by 11:59 PM ET on Sept 30, 2026. Speeches, social media posts and polls do not count. An agency-level email such as the State Department's does not count unless it is itself a presidential action.

The National reported that the East-West pipeline had restarted and was pumping at a low rate. Its only sources were unnamed Reuters sources and satellite-data analysis. The article cited no statement from Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Energy, the government or Aramco.

The Reuters story, headlined 'Saudi Arabia restarts East-West oil pipeline, to resume exports from Yanbu, sources say', credits the restart to unnamed sources. Aramco was trying to bring flow back to 4 million bpd, below the system's full capacity of 7 million bpd.

The Saudi-owned Asharq Al-Awsat also carried the restart under the headline 'Sources: Saudi Arabia Restarts East-West Oil Pipeline', so the report is again attributed to sources and not to an official announcement.
Sources said reaching about 40% of capacity would take a couple of days and a full restart would take 6 to 8 weeks. Another source put the full restart at up to six weeks.

Pumping has resumed at reduced rates, and tanker loadings at Yanbu appear to have restarted this week, but regular exports have not recovered. Two tankers due to load on September 23 had not loaded, and six more were scheduled for September 24–27.

Sources said volumes on the East-West pipeline were building but tanker loading at Yanbu was delayed. Reuters reported that Aramco told European refiners it first needed to build a 'critical mass' of crude at Yanbu.
Industrial Info Resources cited satellite imagery showing vessels loading crude at Yanbu after the pipeline attack.

The Ministry of Energy's statement on SPA was headlined 'East–West Pipeline Shut Down as a Precaution Following Multiple Attacks'. The ministry also posted it on X and said emergency teams were deployed to secure the pipeline and assess its safety.

Saudi Arabia shut the East-West crude pipeline after several drone attacks launched from Iraq hit it in the Riyadh and Medina regions. Satellite imagery and industry sources reported that 3 of its 11 pumping stations were damaged.

There is a precedent from April 2026. On April 9 the Ministry of Energy said attacks had cut about 700,000 bpd of East-West pipeline capacity, and around April 12 it announced on SPA that full pumping capacity of about 7 million bpd had been restored.

Argaam carried the April Ministry of Energy statement that the energy facilities and the East-West line had recovered and regained their operating capacity. The ministry has made such a restoration announcement at least once before.

The 1,200 km pipeline links the eastern oil fields to the Red Sea port of Yanbu and has been rerouting about 4 million bpd around the Strait of Hormuz. The Saudi Foreign Ministry said Riyadh would hold off retaliating to give Iraq's government time to stop attacks from its territory.
The US Energy Secretary said the Saudi East-West pipeline would be back in operation within days. This came from a third party (not the Saudi government) and was about the future.

The questions resolve Yes only if official Saudi government information says the pipeline is operating now; partial capacity counts. Reports from anonymous sources or third parties, satellite data, and forward-looking statements do not count. Searches through 2026-09-27 found no Saudi official statement confirming the September restart.

Figueiredo vs. Talbott is still booked for UFC 332 on October 3, 2026 in Salt Lake City and has been moved up to the co-main event. Figueiredo has defended the card against fan criticism, and no injury or withdrawal has been reported for either fighter.

UFC 332 takes place Saturday, October 3, 2026 at the Delta Center in Salt Lake City and has 13 bouts. The bantamweight co-main is Payton Talbott (11-1) vs. Deiveson Figueiredo (25-7-1). The main event is Natalia Silva vs. Wang Cong for the vacant women's flyweight title, and the main card airs on CBS/Paramount+.

Figueiredo (born December 18, 1987; age 38) is 25-7-1. He has lost 4 of his last 5 fights: a UD loss to Petr Yan (Nov 2024), a TKO loss to Cory Sandhagen from a knee injury (May 2025), a split-decision win over Montel Jackson (Oct 2025), a UD loss to Umar Nurmagomedov (Jan 2026) and a round-2 guillotine submission loss to Song Yadong (May 30, 2026).

Before that losing run, Figueiredo won 4 straight at bantamweight: Rob Font (UD, Dec 2023), Cody Garbrandt (RNC sub, Apr 2024), Marlon Vera (UD, Aug 2024), plus the Jackson win later. He is a former two-time UFC flyweight champion.

Talbott (born September 9, 1998) is 11-1. He has 7 wins by KO/TKO, 1 by submission and 3 by decision. His only loss was a unanimous decision to Raoni Barcelos in January 2025, and his last fight was a unanimous-decision win over Henry Cejudo at UFC 323 on December 6, 2025.
Talbott hasn't fought in 2026; he will have been out about 10 months by fight night. He said he has been training a lot and was 'just detoxing for a second' from public life.

The UFC 332 main event changed after Valentina Shevchenko gave up the women's flyweight title because of back and shoulder injuries, which led to the Figueiredo–Talbott fight moving to co-main. This event is in the U.S. (Utah), and Talbott is from Nevada (Reno).

UFC 332 is scheduled for October 3, 2026 at the Delta Center in Salt Lake City, Utah. The main event is Natália Silva vs. Wang Cong for the vacant UFC Women's Flyweight Championship. The card lists no replacements or changes to the main event.

The UFC announced Silva vs. Wang Cong during the UFC Paris broadcast. Champion Valentina Shevchenko withdrew from her planned fight with Silva because of a back and shoulder ligament injury expected to sideline her for about a year, and the title was vacated.

Silva's pro MMA record is 20-5-1: 5 KO, 7 submission, 7 decision and 1 DQ wins. She is 8-0 in the UFC, ranked #1 at flyweight and #4 pound-for-pound. Her last fight was a unanimous decision win over Rose Namajunas at UFC 324 on January 24, 2026.
Silva is on a 14-fight win streak. Her last three wins were over former champions Rose Namajunas, Alexa Grasso and Jessica Andrade.

September polls disagree widely. Channel 14 has Likud 32, Yashar 22 and the right-wing bloc at 63. i24NEWS has Likud 27, Yashar 22 and the coalition at 60. Maariv has Yashar 22, Likud 18, coalition 49 and Zionist opposition 55. N12 has Yashar 23, Likud 20, coalition 50 and opposition 66 (54 Zionist + 12 Arab). Channel 13 has Yashar 22, Likud 18, opposition 52 and coalition 51.
Averaged across the polls, Likud has 23 seats, Eisenkot's Yashar 22.2, Bennett–Lapid's B'Yachad 10.6 and the Arab parties 12.4. Likud's figure ranges from 18 to 32 seats depending on the pollster.

The Channel 13 poll gave Eisenkot's bloc 52 seats and Netanyahu's bloc 51. Neither reaches the 61 needed to govern. Hendel's Reservists party crossed the threshold with 4 seats for the first time in Channel 13 polling.

In an average of mainstream polls, Netanyahu's bloc (including Winter) is at 53.6 seats and the Zionist opposition bloc at 53.4. The non-Arab opposition cannot reach a majority without the Arab parties, which win about 12 seats.

On September 26, 2026, the opposition leaders signed a declaration of principles to cooperate in the run-up to the October 27 election. The signers were Gadi Eisenkot (Yashar), Avigdor Liberman (Yisrael Beiteinu), Yair Golan (The Democrats), and Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid (Together).

President Herzog said that if neither bloc reaches 61 seats he will 'do everything so that there will not be repeat elections,' and he raised unity or rotation governments as options. He also suggested the Netanyahu pardon question could come into compromise talks. Netanyahu's trial is ongoing, and he has reportedly not answered Herzog's proposal to mediate a plea deal.

Haredi parties are reportedly preparing a possible shift in strategy after the election. They may not recommend any prime minister candidate at first and may stay outside the new coalition until the draft-law crisis is resolved.

Eisenkot says the Jewish opposition parties (Yashar, Beyahad, Yisrael Beiteinu, Democrats) will win 61 or more seats without Arab parties. No mainstream poll has shown either bloc at 61. Bennett–Lapid and Liberman have ruled out Arab parties in a future coalition, and Netanyahu's campaign attacks Eisenkot over possible reliance on Arab parties.

The Knesset dissolved on July 17, 2026, and election day is October 27, 2026. Diplomatic voting is on October 20, and official results are confirmed on November 4, 2026. Candidate lists were due September 8, and the electoral threshold is 3.25%.

The question resolves only when a prime minister is formally sworn in after the 2026 election. A caretaker prime minister, including Netanyahu staying on as interim PM, does not count. The questions close on October 27, 2026, which is election day and comes before any government can be sworn in.

Recent gaps from election to swearing-in: 404 days from April 2019 to May 14, 2020, spanning three elections; about 81 days after March 23, 2021 (Bennett–Lapid government sworn in June 13, 2021); about 58 days after November 1, 2022 (Netanyahu sworn in December 29, 2022).

Of the five elections from April 2019 to November 2022, 3 led to a sworn-in government (2020 Netanyahu–Gantz rotation, 2021 Bennett–Lapid, 2022 Netanyahu). The April 2019 and September 2019 elections produced no government. Netanyahu became PM after 2 of those 3 formations.

No executive order, memorandum or other formal presidential document renaming AI had been signed. The article said: "As of yet, there is no official announcement from the White House on how this is to be implemented."
The article reported that there had been no executive order about 'super intelligence' yet, and that it was unclear what, if anything, would follow from the announcement.

In his September 22 speech to the UN General Assembly, Trump said that 'from this point forward, all of United States documents' would use 'super intelligence' instead of 'artificial intelligence'. The announcement was made in a speech, not a signed order.

The State Department's international organisations bureau told staff to switch terms in an email from Deputy Assistant Secretary Michael Drager titled 'Change in Nomenclature AI to SI'. The email said: 'Following the president's remarks at the GA today, please change all references of Artificial Intelligence to Super Intelligence.' It was an agency email, not a presidential order.

On September 19, Trump posted a poll on X and Truth Social asking which name should replace 'Artificial Intelligence': Superior, Extreme or Supreme Intelligence. 'Superior Intelligence' had about 39% on X, and the poll drew more than 140,000 votes within a day.
On September 21, Trump posted on Truth Social that he would 'only encourage AI or, SI (SUPER INTELLIGENCE)!', the day before his UN speech.
Trump said he had pitched the 'super intelligence' rebrand to Chinese President Xi Jinping and claimed Xi liked the idea.

Earlier Trump renamings were done by executive order: the Gulf of Mexico became the 'Gulf of America' by executive order in 2025. In August 2026 Lake Ontario was renamed 'Lake America' during a trade dispute with Canada.

The 'Department of War' secondary title for the Defense Department was also made formal by an executive order, signed on September 5, 2025, after officials said it was coming. The Gulf of America order was signed on January 20, 2025, about two weeks after Trump first floated the name on January 7.

The window closes on September 30, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET, about 2–3 days from today. Only a signed executive order, proclamation or presidential memorandum counts; speeches, social media posts and agency emails do not. The primary resolution source is whitehouse.gov and the Federal Register.

The seasonally adjusted unemployment rate for August 2026 was 4.1%, the same as July. The number of unemployed people changed little at 7.0 million.
The labor force participation rate was 61.6% in August 2026, down 0.5 percentage points since January.
Nonfarm payrolls rose by 162,000 in August 2026. In the household survey, employment rose 569,000 and 683,000 people joined the labor force. The U-6 rate fell to 7.7%.

The 2026 path of the unemployment rate was reported as: April 4.3%, May 4.3%, June 4.2%, July 4.1%, August 4.1%. That is a slow decline of about 0.1 point or less per month. Figures reported for January and February (4.7%) and March (4.3%) were not seasonally adjusted.
BLS reported that the unemployment rate was unchanged at 4.3% in May 2026.
A year earlier, in September 2025, the unemployment rate was 4.4%.

Initial jobless claims were 197,000 for the week ending September 19, 2026, down 1,000. The 4-week average fell to 202,250. Prior weeks: 206,000 (Sept 5) and 196,000 (Sept 12), which is the survey reference week for the September household survey.
The September 2026 Employment Situation report is scheduled for Friday, October 2, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. ET (12:30 UTC). The question closes at 12:29 UTC that day.
Congress passed a continuing resolution extending federal funding past the September 30 deadline to December 11. The House vote was 370-48, so no shutdown should disrupt the October 2 BLS release.
Precedent: in the 2025 shutdown, the September 2025 report was delayed more than 6 weeks. The October 2025 household survey was never conducted, so no unemployment rate was published for that month.

BLS publishes the seasonally adjusted U-3 rate rounded to one decimal place. The threshold 'above 3.9%' means 4.0% or higher. From August's 4.1%, the rate would have to fall 0.2 points or more to resolve No.

The latest IMF PortWatch daily figure quoted in the 28 Sep brief is for 2026-09-20: 1 transit through Hormuz, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. PortWatch data for Sep 21–27 was not yet shown in any source found.
September 2026 is the quietest month of the year so far, with 78 transits recorded from Sep 1 through Sep 20. That averages about 3.9 per day, or about 27 per 7-day period.

From Jan 1 to Sep 20, 2026 there were 5,367 transits, an average of 20.4 per day. That is 77% below the 23,796 logged over the same span of 2025, and the average includes the pre-closure weeks before Feb 28.
IMF PortWatch recorded 8 transits through Hormuz on 2026-09-13, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day.

Reuters-reported tracking data counted 10 commodity-vessel crossings on Wednesday Sep 23 (9 inbound, 1 outbound) and 7 on Tuesday Sep 22, against a 10-day average of about 17. That tracker counts differently from PortWatch.

One outlet citing a US official put Wednesday Sep 23 traffic at around 60 ships. Totals vary widely depending on whether they count all vessel types, only commodity carriers, or only AIS-visible ships.
Windward counted 24 vessels transiting Hormuz on Sep 27 (9 inbound, 15 outbound), 14 of them dark (AIS off), including five inbound tankers of up to 333m. 11 of the 24 used the south corridor.
PortWatch transit counts are based on AIS data. IMF warns of GPS jamming, AIS spoofing and vessels going dark in the conflict, so dark transits that other trackers count may not appear in PortWatch.
On Sep 27 Trump rejected Iran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a seven-day phased roadmap in exchange for sanctions relief. He said the U.S. will 'win' the Iran war 'very soon'.
As of Sep 28, 248 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth near the strait (281 on Sep 26), and throughput remained a small fraction of normal. Brent was at $106.19.

As of early September, PortWatch Hormuz flows were at about 1% of pre-war levels: single-digit daily transits against a pre-crisis baseline of 80–90+. PortWatch data is published with a lag of several days.

The result is the sum of PortWatch daily transit calls for Sep 21–27, 2026. It resolves no earlier than Tuesday Sep 29 at 9 AM, once complete data is available. The market closes 2026-09-29 13:00 UTC.

On Monday, September 28, Saudi Arabia resumed crude exports through the East-West Pipeline from Yanbu, ending a 17-day export halt. The only source was Bloomberg's 'person with direct knowledge'. Saudi Aramco and the Saudi energy ministry did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Reuters reported on September 22, citing unnamed sources, that Saudi Arabia had restored operations on the East-West pipeline. The report included no official Saudi confirmation. Under the rules, claims attributed to third parties do not qualify.

A search of SPA's English site found the September shutdown statement ('East–West Pipeline Shut Down as a Precaution Following Multiple Attacks') and condemnations from other countries. It found no Ministry of Energy statement after the shutdown saying the pipeline is operating again.

The Ministry of Energy said the East–West Pipeline in the Riyadh and Madinah regions was hit by multiple drone attacks launched from Iraq on the morning of September 10, 2026, and was shut down as a precaution. It said the attacks caused injuries and some damage that was being addressed.

Sources said Saudi Arabia restarted the East-West Pipeline on September 22 at a low pumping rate, with Aramco trying to get back to 4 million bpd. A security source said reaching 40% of capacity would take a couple of days and a full restart six to eight weeks.
On September 22, Bloomberg reported that Saudi Arabia was running tests to resume the East-West oil pipeline.
US Energy Secretary Chris Wright, a US official rather than a Saudi one, described the Saudi pipeline closure as a brief interruption that would last days.

In April 2026, attacks cut about 700,000 bpd of East-West pipeline capacity. The Ministry of Energy then issued an official SPA statement on April 12 saying full pumping capacity of about 7 million bpd had been restored. Precedent: the ministry has formally announced a restoration of this pipeline before.

The latest IMF PortWatch daily count for the Strait of Hormuz is 1 vessel transit on 2026-09-20. Before the crisis, traffic averaged about 85 per day. As of the Sept 29 brief, no PortWatch day after Sept 20 had been reported.

PortWatch recorded 3 zero-transit days at Hormuz between March 1, 2026 and the Sept 20 data. The previous seven years of the series had none. Two of the three zero days came in March 2026, when transits averaged 4.8 per day.
PortWatch counted 5,367 Hormuz transits from Jan 1 to Sept 20, 2026, an average of 20.4 per day. Year-to-date transits are 77% below the same period of 2025.
Other PortWatch daily counts at Hormuz: 6 transits on Aug 30, 6 on Sept 6 and 8 on Sept 13. The next reported day, Sept 20, dropped to 1.

PortWatch updates its daily chokepoint transit data weekly, on Tuesdays at 9 AM ET, with about a two-day lag, so the newest day is usually 2 to 9 days old. Sept 29, 2026 is a Tuesday, which puts the next release after that on Oct 6.
PortWatch builds its transit counts from satellite AIS signals. Ships sailing with AIS turned off ('dark' transits) may not appear in its counts.

Windward counted 24 vessels transiting Hormuz on Sept 27, 14 of them dark (including five tankers), and 21 transits on Sept 26 (9 via the southern corridor). These figures come from Windward, not PortWatch.

The most recent incident is a VLCC reported on fire after a new ship strike in the strait, as Iran-US talks fizzle out. Ships are reported transiting with AIS off and moving cargo through ship-to-ship relays.

US and Iranian envoys were reported to be discussing a phased deal to reopen the strait, but Iran's security chief said 'no step-by-step process exists.' 80 countries at the UN demanded the strait be reopened. The bulk carrier Cape Dao was attacked on Sept 23, killing one person.

raw_facts.source: Wikipedia – List of ships attacked during the 2026 Iran war
raw_facts.fact: Ships were struck in the strait on consecutive days: the LPG carrier AL MARYAH (Sept 20), the tanker LR STEPHANIE (Sept 21, inbound on the southern corridor) and an unidentified cargo ship on Sept 23 that caught fire, with two casualties.

In August 2026, Argus reported that no vessels left the strait in a 24-hour period, after an Iranian attack on a tanker in the US-supported southern corridor. The date is approximate and the count is outbound only; this is not a PortWatch figure.
The strait has been effectively closed to commercial shipping for 212 days, since Feb 28, 2026. On Sept 24, 399 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Gulf watch box.

raw_facts.source: Independent (via search summary of Yahoo/ tech-ish coverage)
raw_facts.fact: Reporting found that no formal executive order or binding federal directive for the name change had been confirmed. As of the evening of September 22, the White House had not published an executive order or a memo telling agencies to switch, and ai.gov still used 'artificial intelligence' throughout.

The State Department told diplomats to use 'Super Intelligence' (SI) in all communications. The instruction came in an email from Deputy Assistant Secretary Michael Drager titled 'Change in Nomenclature AI to SI,' which referred to 'the president's remarks at the GA.' This was an agency email, not a presidential action.
Euronews reported Trump had 'ordered officials' to call AI 'super intelligence.' The order described is the UN speech remark plus State Department follow-up, not a published executive order.

On about September 25, the White House said Chinese President Xi Jinping agreed to call AI 'super intelligence,' and Trump said Xi likes his rebranding plan. In the search results, none of this coverage mentions a signed presidential document.

Before the UN speech, Trump suggested renaming AI, and he and the White House ran polls on X and Truth Social. The options were 'superior intelligence,' 'extreme intelligence' and 'supreme intelligence.' 'Super intelligence' was not one of them.

The most recent AI executive order that turned up in searches is 'Promoting Advanced Artificial Intelligence Innovation and Security,' signed June 2, 2026. It uses the term 'Artificial Intelligence.' Searches found no presidential action on whitehouse.gov that renames AI.

Trump has made past renames official by executive order. Executive Order 14347 of September 5, 2025 restored 'Department of War' as a secondary title, following weeks of public comments. On January 20, 2025, an executive order renamed the Gulf of Mexico the 'Gulf of America.'

The question closes October 1, 2026 at 03:59 UTC, about two days from today. To resolve Yes, the President must personally sign a presidential action that adopts the replacement name for US official use. Speeches and agency-only emails such as the State Department's do not count.

raw_facts.fact: Investing.com's daily WTI futures data puts the lowest September 2026 low at $86.13, on September 1. Every other September session's low was $88.58 or higher. None of the daily lows for September 1–30 reached $85. This is continuous front-month data, not Pyth 1-minute candles.
Early on September 30, WTI futures were at $89.06, with a session range so far of $89.00–$89.06. That is about $4 (roughly 4.5%) above $85.
On September 29, WTI opened at $93.53 and traded between $94.72 and $88.58 before closing at $89.05. That $88.58 low was the lowest level since the September 1 session.

The August 31 session had a low of $84.11 and closed at $85.76. The September 1 session, which starts at 6 PM ET on August 31, opened at $86.31 and bottomed at $86.13. So the sub-$85 trade happened in an August session, before September's trading began.

On September 30, oil steadied after its biggest drop in more than a week. WTI was slipping toward $89 and Brent was near $103. Middle East crude exports had rebounded to 17.5 million barrels a day, 98% of pre-war levels.

On September 29, WTI fell about 3.5% to around $89.38 and Brent fell 2.6% to $102.59. The drop came as Saudi crude exports from its Red Sea ports recovered after an attack on a key pipeline earlier in the month.
On September 28, WTI settled at $92.60 after reaching $96.54 intraday. Prices came off their highs on reports that Saudi Arabia was ramping its East-West pipeline back up after repairs.

WTI's September peak was a high of $105.63 on September 16. The price then fell to around $89–92 in the last two weeks of the month, as U.S.-Iran truce hopes and a recovery in Saudi supply weighed on it.

Only one session is left: September 30, which ends at 5:00 PM ET. The market closes at 03:59:59 UTC on October 1, which is 11:59 PM ET on September 30. The active month is the November 2026 contract (CLX26), because October CL's last trade was around September 22 and the roll happened around the September 18 session.

Bloomberg reported that flows through the East-West pipeline to the Red Sea had reached at least 3.5 million b/d after repairs, about half of its 7 million b/d capacity. The report adds that neither the Saudi Energy Ministry nor Saudi Aramco had made any public statement on the pipeline since the attack. The information came from people familiar with the matter.

The article's timeline gives the restart on September 22, 2026 at minimal capacity, citing unnamed Reuters sources, and says full recovery could take 6 to 8 weeks. It cites no Ministry of Energy, Saudi Press Agency (SPA) or Energy Minister statement about the restart.

Three unnamed sources said Saudi Arabia had restarted the East-West Pipeline, which was pumping at a low rate, and that exports from Yanbu could resume. Aramco did not comment, and a security source said a full resumption could take weeks. Before the shutdown the line carried about 4 million b/d.
Bloomberg reported that Saudi Aramco was running tests and building pressure on the East-West pipeline with the aim of restoring significant flows by the end of that week.

Reuters reported that Saudi Arabia had resumed crude loadings at Yanbu after the pipeline restart, averaging about 2 million b/d since the previous week. The report is based on sources and tracking data, not an official government statement.

The Ministry of Energy announced that the East-West Pipeline had been shut down as a precaution after multiple attacks on the morning of September 10 in the Riyadh and Madinah regions. This is the official announcement the question refers to.
US Energy Secretary Chris Wright called the Saudi pipeline closure a brief interruption that would last days. This is a US official's statement, not a Saudi government one.

After attacks on a pumping station in April 2026 cut East-West throughput by 700,000 b/d, the Saudi Ministry of Energy issued a public SPA statement on April 12, 2026 that full pumping capacity of about 7 million b/d had been restored. This shows the ministry has formally announced a pipeline restoration before.

Only an official Saudi government announcement that the pipeline is currently operating (partial capacity counts) qualifies. Media reports citing unnamed sources, Aramco tests, or tanker-tracking data showing flows do not count unless the government itself says the pipeline is operating.
The window for a qualifying Saudi government announcement closes October 15, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. As of September 28 reporting, no official statement on the restart had been found.

raw_facts.source: Wikipedia (2026 United States naval blockade of Iran)
raw_facts.fact: The reimposed US naval blockade of Iranian ports began July 14, 2026, after Trump announced it on July 13. The article says it is still in effect, with no end date announced.
Trump publicly rejected Iran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, saying "They made a proposal but I rejected it." Iran's price for reopening included an end to the US naval blockade.

Iran's plan would reopen Hormuz within 7 days if the US lifts the blockade, waives sanctions, releases $12bn in frozen assets and agrees to a regional ceasefire that includes Lebanon. The US wants all issues, including nuclear, settled together rather than step by step. Araghchi said Iran's position has not changed, and no formal next meeting has been announced.

On September 30, Iran was reported to have received Washington's response to its seven-point proposal through Qatari mediators. The main dispute is said to be the order of steps in the 7-day framework, and the White House is reported to be tempering expectations of an imminent breakthrough.
Reports said Trump expects to resume bombing Iran after the early-November US midterm elections. Officials said he has not made an irrevocable decision to restart major combat.

Trump posted on Truth Social "I offered them NOTHING!" A US official said sanctions relief is possible if there is concrete progress on nuclear issues, but the two sides disagree on timing. The US also imposed new sanctions on Iranian military suppliers.
Axios reported that Trump is willing to ease sanctions and unfreeze assets in exchange for nuclear concessions from Iran. The full article could not be accessed.

Precedent: the first blockade (April 13 to June 18) ended when Trump announced a deal on June 14, signed an MOU on June 17, and CENTCOM formally announced the blockade's removal on June 18. It lasted about 2 months, and the lifting came only as part of a signed war-ending agreement.
By September 12, CENTCOM said it had redirected more than 100 vessels. The WSJ reported in early September that the blockade had halted new Iranian oil exports from the Persian Gulf.

On September 5, the IRGC fired ballistic missiles at a US carrier and a destroyer enforcing the blockade; CENTCOM said neither was hit. Iran threatened more severe attacks if the blockade continues and on September 6 announced a "restricted zone" running south of Hormuz.

No formal US-Iran negotiating session is scheduled before the October 15 deadline. Indirect talks run through Qatar, and the US midterms, which Trump has linked to the timing of a deal, fall in early November, after the question closes.

raw_facts.source: Bureau of Labor Statistics, Employment Situation Summary (August 2026)
raw_facts.fact: The seasonally adjusted U-3 unemployment rate was unchanged at 4.1% in August 2026, with 7.0 million people unemployed. For the September figure to be 3.9% or lower, the rate would have to fall by at least 0.2 percentage points in one month.

Nonfarm payrolls rose 162,000 in August 2026, compared with an average gain of 31,000 a month over the prior 12 months. Unemployment rates were 4.0% for adult men, 3.5% for adult women and 14.1% for teenagers.
Labor force participation edged up to 61.6% in August 2026, still below January's level. June and July payrolls were revised up by a combined 55,000.

The unemployment rate fell from 4.2% in June to 4.1% in July 2026 even though payrolls fell by 23,000. The drop came mainly from people leaving the labor force: participation fell to 61.4%, its lowest in more than five years.
Bloomberg described 4.1% as a one-year low for the unemployment rate, meaning the rate has not been below 4.1% at any point in the past year.
Initial jobless claims were 197,000 for the week ending September 19, 2026, down from 198,000 the week before. Continuing claims fell to 1.719 million.
Jobless claims fell to 196,000 during the holiday week, which included the September CPS survey reference week around September 12. Continuing claims also dropped.
The September 2026 Employment Situation report is scheduled for Friday, October 2, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. ET (12:30 UTC). The question closes one minute earlier, at 12:29 UTC.

The House passed a continuing resolution 370-48, and the Senate had earlier passed it 90-6. It funds the government through December 11, 2026, and was signed into law, so there is no shutdown on October 1 to delay the BLS release (unlike the October 2025 shutdown, which cancelled the October 2025 household survey).
BLS publishes U-3 rounded to one decimal place, from the household survey (CPS). 'Above 3.9%' therefore resolves Yes if the published September rate is 4.0% or higher.

The BTG/Nexus poll (Sept 25–27, 2,000 voters) had Lula at 42% and Flávio Bolsonaro at 37% of total first-round votes, with Caiado and Cury at 5% each. That is a 5-point gap in total votes. The earlier BTG/Nexus poll, released Sept 21, had 40% to 37%.

PoderData (Sept 20–23, 3,000 interviews, margin of error 1.8 points) had Lula at 43% and Flávio at 42% of valid votes, Cury at 6%, Renan Santos at 3% and Caiado at 2%. PoderData's Sept 13–16 poll had 37% to 36%.

Datafolha's early-September poll had Lula at 38%, Flávio Bolsonaro at 32%, Augusto Cury at 7%, and Renan Santos and Ronaldo Caiado at 4% each in the prompted first-round scenario. These look like total-vote shares, a 6-point gap. The simulated runoff was 46% to 44%.
Al Jazeera reported on Sept 25 that a new poll showed Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro still essentially tied.
A September Veritá poll showed Flávio Bolsonaro leading Lula in both the first round and the runoff.
In Quaest's weekly tracking, blank and spoiled ballot intentions rose from 7% to 10%. Pollsters agree Lula leads the first round but differ on the size of the gap.

The main candidates are Lula (PT), Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), Ronaldo Caiado (PSD), Romeu Zema (Novo) and Augusto Cury (Avante), plus six minor candidates. The campaign was affected by the Banco Master and INSS fraud scandals and by a crisis at the Supreme Court from Sept 1 to 23.
The first round is on Oct 4, 2026, and a runoff, if needed, is on Oct 25. The TSE publishes valid-vote percentages on election night.

In the 2022 first round, Lula won 48.43% of valid votes to Jair Bolsonaro's 43.20%, a 5.23-point margin. Final polls had shown a much larger Lula lead: Datafolha's last poll had about 50% to 36% in valid votes, so Bolsonaro was underestimated by several points.
In the 2018 first round, Jair Bolsonaro won 46.03% of valid votes to Fernando Haddad's 29.28%. His vote came in above the final polls.

The margin is the absolute difference in valid-vote percentages between the top two candidates; blank and null votes are excluded. A result exactly on a bracket boundary, such as 5.0 or 10.0, resolves to the higher bracket. The question also requires Lula to finish first.

From 2000 to 2026, 47.1% of NFL regular-season games were decided by 7 points or fewer, so roughly 53% were decided by 8 or more. About 15% of games end with a 3-point margin and about 9% with a 7-point margin. A 7-point win counts as Yes here.
The share of one-score games (margin of 8 or fewer) was 52.7% in 2017-2025, up from 47.9% in 2005-2010. This figure counts both teams, not a specific side winning by 7 or more.
Philadelphia is 2-1 and Los Angeles is 1-2 going into the Week 4 game at Lincoln Financial Field, so the Eagles are at home. If the game ends in a tie, both markets resolve at $0.50.
The Bears beat the Eagles 27-7 on Monday Night Football in Chicago on Sept 28. Case Keenum threw two touchdowns in his first start in almost three years, and the Bears shut down Jalen Hurts.

Seven points was the Eagles' lowest total since 2021 and ended a franchise-record streak of 75 games with at least 10 points. Under new OC Sean Mannion, Philadelphia has thrown a league-low 15 play-action passes in three games, and the paper says the defense under Vic Fangio has declined, with missed tackles and coverage breakdowns.

S Kam Kinchens (hamstring) was limited, returning to practice for the first time since Week 1.

The Eagles have won 4 straight meetings with the Rams, including a win last season that the Inquirer called a 'signature win'. Four games is a small sample, and I could not confirm the count from a primary source.

The Giants have 1 sack in 3 games. Only Miami, with 0, has fewer, and most teams have 6 or more. SI lists Arizona S Dadrion Taylor-Demerson as questionable.
Arizona (1-2) plays at the NY Giants (2-1) at MetLife Stadium on Sunday 2026-10-04 at 1:00 PM ET, on CBS.

Unverified and not from a cited source: in recent NFL seasons the average combined score has been about 43-46 points per game, and roughly two-thirds to three-quarters of games have totaled 32 or more. In this matchup's six 2026 team-games, 5 of 6 totaled 32 or more.

Datafolha poll of 2,002 people, fieldwork from Sept 22 (registration BR-00304/2026, margin of error ±2 pts): Lula 40%, Flávio Bolsonaro 36% of total voting intentions. In valid votes (excluding blank and null): Lula 43%, Flávio 39%.

Quaest poll released Sept 28 (fieldwork Sept 24–27): Lula 45.9% and Flávio Bolsonaro 40.0% of valid votes in the first round. Augusto Cury (Avante) and Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) each had 4.7%. In total votes it was Lula 39%, Flávio 34% (±2 pts).
AtlasIntel/Bloomberg poll (fieldwork Sept 23–28): Lula 46.2% and Flávio Bolsonaro 43.1% of valid votes in the first round. In total votes it was Lula 45.3%, Flávio 42.2%.
DataTempo national poll (BR-04527/2026), September: Lula 40.2%, Flávio 30.9% of total votes. In valid votes (excluding blank, null, undecided and no answer): Lula 45.8%, Flávio 35.2%.

raw_facts.source: Wikipedia (Opinion polling for the 2026 Brazilian presidential election)
raw_facts.fact: Other late-September first-round polls, as listed (shares of total votes): Palver (Sept 24–27) Lula 44%, Flávio 44%; Futura (Sept 25–29) Lula 39.4%, Flávio 42.2%.

raw_facts.source: Wikipedia (Opinion polling for the 2026 Brazilian presidential election)
raw_facts.fact: Poll aggregators, Sept 24–25, Flávio Bolsonaro's share of total votes including undecided: UOL 34.9% (blank/null/undecided 4.2%), BBC/PollingData 37.5% (8.0% blank/null/undecided), Poll+Trend 40.43%, Plano Político 40.7% (Lula 43.1%).

Datafolha trend: its Sept 8–10 poll had Lula 43% and Flávio 38% of valid votes (total votes: Lula 39%, Flávio 35%, up from 33% on Sept 3). Flávio's valid share then rose to 39% in the Sept 22–24 poll.
2022: the final Datafolha poll (Sept 29) had Lula 43% and Jair Bolsonaro 39% of valid votes. The actual result was Lula 48.4% and Bolsonaro 43.2%, so Bolsonaro was underestimated by about 4 pts.

2018: the final Datafolha poll (Oct 2) had Bolsonaro at 32% of total votes; he got 46.03% of valid votes. 2014: the final poll had Aécio Neves at 26% of valid votes; he got 33.55%. 2010: the final poll had Dilma at 52% of valid votes; she got 46.91%. This is a small sample (about 5 elections, unverified as a base rate). In 2014, 2018 and 2022 the main right-of-centre candidate outperformed the final poll.
Polls still due before the first round on Sunday, Oct 4: Datafolha on Thursday Oct 1 and Saturday Oct 3, and Quaest's national round on Saturday Oct 3.

The question resolves on Flávio Bolsonaro's share of valid votes (blank and null votes excluded) in the TSE official first-round count on Oct 4, 2026. A value exactly at a bracket boundary resolves to the higher bracket, so exactly 39.0% counts as 39% or more.

CPI-U for all items rose 3.4% in the 12 months to August 2026 before seasonal adjustment, the same 12-month rate as in July. The August 2026 index (not seasonally adjusted) was 334.980, which is 1982-84=100.

In August 2026, CPI-U rose 0.4% seasonally adjusted (July: +0.1%) and 0.3% not seasonally adjusted. Gasoline rose 3.9% seasonally adjusted in the month and made up over a third of the all-items increase. Over 12 months, energy was up 16.3% and gasoline 27.4%.
Core CPI (all items less food and energy) rose 2.4% in the 12 months to August 2026, down from 2.5% in the 12 months to July.

raw_facts.source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (September 2025 CPI release)
raw_facts.fact: The September 2025 CPI-U index (not seasonally adjusted) was 324.800, and the 12-month rate was 3.0%. The August 2025 index was 323.976, so the index rose about 0.25% from August to September 2025 before seasonal adjustment. Desk arithmetic: for BLS to print 3.7% or higher, the September 2026 index must be about 336.66 or higher, roughly a 0.50% rise from August 2026 before seasonal adjustment. A print of exactly 3.6% (which resolves No) covers an index of about 336.49 to 336.65.
AAA's national average for regular gasoline was $4.14 on Sep 3, $4.27 on Sep 10, $4.43 on Sep 17 and $4.48 on Sep 24, 2026. AAA said the Sep 24 price was the highest ever for that time of year.

AAA said September 2026's average to date was $4.30 per gallon, a record for the month (the previous September record was $3.83 in 2023). It linked the rise to volatility in the Strait of Hormuz and crude oil near $100 per barrel.

AAA's August 2026 weekly national averages were $4.06 (Aug 6), $4.07 (Aug 13), $4.10 (Aug 20) and $4.09 (Aug 27). That means the August average was about $4.08, and the September average to date of $4.30 is roughly 5% higher.
As of mid-September 2026, AAA said the national average gas price was more than $1 higher than a year earlier. Crude oil averaged about $100 per barrel, up from about $90 in early September.
BLS has scheduled the September 2026 CPI release for Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. ET, which is the day the question closes.

A continuing resolution signed on Sep 2, 2026 funds federal agencies through December 11, 2026. That averts an October 1 shutdown, so no shutdown-related delay to the October 14 CPI release is expected.
The question resolves on the 12-month all-items CPI-U change, unadjusted, as BLS reports it to one decimal place. Only a value of 3.7% or higher counts as 'above 3.6%'.

In its chart preview, HITS says Taylor Swift's 'The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore' should take #1 on the next HITS Top 50, with about 150k in activity, 21k of it pure sales. That projection lands exactly on the 150k threshold.

As of today, the HITS Top 50 page shows the chart dated 2026-09-24, which is the week before The Encore. The final chart for the debut week (covering the Sept 25 release) did not appear to be posted yet, and the page returned no entry data.
HITS posted a follow-up chart preview on 2026-09-29 titled 'Chart Preview: The Show Goes On'. Its text could not be retrieved, so it is unknown whether it changed the 150k projection.

raw_facts.source: Gaga Daily forum (relaying Hits Daily Double)
raw_facts.fact: A forum post relaying the HITS preview repeats the figure of 150k activity with 21k pure sales for Showgirl/The Encore. It also lists Alice in Chains 'Unplugged' reissue at #16 with 25k (24k pure) and Ms. Rachel at #20 with 22.1k.

raw_facts.source: InMusicBlog / Talk of the Charts (citing Nora Music)
raw_facts.fact: A non-HITS early estimate from Nora Music put the album at about 178K US album-equivalent units for the week after The Encore came out. This tracker is not the resolution source and its method differs from HITS.

raw_facts.source: Talk of the Charts on X
raw_facts.fact: The Encore is a deluxe edition of 'The Life of a Showgirl' that came out 2026-09-25. Its units count toward the parent album's chart entry, described as a 13th week at #1, not as a separate new album. The resolving HITS 'Activity' figure is therefore likely to be the combined album total for that week.
In the week before The Encore, 'The Life of a Showgirl' rose to #21 on the Billboard 200 with about 24K, up 20%. That gives a baseline of roughly 24K units before the deluxe release.
The four new Encore tracks drew 40.5 million global Spotify streams on their first day, a Spotify record for a deluxe album. 'Patient Zero' led with 13.709 million.

This outlet also reported an initial projection of about 150,000 units for Showgirl after The Encore. The same article says Miley Cyrus's 'Bass Persuades' beat its projections of 40–46K and opened with 61K, though that seems to refer to an earlier chart week.

Unverified single example: one recent album's early projections (40–46K) came in below its final total (61K), which shows early-week projections can be off by 15K or more. No systematic count of how HITS projections compare with final HITS Activity figures was found.

The final HITS Top 50 for the debut week (tracking week starting 2026-09-25) is due on the usual weekly schedule, likely around 2026-10-01 to 10-02, before the question closes on 2026-10-03 03:59 UTC.
The question resolves Yes only if Spain is winning after 90 minutes plus stoppage time. Extra time and penalties do not count, so a draw resolves No for 'Spain wins'.

At stumps on day 2 of the 2nd unofficial Test in Puducherry, India A were 122 for 5 in their first innings, 236 runs behind Australia A's 358. Shaik Rasheed was not out on 36 and Tanush Kotian not out on 6. Todd Murphy had figures of 2 for 26 from 17 overs. No day-3 score (Oct 1) could be found in any source.

Australia A resumed day 2 on 282 for 7 and were bowled out for 358. Sam Harper top-scored with 128; he resumed on 101 and was caught behind off Tanush Kotian. Murphy dismissed B Sai Sudharsan and Yash Rathod.

On day 1, Nachiket Bhute and Shams Mulani had Australia A at 104 for 5 before Harper's sixth first-class century led a recovery to 282 for 7. Liam Scott made 34 off 82 balls and Murphy 33 off 91 in support.

This is a four-day match (unofficial Test) scheduled for September 29 to October 2, 2026. Today, October 1, is day 3, so two days of play remain counting today. If there is no result by the end of day 4, the match is a draw, which resolves the Draw/Tie market Yes and the Australia A market No.

Australia A wins resolves Yes only if Australia A win outright. A draw or tie resolves the Draw/Tie market Yes. If the match is abandoned after the toss, the official result recorded by the governing body is used.

India A won the 1st unofficial Test at the same ground (CAP Siechem Ground, Pondicherry, Sept 22–25, 2026) by 162 runs: India A 334 and 199, Australia A 171 and 200. India A lead the two-match series 1-0.

In the first match at the same venue, the Puducherry pitch 'had started to misbehave on day three'. Murphy took 4 wickets in India A's second innings and 3 in the first, and that match ended with a result inside four days.
Australia A made three changes for the second match, with Jhye Richardson leading the attack and Sam Harper coming into the side.
The 2025 1st unofficial Test in Lucknow was a high-scoring draw: Australia A 532/6d and 56/0, India A 531/7d. The 2025 2nd unofficial Test was won by India A by 5 wickets. Small sample (2 matches).
Across the three most recent India A vs Australia A four-day matches in India (two in 2025, one in 2026), the results were 1 draw and 2 India A wins. This is a very small, unverified sample.

The market resolves Yes only if Green Bay wins the game originally scheduled for Oct 4, 2026 by more than 3.5 points, which means by 4 or more. A Packers win by 1–3 points, a tie or a Packers loss all resolve No.

Undrafted rookie QB Jalon Daniels will make his first NFL start for Tampa Bay against Green Bay. Baker Mayfield dislocated his right thumb and is expected to miss about three weeks. Daniels is the first undrafted rookie QB to start for the Buccaneers in the franchise's history.
Tampa Bay lost 23-16 to Minnesota in Week 3 and fell to 0-3. Mayfield went 17 of 34 for 217 yards with 1 TD and 1 INT before he dislocated his thumb late in the game.
Tampa Bay lost its first two games by one score each: 33-27 at Cincinnati in Week 1 and 23-19 at home to Cleveland in Week 2. All three Bucs losses were decided by 7 points or fewer.

Green Bay lost 35-14 at home to Atlanta on Thursday night in Week 3, which ended the Packers' streak of 13 straight home-opener wins. Atlanta scored 27 straight points to turn an early 0-7 deficit into a 27-7 lead in the fourth quarter. The Packers are 1-2.

The Packers' results so far: in Week 1 they lost to Minnesota by 17 points. In Week 2 they beat the New York Jets in overtime after coming back from a 10-point deficit in the fourth quarter. In Week 3 they lost 35-14 to Atlanta.

Packers DE Micah Parsons (torn ACL and meniscus from last December) is still on the PUP list. His 21-day practice window had not opened, so he must miss at least one more game. RB Josh Jacobs is on the commissioner's exempt list after an offseason arrest and a groin injury in camp.

A senior Israeli official said the Omani co-pilot 'most likely acted alone' and that investigators 'have so far ruled out an apparent connection to the Islamic Republic.' Israeli officials increasingly see the motive as 'nationalist and religious.'
Two Israeli security officials told AP that Israel had not found any Iranian involvement. A senior U.S. official said there were 'no indications that Iran directed or was involved' in the attack.

Asked about Iranian involvement, PM Netanyahu said it was 'too early to say.' He said 'personal information' from questioning showed the co-pilot 'underwent Islamist radical indoctrination,' and he also said the incident 'looked like a suicide attempt.'

Netanyahu said: 'We'll get to the root of this attacker, whether he had accomplices, whether Iran was behind it. I think we'll find out very soon.' As of that report, Israel had made no official suggestion that Iran was behind the attack.
Defense Minister Israel Katz, a cabinet minister whose statements count under the rules, called the incident 'an attempted jihadist terror attack.' He did not attribute it to Iran or any named group.

President Trump said the co-pilot may be linked to Iran 'based on what I'm hearing' and gave no details. Asked whether Iran's IRGC could have placed him there, he said 'Could've been, yeah.' Trump is not an Israeli official, so his statements do not count for resolution.
An Omani official told CBS the attacker was born in Oman and holds Omani citizenship. The Omani government had not publicly confirmed this, and the co-pilot had not been publicly named.

The co-pilot was moved to UAE custody on Thursday (Oct 1). Saudi Arabia turned down Israel's request for observer status in its investigation. Israel is relying on its ties with Abu Dhabi for access, and Netanyahu said the UAE was giving 'full cooperation.'
The UAE was reportedly frustrated that Israel called the incident terrorism before the investigation was finished. Israel is looking into the suspect's social media activity.

Saudi Arabia, Israel and the UAE have each announced investigations. Saudi Arabia's initial findings describe 'an assault on the pilot by his co-pilot,' and the Saudi Interior Ministry said both pilots were moved to Abu Dhabi after medical clearance.

Israel said the co-pilot tried to crash the flydubai plane during the cockpit fight. Flight FZ1073 had 174 people on board, mostly Israelis, and landed in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, after passengers and two off-duty pilots subdued the attacker.

A report found that dozens of Omani pilots had flown to Tel Aviv before the attack despite a ban, and Netanyahu acknowledged a 'loophole' in vetting pilots on Israel-bound flights. Coverage is now partly about vetting failures, not Iranian direction.

On Oct 1-2, Trump said Iran is "ready to fold up" and suggested the war would end "right after the election," though he added it could end sooner. He said "We blow them up or make a deal." The US is keeping its maritime blockade of Iranian ports in place.

On Oct 1, Trump said Iran's latest peace proposal, which included terms for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, was not enough. He said the US would decide "very soon" whether to strike Iran or negotiate. Iran received Washington's response to its seven-day Hormuz proposal through Qatari mediators.

Trump rejected Iran's seven-day ceasefire plan, saying it "would not be acceptable." Under the plan, the US would lift its blockade of Iranian ports and unfreeze Iranian funds, and Iran would reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days. FM Araghchi said "only a negotiated solution" can end the deadlock.

US and Iranian officials held talks on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York, mediated by Qatar, Pakistan and Egypt. Iran proposed a regionwide ceasefire of up to 60 days, a phased reopening of Hormuz and an end to the US blockade.
Iran's stated conditions for talks with the US are an end to the war on all fronts, the unfreezing of Iranian funds, and an end to the naval blockade.

Iran loaded no crude onto tankers in September 2026, down from about 250,000 bpd in August, the first time this has happened since the war began in February. Kpler and Vortexa also recorded zero loadings.

Treasury imposed new sanctions on Iran's rail and automotive sectors under "Operation Economic Outcast." Three tankers were struck by unknown projectiles in the Strait of Hormuz on Sept 30, and Trump told TIME he doesn't believe "you could ever have peace" with Iran.

The reinstated blockade took effect on July 14, 2026 at 20:00 GMT. By Aug 11, CENTCOM had redirected 55 vessels, and by Sept 12 more than 100 vessels had been redirected since reinstatement. Several tankers (Belma, Lavine, Vela Nova) were disabled.

The previous precedent: the first blockade began April 13, 2026, and was lifted on June 18, 2026, when CENTCOM announced its removal about 66 days later. This came after a deal announced June 14 and signed at Versailles, which started a 60-day clock for a final deal. The blockade was reinstated about 4 weeks later. This is a single case and should not be read as a statistical base rate.

In April 2026, Trump rejected an earlier Iranian proposal and told Axios he would "maintain the blockade in order to pressure Tehran toward a nuclear agreement." The blockade was lifted only after a signed agreement about 7 weeks later.
The June ceasefire/MOU collapsed in less than three weeks, with Iran accusing the US of violating its terms. Trump announced the blockade's reinstatement on July 13.

The US midterm elections are on Nov 3, 2026, after the question closes on Oct 31. Trump has tied resuming strikes or ending the war to the period after the election. Talks through Qatari and Pakistani mediators are ongoing.

In a late-September article, AGBI reported that oil was flowing again through the East-West pipeline at about 3.5 million bpd, roughly half its pre-attack volume, citing Bloomberg and the Wall Street Journal. It said neither the Saudi Energy Ministry nor Saudi Aramco had made any public statement on the pipeline since the attack. The publication date is approximate; the article page itself could not be opened.

On Sept 22, Reuters reported that Saudi Arabia had restarted the East-West pipeline and could resume exports from Yanbu, citing three unnamed sources briefed on the matter. This was not an official Saudi government announcement.

Reports of the restart said the pipeline was pumping at a low rate and Aramco was working to bring flows back to about 4 million bpd, which could take weeks. Aramco had not publicly confirmed the throughput.

As of its Sept 29 update, the Wikipedia article says the pipeline restarted at very low volume on Sept 22 and will likely need at least 6–8 weeks to regain full capacity. The only Ministry of Energy statement it cites is the Sept 11 shutdown confirmation.

On Sept 11, the Ministry of Energy, via SPA, announced that the East-West pipeline had been shut down 'as a precaution' after multiple drone attacks on pumping stations in the Riyadh and Medina regions on Sept 10–11. The drones were launched from Iraq.
US Energy Secretary Chris Wright told CNBC that the pipeline closure would be a brief interruption lasting days. He is a third party, not the Saudi government.
The pipeline has 7 million bpd of capacity and had been carrying 4–5 million bpd to Red Sea terminals to get around Hormuz disruption. After the shutdown, Brent rose to about $108.

Precedent from earlier this year: after attacks on Saudi energy facilities, the Ministry of Energy officially announced on April 12, 2026 that the East-West pipeline was back to full pumping capacity of about 7 million bpd. That shows the ministry has publicly announced pipeline restorations before. This is a single case.

In the April episode, SPA had reported 'last week' that attacks cut pipeline output by 700,000 bpd, and the ministry announced full restoration on April 12. That puts the gap between the official damage report and the official restoration announcement at roughly one week or a little more. The exact attack dates are not given.

On Sept 30, CNBC reported that crude exports through the Strait of Hormuz were back at pre-war levels, while fuel shipments were still limited. That reduces how much Saudi Arabia depends on the Red Sea route for now.

Only an official Saudi government announcement that the pipeline is operating now, even at reduced capacity, counts, and it must come before Oct 31, 11:59 PM ET. Media reports citing unnamed sources, such as the Sept 22 Reuters story, do not count, and neither do statements that operation is planned or expected.

At the All-In Summit, Musk was asked why Tesla and SpaceX are still separate. He answered: 'Great question... who can imagine what action one might take when there's so much close collaboration in so many areas.' He did not confirm any deal or give a timeline.

A combination would face geopolitical and regulatory hurdles: SpaceX is a major US defense and national-security contractor, while Tesla owns factories in China outright. Media identify this as the main obstacle to a deal.

Seasonally adjusted CPI-U rose 0.4% in August 2026, after 0.1% in July. Over 12 months, before seasonal adjustment, it was up 3.4%. In August, energy rose 2.1%, food 0.1%, core 0.3% and shelter 0.3%.

August 2026 gasoline rose 3.9% seasonally adjusted but only 2.5% before adjustment, so seasonal adjustment added to the gasoline gain. Gasoline accounted for over one third of the 0.4% all-items increase.

AAA's national average for regular gasoline was $4.14 on Sept 3, $4.27 on Sept 10, $4.43 on Sept 17 and $4.48 on Sept 24, then $4.396 on Oct 2. AAA said $4.48 was the highest ever for that time of year, driven by volatility in the Strait of Hormuz and high crude prices.

AAA's September 2026 monthly average gas price was reported as $4.33, a record for September and 50 cents above the previous September record. The figure came from a search summary; the AAA page that was read did not state a monthly average.
AAA's August 2026 monthly average gas price was $4.06/gal, a record for August. On this basis, September's $4.33 average would be about 6.7% higher than August before seasonal adjustment.
The question resolves on the single-decimal seasonally adjusted all-items CPI-U monthly change. 'More than 0.6%' requires a published 0.7% or higher; a published 0.6% would resolve No.
The September 2026 CPI report is scheduled for Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. ET.
Congress passed a continuing resolution funding the government through December 11, 2026 (House vote 370-48; Senate 90-6), so no shutdown began on October 1, 2026.
Monthly seasonally adjusted headline CPI in 2026: March +0.9%, April +0.6%, May +0.5%, June -0.4%, July +0.1%, August +0.4%. Only 1 of these 6 months (March) was above 0.6%.
In March 2026, CPI rose 0.9% seasonally adjusted. Gasoline rose 21.2%, its largest monthly rise since 1967, and energy rose 10.9%. Nearly three-quarters of the headline increase came from gasoline.
Energy-to-headline comparisons in 2026: April energy +3.8% came with a 0.6% headline (core +0.4%), and May energy +3.9% came with a 0.5% headline (core +0.2%).

The Braves won 5 of 6 regular-season games against the Dodgers, including five straight and a three-game sweep at Truist Park on Aug 25–27. Six games is a small sample.
A Yahoo Sports preview is headlined 'Dodgers host Braves in NLDS with Ohtani questions looming.' The specific issue (health or role) could not be confirmed.

Besides Skubal, the Dodgers' playoff rotation includes Yoshinobu Yamamoto (2025 World Series MVP), Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow. The Dodgers are trying for a third straight title.

raw_facts.source: CNBC / Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta (FOMC statement)
raw_facts.fact: At its Sept 16, 2026 meeting the FOMC voted 12-0 to raise the federal funds target range by 25 bp, from 3.50%-3.75% to 3.75%-4.00%. The upper bound is now exactly 4.00%, so the Oct 28 decision would have to be another hike for the upper bound to be above 4.00%.

The FOMC states the target range as a lower and upper bound, and moves usually come in 25 bp steps. Holding at 3.75%-4.00% leaves the upper bound at 4.00%, which is not above 4.00%. A 25 bp hike would raise it to 4.25%.

The September dot plot's median has the fed funds rate ending 2026 at 4.1%, which implies one more 25 bp hike this year. The median shows no change in 2027. Two FOMC meetings are left in 2026: Oct 27-28 and Dec 8-9.

August core PCE inflation was 3.0% year on year (+0.2% m/m), and July core was revised down to 3.0% from 3.3%. Core has held at 3% for three months. Headline PCE was 3.4% y/y in August, and Q2 GDP was revised up to 2.2%.

The next FOMC decision comes at the end of the Oct 27-28, 2026 meeting, with the statement usually released at 2:00 PM ET on Oct 28.

On 10 September 2026 the ECB raised all three key rates by 25 bps, taking the deposit facility rate to 2.50%, the MRO rate to 2.65% and the marginal lending rate to 2.90%. Lagarde called the unanimous decision 'a no-brainer'. The October decision will be measured against the 2.50% deposit rate.

The ECB said it follows 'a data-dependent and meeting-by-meeting approach' and is 'not pre-committing to a particular rate path'. Lagarde said the Council did not debate any future path and that future action 'will be determined at each and every meeting'.

The next ECB monetary policy meeting is 28–29 October 2026, with the decision announced on 29 October. There is no ECB staff projection round in October; the next projections come with the December meeting.

Flash euro-area HICP inflation rose to 3.8% in September from 3.2% in August, above the 3.6% consensus and the highest in three years. The rise was driven by fuel, natural gas and food. Core inflation edged up to 2.5% from 2.4%.

Capital Economics' Jack Allen-Reynolds said the September data don't change the firm's view that the ECB is most likely to wait until December for its next hike. He added that an October hike 'would not be a big surprise' if energy prices rose further in the coming weeks.

Lagarde said 'measured' hikes remain appropriate: 'We see higher inflation ahead but no signs yet that it is becoming embedded', and there is no evidence yet that energy prices are feeding into wages. She pushed back on the idea that rates will automatically track energy costs. Economists read this as spacing hikes several months apart, which points more toward December than 29 October.
ECB Governing Council member Alexander Demarco (Malta) backed an October hike, citing firm core inflation as grounds for further action.

Ahead of the October vote, ECB Governing Council member Olli Rehn said the AI-related debt glut is doing part of the ECB's tightening work. In the same vein, Lagarde said higher bond yields since the September meeting would dampen growth and inflation.
On the day of the September hike, Bloomberg reported that ECB officials expect more tightening and that an October move is 'in play'.

Bundesbank President Joachim Nagel said it is too early to speculate about the next meeting. He added that rates may eventually need to move into mildly restrictive territory, depending on how energy prices develop. (The publication date is approximate.)

In the current cycle the ECB has gone hike, hold, hike. It made its first hike since 2023 in June 2026 (deposit rate to 2.25%), held unanimously on 23 July 2026, then hiked again on 10 September. So far it has not raised rates at two meetings in a row.

According to the account of the July meeting, the pause was not meant as the end of tightening, and some members would not have opposed a hike. Members also cited elevated uncertainty and said the full inflationary effect of the energy shock had yet to appear.
The September 2026 staff projections put headline inflation at 3.0% for 2026, 2.5% for 2027 and 2.1% for 2028, and core at 2.5%, 2.6% and 2.3%. GDP growth is projected at 0.9%, 1.4% and 1.5%.

In the last poll Ipsos was allowed to publish (fieldwork Sept 24–25, 2026), voting intention for Lima mayor was: López Aliaga (Renovación Popular) 25%, Carlos Bruce (Somos Perú) 14%, Francis Allison (Avanza País) 13%, Daniel Urresti 8% and Samuel Daza 6%. In Ipsos's mock ballot it was López Aliaga 30%, Bruce 15.6% and Allison 15.1%.
Ipsos said Allison had rebounded from 9% in its August 2026 poll to 13% in late September.

CPI's mock ballot (Sept 20–26, valid votes) had López Aliaga 27.2%, Bruce 15.2%, Allison 10.4%, Urresti 7.5%, Daza 4.8%, with 12.3% blank or spoiled and 7.2% undecided. CPI's director said the order of candidates had stayed the same for several weeks.
CIT's late poll had López Aliaga 33.4%, Bruce 12.0% and Allison 11.8%. In an earlier CIT poll (June 14–16) that left López Aliaga out, Allison led with 15.8%.
The Lima mayoral race is decided in a single round with no runoff, so the candidate with the most votes wins. There are 26 candidates.

López Aliaga, who was Lima's mayor until 2025, is registered as first councillor (primer regidor) on Renovación Popular's list. The list's mayoral nominee resigned, which makes him first in line to become mayor. Critics call this a disguised re-election that gets around the constitutional ban on immediate re-election.
The JNE (National Jury of Elections) confirmed López Aliaga's candidacy and rejected an appeal to exclude him. It said no challenge had been filed within the three-day deadline.
Days before the vote, the JNE had still not said whether it would give López Aliaga the mayor's credential if his list wins. APRA candidate Mónica Yaya asked Congress to call the JNE in to clarify.
Carlos Bruce took his complaint about a possible disguised re-election of López Aliaga to the OAS (Organization of American States).

Allison has been mayor of Magdalena del Mar for several terms over about 20 years and was briefly Housing Minister under Alan García. He was once arrested in the US for carrying more than $50,000 in cash and pleaded guilty to smuggling and perjury charges.
Allison said that if elected he would audit López Aliaga's administration, saying there were 'very clear signs of corruption'.
Campaigning closed on Oct 2. The municipal election is on Sunday, October 4, 2026, and ONPE (the national elections office) will publish the official count afterwards.

In 2018, Jorge Muñoz polled only 3.5% in Datum's final poll 11 days before the vote, yet went from fifth to first in the last week and won about 32% to Urresti's 21%. Reggiardo, who had led the polls, finished third with about 10%. (A single example; how often late reversals happen in Lima is unverified.)

Aleksandar Vučić resigned as President of Serbia on Sept 27, 2026. He did so to lead his Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) in the Oct 25 early parliamentary election as its candidate for prime minister. The constitution barred him from a third presidential term.
SNS formally proposed Vučić as its prime minister if it wins the early election. He heads the list called 'Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia'.

Vučić dissolved parliament and called early parliamentary elections for Oct 25, 2026. The regular election had been due by December 2027. The question closes the same day, Oct 25, 2026, which is before any new government could be elected by the Assembly.

raw_facts.source: Wikipedia (Opinion polling for the next Serbian parliamentary election)
raw_facts.fact: Latest poll: NSPM (fieldwork Sept 30) has the Student List at 44.4% and SNS/United Serbia at 41.7%. In the previous NSPM poll (July 30) the Student List led 39.6% to 37.5%.

Faktor Plus (fieldwork Sept 16–20, n=986) has SNS/United Serbia at 48.6%, Student List 37.1%, SPS 4.9% and European Serbia 3.6%, with 16% undecided. Its Sept 4 poll had SNS at 47.2% and the Student List at 31.5%.

A CRTA poll published July 15, 2026 had the Student List at 44.9% and SNS at 35.7%. Wikipedia says this was the first regular national poll since July 2010 in which any option other than SNS came first. Different pollsters disagree on who leads: Faktor Plus puts SNS first, while NSPM and CRTA put the Student List first.

All 250 Assembly seats are filled by closed-list proportional representation in one nationwide constituency, using the d'Hondt method. The threshold is 3%, and it is waived for ethnic minority lists. A government needs 126 votes in the National Assembly. 16 lists are running.

The Student List ('Students Win') says it has no leader. Dr. Ilija Srđanović is first on the list, and its candidates include Dejan Bodiroga and former central bank governor Dejan Šoškić. It has not named a prime ministerial candidate, so if it wins, the next PM would be someone other than Vučić.
Ana Brnabić, the parliament speaker and a close Vučić ally, became acting president. She must hold a presidential election within 90 days of the resignation, so no later than Dec 27, 2026.

The current prime minister is Đuro Macut, an independent who took office after Miloš Vučević resigned in January 2025. Wikipedia gives the date as April 16, 2026, which is probably a typo for 2025. Macut is not running as a PM candidate, and there is no mention of a new government being formed before the election.

Unverified, from memory: after recent Serbian elections, new governments were elected roughly 1.5 to 7 months after the vote. Examples: 2014 vote Mar 16, government Apr 27; 2016 Apr 24 to Aug 11; 2020 Jun 21 to Oct 28; 2022 Apr 3 to Oct 26; 2023 Dec 17 to May 2, 2024. SNS won the most seats in every parliamentary election from 2012 to 2023, and Vučić was elected PM in 2014 and 2016.
Polling context: before July 2026, SNS had come first in every regular national poll since July 2010. 2026 is the first election cycle in which polls are split on who will finish first.

raw_facts.fact: Real Time Big Data (Sept 26–30, 2026) has Flávio Bolsonaro on 41% of valid votes in the first round and Lula on 46%. Among all respondents it was 39% for Flávio and 43% for Lula.

AtlasIntel (Sept 23–28, 2026) has Lula at 45.3% and Flávio Bolsonaro at 42.2% in the first round, with only 2.1% undecided or blank. A late-September AtlasIntel estimate of the first-round result had Flávio on 43.1% and Lula on 46.2%.

Quaest (Sept 24–27, 2026, 2,004 voters, ±2 pts) has Flávio Bolsonaro on 40% of valid votes and Lula on 45.9%. Among all respondents it was 34% for Flávio and 39% for Lula, with 5% undecided and 10% blank, null or not voting.

Other late polls, counting all respondents: Vox (Sept 29–Oct 1) has Flávio 41.2% and Lula 40.4%, with 10.2% undecided or blank. Veritá (Sept 20–25) has Flávio 44.3% and Lula 43.8%. Other candidates combined poll about 8–11%.

In the 2022 first round, Datafolha's final pre-election poll had Jair Bolsonaro on 36% of valid votes; he won 43.21%, so Datafolha underestimated him by 7.2 points. Several other major pollsters also underestimated him beyond their margins of error. This is a single election.

For 2022, Congresso em Foco names Paraná Pesquisas (40%) and AtlasIntel (41.1%) as the only polls that came close to Bolsonaro's actual 43.2% in the first round. Datafolha, Ipec and Quaest underestimated him. It is unverified whether those figures are valid-vote or all-respondent shares.
The first round is on October 4, 2026. The TSE publishes valid-vote percentages, which exclude blank and null votes, on election night as it counts the electronic ballots.

raw_facts.source: Sul21 / Band (Quaest, commissioned by Grupo RBS)
raw_facts.fact: Quaest surveyed 900 voters Sept 20–23 (±3 points). First round: Zucco 29%, Brizola 23%, Gabriel Souza 10%, Marcelo Maranata (PSDB) 3%. Runoffs: Zucco 40% vs Brizola 34%, which Quaest called a technical tie; Zucco 42% vs Souza 26%; Brizola 34% vs Souza 27%.
AtlasIntel surveyed 1,819 voters Sept 15–20 (±2 points). First round: Zucco 41.6%, Brizola 36.1%. Runoff: Zucco 49.7%, Brizola 39.3%, with 11% blank, null or no answer.
An earlier AtlasIntel poll, taken Aug 27–Sept 1, had Zucco at 44.3%, Brizola 37.5% and Gabriel Souza 10.4% in the first round. Its runoff had Zucco 48.5% vs Brizola 43.9%.

Pollsters disagreed on the runoff in late August and early September: Quaest (Aug 20–23) had Brizola 36% vs Zucco 33%; AtlasIntel had Zucco 48.5% vs Brizola 43.9%; Real Time Big Data (Sept 5–9) had them tied at 44%. Real Time's first round that week was Zucco 36%, Brizola 35%, Souza 22%.
Quaest's August poll had Brizola slightly ahead of Zucco in a runoff. Quaest's July poll had the two tied in the runoff, with many voters undecided.

The first round is on Oct 4, 2026. If no candidate gets a majority of valid votes, a runoff will be held Oct 25, 2026. The question closes at 2026-10-05T03:59Z, so if there is a runoff the winner will not be known before it closes.

The question resolves to the election winner based on a consensus of credible reporting, or on official TSE results if that is ambiguous. If the result is not known by June 30, 2027, it resolves to 'Other'.
