Talarico and Republican nominee Ken Paxton launched dueling ads in early October in what the Post calls a heated general-election race.
The general election between Talarico and Paxton is on 2026-11-03, the day the question closes, which leaves about four weeks for an endorsement. No scheduled joint Sanders–Talarico event was found.
The resolution page for The Social Reckoning shows no Tomatometer yet: 0 reviews and no critics consensus. It lists a wide theatrical release on October 9, 2026 (Columbia Pictures, R, 1h52m).

The review embargo reportedly lifts Wednesday, October 7, 2026, two days before the October 9 wide release. The market resolves on the score shown Monday, October 12 at 10:00 AM ET, so about 5 days of reviews will count.
The score must be strictly above the strike to resolve Yes. A score of exactly 70 makes 'Above 70' No, and exactly 60 makes 'Above 60' No.

Of 9 early critic reactions compiled, about 5 were positive: Joey Magidson (Awards Radar), Luke Hearfield, Edward Douglas ('still very good'), G. Allen Johnson ('All the President's Men-level') and Movies with Epicz. The other 4 were mixed: Tom Chatalbash ('good, just not great'), Matt Neglia (Next Best Picture, mixed-positive), Patrick T. ('uninspiring' direction) and DawsOn. None were outright negative.

After the London gala premiere on September 30, World of Reel described the reaction consensus as 'rather mid.' Criticisms included flat, TV-like visuals, an overbearing score and a cheap-looking January 6 sequence. Box-office tracking was $4M–6M for the opening weekend.
World of Reel's first reaction called the film a timely indictment of Facebook but asked 'where's the cinema?', faulting the filmmaking more than the script.
25YL published a review calling the film a 'sharp op-ed missing its Fincher.' It praised Sorkin's script and the lead performances but criticized the direction, which reads as mixed to positive.
Critic Stephen Silver's piece is titled 'Is The Social Reckoning really as bad as it looks?', which points to negative pre-release buzz about the film's look and trailer.

Sorkin's three earlier films as director scored 82% (Molly's Game, 2017), 89% (The Trial of the Chicago 7, 2020) and 68% (Being the Ricardos, 2021) on the Tomatometer. All 3 are above 60 and 2 of 3 are above 70. These are final lifetime scores, not scores from opening weekend.
Commentary noted that a Wednesday embargo for a Friday release usually means the studio is in no hurry to start the conversation about the film.

As of October 3, 2026, the US naval blockade of Iran was still in force, and Trump was sending another aircraft carrier and 10,000 sailors and Marines to the region. Diplomacy was reported as deadlocked.

Preliminary tanker-tracking estimates showed Iran loaded no crude onto tankers in September 2026, down from about 250,000 barrels per day in August. It was the first such month since the war began in February.

Trump rejected Iran's 7-day proposal, under which Iran would reopen the Strait of Hormuz and restart nuclear talks within a week if the US lifted its naval blockade, removed oil sanctions and reinstated a regional ceasefire. Trump said Iran had 'overplayed their hand' but said he expected talks to resume that week.

On October 4, Iranian Deputy FM Gharibabadi said Iran was still reviewing a US counterproposal, sent through intermediaries. Iran's foreign ministry spokesman said it was 'in line with their previous proposals concerning nuclear issues.' FM Araghchi said there is 'no military solution.'

The two sides disagree on what comes first. Iran insists the Hormuz and US blockade issues be settled first, while Washington insists on nuclear concessions. Qatar and other regional mediators are trying to revive the talks.

Trump said he was 'open to a deal, but not to the one the Iranians offered.' He reportedly told officials he expects to resume bombing Iran after the November 3 US midterm elections. The US also launched an expanded sanctions regime, 'Operation Economic Outcast,' in August 2026.

An IRGC advisor claimed that no US naval vessels are now in the Persian Gulf, the Strait of Hormuz or the Gulf of Oman, and that US warships have pulled back 1,000 km. This is an Iranian claim; no official US announcement about the blockade accompanied it.

Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf said Hormuz stays closed until the US meets seven conditions based on the June MOU, including ending the naval blockade. Araghchi said the strait could reopen within seven days if those conditions are met.

Precedent: the first blockade ran from April 13 to June 18, 2026 (about 66 days). On June 14 Trump said he had 'authorized lifting the US naval blockade' once an accord was reached. The MOU was signed at Versailles on June 17, and CENTCOM announced the blockade's removal on June 18. That is one prior instance, so this is an unverified base rate.
The second blockade phase began July 14–15, 2026, after Trump's July 13 announcement, and was about 83 days old as of October 5. More than 100 vessels had been redirected by September 12.

No signed agreement or scheduled formal US-Iran negotiating session was reported before October 31. The next known date is the US midterm election on November 3, after which Trump reportedly expects renewed bombing.

Only an official, unambiguous US government announcement of a general end or suspension of the blockade counts. Iranian claims, leaks, partial exemptions for specific vessels, and naval repositioning without an announcement do not qualify.
Tampa Bay beat the Yankees 1-0 in ALDS Game 1 on Oct 3, 2026 (attendance 40,542, game time 2:30). The Rays lead the best-of-five series 1-0, so they need two more wins and the Yankees need three.

In Game 1, Drew Rasmussen struck out 10 over eight innings and took a no-hitter into the eighth. Jonathan Aranda's third-inning solo homer off Gerrit Cole was the only run, and Bryan Baker pitched a 1-2-3 ninth.
CBS Sports' Game 1 recap headline says a baserunning decision by Yankees catcher Austin Wells doomed New York in the 1-0 loss.

Remaining schedule: Game 2 Mon Oct 5 at Tampa Bay, 8 PM ET; Game 3 Wed Oct 7 at Yankee Stadium; Game 4 (if needed) Thu Oct 8 at Yankee Stadium; Game 5 (if needed) Sat Oct 10 at Tampa Bay. Tampa Bay's home games are at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg.
Game 2 starters: Yankees RHP Cam Schlittler (14-6, 1.95 ERA, 0.92 WHIP, 239 K) against Rays RHP Freddy Peralta (10-11, 4.42 ERA, 1.32 WHIP, 156 K). As of research time, Game 2 had not been played.

MLB.com calls Schlittler the likely AL Cy Young winner and says he had a 1.16 road ERA. Peralta went 5-0 with a 0.79 ERA over his final six starts. Rasmussen went 16-5 with the AL's best WHIP (0.91) and has a career 5-2 record and 1.81 ERA in 11 appearances against New York.

Game 3 starters were not confirmed. Carlos Rodón is possible for New York, and Peralta or Nick Martinez for Tampa Bay; Martinez has a 2.38 road ERA versus 3.90 at home. Griffin Jax (no runs allowed... one run in his last 18 innings over four outings) was also a starting option for the Rays.

Regular season: Tampa Bay went 98-64 and won the AL East, earning a first-round bye. New York went 93-68 and finished 2nd in the AL East. The source says the teams played 15 times with Tampa Bay leading 8-6, which doesn't add up, so the exact head-to-head is unconfirmed.
Aaron Judge is not on the Yankees' ALDS roster. He has a moderate right-calf (soleus) strain from Sept 16 and also missed the Wild Card Series. He could be added for a potential ALCS.

Other injuries. Rays: Gavin Lux (60-day IL, shoulder), Shane McClanahan (15-day IL, forearm), Griffin Jax (day-to-day, back). Yankees: Clarke Schmidt (15-day IL, biceps), Fernando Cruz (60-day IL, elbow).
The Yankees reached the ALDS by sweeping the Boston Red Sox in the AL Wild Card Series, winning Game 2 by 9-2.

Since best-of-five Division Series began in 1995, the Game 1 winner has won the series about 73% of the time. One source cites 116 of 160 best-of-five series. This count runs only to about 2017 and is not verified through the current format.
The series is best-of-five, and the first team to 3 wins takes it. One of the two questions resolves Yes and the other No, depending on which team wins the series.

Milwaukee won NLDS Game 2 4-3 on Oct. 4 and leads the best-of-five series 2-0, so it needs one more win to clinch. Jackson Chourio hit a walk-off two-run single against Mason Miller with the bases loaded and two out in the 9th. The win went to Trevor Megill and the loss to Miller, who gave up 2 earned runs in 1.2 IP.
Milwaukee won NLDS Game 1 3-2 at home on Oct. 3, with home runs from Chourio and Contreras. Attendance was 42,843.

The series is best-of-five, and San Diego must win three straight games to advance. Games 1 and 2 were in Milwaukee, and the series moves to Petco Park in San Diego for Game 3. Unnamed people familiar with the matter told Bloomberg that the East-West pipeline is still running normally after reports of a new weekend strike on a pumping station near Khurais. Saudi Aramco and the Energy Ministry did not immediately answer Bloomberg's requests for comment. The 'operating normally' claim comes from those sources, not from the government.

Reports say that neither the Saudi Energy Ministry nor Aramco has said anything publicly about the pipeline since it was attacked in September. Every report of a restart or higher flows so far comes from anonymous sources or market-intelligence firms.

Bloomberg reported that Saudi Arabia raised flows on the 7 million b/d East-West pipeline to more than 80% of capacity, close to 6 million b/d, with about 4.5 million b/d available for export. These figures came from tanker-tracking and market data such as Kepler, not from a government statement.

Anonymous Reuters sources said the pipeline restarted on September 22 at a low rate, with Aramco working to bring flows back to about 4 million b/d. The article cites no statement from the government or the Ministry of Energy.

The Ministry of Energy said in an official SPA statement that the East-West pipeline had been shut down as a precaution after several drone attacks on September 10 in the Riyadh and Medina regions. The ministry said teams were taking steps to secure the pipeline and assess its safety.
The Saudi Foreign Ministry condemned the attack, carried out by several drones from Iraq, saying it caused injuries and 'some damage that is currently being addressed.'

Precedent from earlier in 2026: after attacks in April cut flows on the East-West pipeline, the Ministry of Energy announced through SPA on April 12 that full pumping capacity of about 7 million b/d had been restored. This shows the ministry has publicly confirmed restorations before. This is a single case.

US Energy Secretary Chris Wright told CNBC the closure would be a short interruption lasting days. He is a US official, not part of the Saudi government, so his statement does not count toward resolution.

Sources gave different repair estimates: one said five to six weeks, another said sooner. After the September 22 restart, Reuters sources said getting back to full capacity would likely take at least six to eight weeks.

The question resolves Yes only if official Saudi government information says the pipeline is currently operating, at any capacity, by October 31, 11:59 PM ET. Anonymous-source reports like the Reuters and Bloomberg pieces do not count, and neither do statements about future or planned resumption. Based on what was found, no qualifying government statement has been reported as of October 5.

About 26 days remain before the deadline (October 31, 11:59 PM ET; the question closes November 1, 03:59 UTC). No scheduled ministry briefing on the pipeline was found. Attacks are continuing, including the reported strike near Khurais on the weekend of October 3–4.

Seasonally adjusted monthly all-items CPI changes in 2026: Feb +0.3%, Mar +0.9%, Apr +0.6%, May +0.5%, Jun -0.4%, Jul +0.1%, Aug +0.4%. That is 2 of 7 months above 0.5%, 3 of 7 above 0.4%, and 1 of 7 above 0.6%.

The August 2026 national average gas price was $4.19 a gallon, using EIA data. This is a different provider from AAA, so comparing it with AAA's $4.33 September average (roughly +3%) is only approximate.

The headline figure is the seasonally adjusted one-month percent change in CPI-U, rounded to one decimal. For the seasonal factors introduced in January 2026, BLS used intervention-analysis seasonal adjustment on 57 series, including motor fuels.

Precedent: in the Oct 1 to Nov 12, 2025 shutdown (43 days), BLS pushed the September 2025 CPI back from Oct 15 to Oct 24 so Social Security could meet its COLA deadlines, and it cancelled the October 2025 CPI. My searches found no reporting of a 2026 shutdown affecting BLS (unverified).

At its September 16, 2026 meeting the FOMC voted 12-0 to raise the federal funds target range by 25 bps to 3.75%-4.00%. That makes 4.00% the upper bound going into the October meeting. It was the first hike since July 2023 and the first under Chair Kevin Warsh.

The September dot plot had a median of 4.1% for end-2026, which means one more 25 bp hike this year. 16 of 18 participants projected at least one more hike in 2026 and four projected two. The median showed no change in 2027 and cuts in 2028-2029.

The September statement cited persistent inflation, with core PCE above 3% in every month of 2026, and 'geopolitical developments'. Three members had already favored a hike at the July meeting. Only two FOMC meetings remain in 2026: October 27-28 and December.
September nonfarm payrolls rose by only 29,000, against a consensus of about 84,000. Unemployment rose to 4.2%, and July and August payrolls were revised down by a combined 60,000.

Before the jobs report, Fed Vice Chair Philip Jefferson said labor market conditions 'have stabilized'. NY Fed President John Williams said there was 'no need for urgency' in deciding whether to follow September's hike with another.

Before the jobs data, Williams called another hike before year-end 'reasonable'. Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack warned that inflation expectations could become entrenched after five years above target. Governor Lisa Cook said AI appears to be adding inflationary pressure and that the labor market 'appears to be well positioned to handle an increase in rates'.

At his September press conference Warsh said 'Inflation is too high and has been for too long.' He said the hike was made because the committee was not confident that underlying inflation was moving toward 2% fast enough. Warsh did not submit SEP projections because he views them as forward guidance.
At Jackson Hole in late August, Warsh said 'We have work to do' and suggested a rate hike in the coming months because of high inflation.

After the September jobs report, coverage shifted toward the Fed skipping October and possibly hiking in December. J.P. Morgan's stated base case is one more hike at the December meeting, and it notes that one argument for skipping October is giving the September hike time to work.
The September 2026 CPI is due Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. ET. It is the main inflation release still to come before the October 27-28 FOMC meeting.
The FOMC meets October 27-28, 2026, and the statement is released on October 28. If no statement is released by the end of the meeting, the market resolves 'No change'.

Resolution uses the change in the upper bound of the target range from its pre-meeting level of 4.00%. An upper bound of 4.25% resolves '25 bp hike' and 4.00% resolves 'No change'. Changes that are not multiples of 25 bp are rounded up to the nearest 25.

After Macklem's speech, TD Economics still called for the Bank of Canada to stay on hold for the rest of 2026.

Capital Economics calls for two quarter-point hikes starting next year (2027), which would take the policy rate to 2.75%, and cites U.S. trade friction and slower population growth. Senior Deputy Governor Rogers said the policy rate is too blunt a tool for housing affordability.

August CPI rose 3.0% year over year, the same as July. The Bank's preferred core measures averaged 2.0% (trim 1.9%, median 2.0%), and CPI excluding gasoline rose 2.4% after 2.2% in July. Gasoline inflation eased to 22.8% from 25.7%, and rent rose to 2.8% from 2.5%.
Analysts said the August core measures still showed limited evidence that high energy prices were spreading into broader inflation.
Q3 GDP growth is estimated at 1.4–2% annualized, Q2 GDP was up 1.2% year over year, and business investment rose for the first time since Q4 2024.
Statistics Canada is due to release the September Labour Force Survey on October 9, 2026.

The Bank of Canada is due to publish its Business Outlook Survey and Canadian Survey of Consumer Expectations on October 19, 2026 at 11:30 ET. September CPI is reported to be due around October 19–20.

The next Bank of Canada rate decision is Wednesday, October 28, 2026 at 9:45 a.m. ET, released with the October Monetary Policy Report and its updated forecasts. The questions close at 13:29 UTC that day, which is 9:29 ET.
The target for the overnight rate is currently 2.25%. A hold resolves 'Maintains rate' (0bps) and a move to 2.50% resolves 'Hike 25bps'.

At its September 15-16, 2026 meeting the FOMC voted unanimously to raise the federal funds target range by 25 bp to 3.75%–4.00%. This was the Fed's first rate increase since 2023, and it leaves the upper bound at exactly 4.00%.

The current upper bound is 4.00%, so the question needs a hike at the October 27-28 meeting to resolve Yes. A hold or a cut would leave the upper bound at or below 4.00%. A 25 bp hike would make the range 4.00%–4.25%.

In the September Summary of Economic Projections, the median participant showed one more 25 bp hike in 2026, ending the year at 4.1%. The median showed no change in 2027 and cuts in 2028 and 2029. Two FOMC meetings remain in 2026: October 27-28 and December.
New York Fed President John Williams said on Sept. 29 that one more rate increase by the end of this year could be appropriate, but that there was no need to rush.

Fed Vice Chair Philip Jefferson said on Oct. 1 that policymakers must carefully assess trends in the data and the outlook when adjusting policy, and that reaching a judgment could take more time. Chair Kevin Warsh has avoided signaling the near-term path of rates.

September nonfarm payrolls rose only 29,000, against an 84,000 consensus, and unemployment rose to 4.2% from a forecast 4.1%. July was revised to -10,000 and August down to 133,000, a combined revision of -60,000. Average hourly earnings rose 0.1% m/m and 3.0% y/y, the slowest annual wage growth since 2021.
August core PCE rose 0.2% m/m and 3.0% y/y, below the 0.3% m/m and 3.3% y/y consensus. Headline PCE rose 0.3% m/m and 3.4% y/y, with annual rates unchanged from revised July.

August CPI rose 0.4% m/m and 3.4% y/y, in line with estimates, driven by a 3.9% jump in gasoline prices. Energy prices were up 16.3% y/y amid Middle East tensions. Core CPI rose 0.3% m/m. The search summary gave core CPI at 2.4% y/y, which looks inconsistent with core PCE at 3.0%, so that figure is unverified.

Speaking at Jackson Hole, Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said 'we have work to do' on inflation and signaled a possible rate hike. At the September press conference he said inflation 'is too high, and has been for too long.'
Data still due before the Oct 28 decision: September CPI on Oct 14, September PPI on Oct 15, and import/export prices on Oct 16, all at 8:30 AM ET. The FOMC statement is due Oct 28 at 2:00 PM ET.

In late September, fixed-income traders saw the Oct. 28 meeting as the most likely point for the next move, which would take the range to 4.00%–4.25%. A Bloomingbit report on Oct 3 said expectations of an October hike fell quickly after Williams' remarks and the softer August PCE data.
At its September 16, 2026 meeting the FOMC voted unanimously to raise the federal funds target range by 25 bps to 3.75%–4.00%. It was the Fed's first rate hike since 2023.

raw_facts.fact: The September dot plot's median shows one more 25 bp hike in 2026, ending the year at about 4.1%. It shows no change in 2027 and cuts in 2028–2029. Four participants projected two more hikes in 2026. Only the October 28 and December meetings remain this year.

September nonfarm payrolls rose by only 29,000, against a consensus of about 84,000–100,000. Unemployment rose to 4.2%. Jefferies' chief U.S. economist called the report 'the nail in the coffin for an October hike'.

New York Fed President John Williams, a permanent FOMC voter, said: 'With the policy action we took at our September meeting, there is no need for urgency.' He added that incoming data 'should provide greater clarity'. Earlier, on Sept 24, he had called another hike before year-end 'reasonable'.

Fed Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman said, 'I don't currently see an urgent need for further action.' She wants time to judge the effects of the September hike. Bowman has indicated she prefers no further hikes in 2026.
After the jobs report, coverage said at least three FOMC voters were in no rush for another hike. Expectations for the next move shifted toward the December meeting rather than October 27–28.

Before the jobs report, several officials sounded hawkish. Governor Lisa Cook said the labor market 'appears to be well positioned to handle an increase in rates'. Barr (Sept 23) said further adjustments were likely needed, and Hammack (Sept 25) worried about inflation expectations. Paulson (Sept 24) said more increases may be needed.

Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said 'inflation is too high and has been for too long'. He estimated that PCE inflation was running at 3.6% year over year through August. Three members had dissented at the prior (July) meeting in favor of a hike.

August 2026 CPI rose 0.4% month over month and 3.4% year over year. Core CPI rose 0.3% month over month and 2.4% year over year, down from 2.5%. Gasoline, up 3.9% on the month, accounted for over a third of the monthly increase.

The FOMC meets October 27–28, 2026, and the decision is announced Wednesday, October 28. That is days before the November midterm elections. The minutes of the September meeting are also due in October.

Preliminary figures show 290 vessels transited Bab el-Mandeb in the week of 21–27 September 2026 (about 41 per day) and 264 in the week of 14–20 September (about 38 per day). The four-week average was 280 per week (about 40 per day). This is Lloyd's List's own count, not IMF PortWatch's.
Bab el-Mandeb transits are above the levels seen before the 2026 Middle East Gulf crisis but below the peak driven by tankers. Weekly transits averaged 316 in June 2026 and 257 in January 2026.

raw_facts.source: USNI News / Al Jazeera (summarized via search)
raw_facts.fact: After the Houthis took Mokha, Perim Island and the rest of Yemen's Red Sea coast in September 2026, daily Bab el-Mandeb traffic fell from about 35 transits to 25. It then recovered and reached 45 transits on a Sunday.

Owners and operators are carrying out plans to return to the Red Sea, with ships that had avoided the route for years increasingly tracked sailing through it. The Houthi blockade of Saudi Arabia has dampened growth, but their threats have not derailed the return.

The Houthis now control Yemen's entire Red Sea coastline, including the Bab el-Mandeb approaches. They have declared a blockade on Saudi-flagged vessels and attacked energy infrastructure. Analysts note that shipping firms might avoid the strait based on perceived risk alone.
In September 2026 the Houthis attacked Saudi Arabia's East-West crude pipeline. Their stated maritime blockade targets Saudi Arabia, and they say other ships are free to pass through Bab el-Mandeb.

A Houthi attack on the Egyptian-owned cargo ship Tihamah in Bab el-Mandeb killed six people and wounded 10. These were the first shipping deaths linked to the Houthis since the US-Israel war on Iran began in February 2026.

The Houthi naval blockade of Saudi Arabia, aimed at Saudi ships and vessels calling at Saudi ports, took effect on 20 July 2026 at 1200 UTC. Clarksons reported an average of 31 transits a day over 25–26 July, and 33 transits were preliminarily recorded on 21 July.

Even during the worst Houthi attacks in early 2024, PortWatch showed daily Bab el-Mandeb transits staying in the 30–50 range, against a pre-crisis baseline of about 50 or more a day. This is a secondary summary and unverified against PortWatch's raw series.
The lowest weekly Bab el-Mandeb transit total of the 2023–24 Houthi crisis came in the week ending 10 March 2024: 218 passages, or about 31 a day. This is Lloyd's List's count, not PortWatch's.
Daily Bab el-Mandeb transits averaged 31 in the week ended 2 March 2026, compared with a normal level of more than 70. No source found shows a 7-day average near 10 at any point since 2023.

An earlier question in the same series asked whether PortWatch's 7-day average for Bab el-Mandeb would reach 10 or fewer transit calls by 30 September 2026. Recent weekly figures (about 38–41 a day) suggest it did not, but the PortWatch page could not be read directly to confirm.

The question resolves on PortWatch's AIS-based count of 'Arrivals of Ships' (transit calls) for Bab el-Mandeb, as a 7-day moving average. The threshold is 10 or fewer, roughly a 75% drop from the current level of about 40 a day. PortWatch data usually lag by several days, and data published up to 14 days after 31 October counts.
About 25 days remain until 31 October 2026. Any qualifying daily 7-day average from market creation through 31 October triggers YES; otherwise it resolves NO once data for 31 October is published.

Physical supply is still tight. Hormuz crude exports were 33.7 million barrels for the week, 'far from normal conditions'. European diesel stocks are below the five-year average, and Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia plus drone strikes on Russian refineries are adding to supply risk.
On Oct 5, Brent held above $102 and WTI was near $91 as Middle East supply rose.

Oil fell after a Kpler report said crude flows out of the Strait of Hormuz are now above pre-war levels. OPEC and the IEA have both cut their 2026 demand forecasts, with OPEC's growth estimate at 580,000 b/d, down from 780,000 b/d. The publication date is approximate.

Unverified, from memory: a WTI drop of 18% or more within about 4 weeks is uncommon. It has happened mostly in crisis periods (2008, 2014–15, 2020) or when a geopolitical supply premium unwinds quickly, such as March–April 2022.

Before the Nov 3 settlement there are about 20 trading sessions left, including weekly EIA inventory reports, the November contract expiry around Oct 20, and any developments in the U.S.–Iran Hormuz talks.

Control goes to whichever party wins a majority of voting seats (218 of 435). Independents count toward a party only if they caucus or announce they will. In the Montana Free Press–Rutgers Eagleton poll of randomly selected registered voters (Aug 27–Sept 7, 2026), Republican Aaron Flint had 42% and Democrat Sam Forstag 41%. The margin of error was ±6 points, so the race is a statistical tie.

Public Policy Polling, sponsored by the Democratic committee The Bench, surveyed 536 registered voters on Sept 9–10 and found Forstag 45%, Flint 43% (±4.2 points). A NonStop Local News/American Pulse poll of 314 likely voters on Sept 19–24 found Flint 46%, Forstag 45%.
Cook Political Report moved MT-01 from Likely Republican to Lean Republican. Sabato's Crystal Ball also moved it from Likely Republican to Leans Republican.

Four candidates are on the Nov 3, 2026 general election ballot: Sam Forstag (D), Aaron Flint (R), Nick Sheedy (Libertarian) and Kimberly Persico (Independent). Incumbent Rep. Ryan Zinke (R) did not run for re-election, so the seat is open.
The Trump-backed No Going Back PAC spent $811,000 in September 2026 on the race. That included $743,275 on mailers opposing Forstag, mostly sent Sept 11–27.
Both the DCCC (Democrats' House campaign committee) and the NRCC (Republicans' House campaign committee) have put the open MT-01 seat on their target lists.
Forstag is running ads attacking Flint on health care and Medicaid expansion. The pro-Flint No Going Back PAC is running ads calling Forstag a lobbyist and attacking him on gender-related issues.

In 2024, Republican Ryan Zinke won MT-01 with 52.3% (168,529 votes) to Democrat Monica Tranel's 44.6% (143,783), a margin of 8.7 points.
In 2022, the district's first election after it was created in 2020 redistricting, Zinke beat Tranel 49.6% to 46.5%. Republicans have won both elections held in the district (2 of 2).
Trump won the district about 54% to 43% in 2024. Under the district's current lines, Trump beat Biden 52.2% to 45.3% in 2020.

raw_facts.source: Wikipedia (Opinion polling for the 2026 Serbian parliamentary election), citing NSPM
raw_facts.fact: The latest listed poll, NSPM on 30 Sept 2026, puts Student List at 44.4% and the SNS-led coalition (Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia) at 41.7%, with 13.9% for others. In NSPM's 30 July poll (n=1,000) the figures were Student List 39.6% and SNS 37.5%.

Faktor plus polled 986 respondents on 16–20 Sept 2026. Results: 'Aleksandar Vučić – Ujedinjena Srbija' 48.6% (up 1.4 points in a month), Studentska lista 37.1% (up 5.6 points), SPS 4.9%, European Serbia 3.6%, Authentic Right 2.8%. Faktor plus expects turnout of about 62%.
Faktor plus's August–September poll (about 1,200 respondents) had SNS at 47.2%, the Student List at 31.5% and SPS at 4.9%. Its 26 June poll had SNS 47.1% and Student List 30.7%.
CRTA's 15 July 2026 poll (n=2,324) had the Student List at 44.9% and SNS at 35.7%. According to the page, this was the first poll since July 2010 to put any option other than SNS in first place.

The article describes the race between SNS and the Student List as having tightened: some polls put SNS first and others put the Student List first. Across the polls it lists, SNS ranges from roughly 30% to 45% and the Student List from roughly 15% to 40%.

All 250 seats are allocated by closed-list proportional representation in a single nationwide constituency using the D'Hondt method. The threshold is 3% of votes and is waived for ethnic-minority lists, so the list with the most votes normally wins the most seats.

Vučić resigned as President of Serbia on 27 Sept 2026 to head the 'Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia' list as its candidate for prime minister. He had called the early election in September 2026; parliamentary elections were otherwise due by December 2027.

RIK announced 17 electoral lists and one was withdrawn, leaving 16 lists competing for 250 seats. 'Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia' is No. 1 on the ballot and 'Student List – Students Are Winning' is No. 3. Vreme describes these two as the dominant blocs in the polls.

The student movement submitted its 'Student List – Students Win' to RIK after thousands of supporters marched through Belgrade. The list has a full 250 candidates and is headed by Novi Sad cardiology professor Ilija Srdanović.

Controversies so far: fact-checkers documented pro-government tabloids using AI-manipulated photos against Srdanović; opposition parties and NGOs left a working group on improving election conditions, citing government obstruction; and the government has called the student movement a Western-funded 'colour revolution'. The 2023 election drew allegations of vote buying and transported voters.
Election day is 25 Oct 2026, with polls open 7 AM–8 PM at 8,210 polling stations for about 6.44 million registered voters. The voter-register and summary-list deadline is 9 Oct 2026.

raw_facts.source: Wikipedia (2023 Serbian parliamentary election and prior election articles)
raw_facts.fact: SNS-led lists have won the most seats in all 6 parliamentary elections since 2012 (2012, 2014, 2016, 2020, 2022, 2023), and SNS has governed throughout. This count is my own tally from the election articles rather than a single cited source, so treat it as unverified.

A Nanos poll taken Sept 30–Oct 4 had incumbent Olivia Chow at 52.4% of decided voters, Brad Bradford at 42.6% and Chris Alexander at 4%. Of all respondents, 22% said they were still undecided.
A Mainstreet Research poll released as the campaign entered its final month had Chow at 38.1%, Bradford at 32.2% and Alexander at 7.2%, a 6-point lead for Chow.

A Liaison Strategies Toronto Pulse poll had Chow ahead of Bradford 48% to 39% among decided and leaning voters, with Alexander at 10% and others at 3%. Chow's lead was slightly wider than in Liaison's previous poll, although her job approval had fallen below 50%.
An earlier Liaison poll had Chow at 47%, Bradford at 40% and Alexander at 10% among decided and leaning voters. Women backed Chow 56% to 32%, while men backed Bradford 47% to 41%.

On Tuesday, Oct. 6, the day advance voting began, Chris Alexander, a former Conservative minister who placed third, dropped out of the race. He endorsed no other candidate, and his name is likely to stay on the ballot.

Wikipedia's summary of the campaign polling says Chow has led Bradford in most polls, by 7 to 17 points. More than 60 candidates registered, and the main contenders are Chow, Bradford (councillor for Ward 19) and Alexander, who has now withdrawn.

Chow is endorsed by CUPE Local 79, LiUNA Local 183, the Toronto and York Region Labour Council and several NDP MPPs and MPs. Bradford is endorsed by Liberal MPs Yvan Baker and Judy Sgro, former MPs Peter Kent and John McKay, and musician Geddy Lee.

Bradford promised to scrap the municipal land transfer tax on homes under $1.1 million, a measure he puts at $300 million, with buyers saving up to $18,000. He also promised to cut water bills by 25%.
Advance voting began on Oct. 6, and election day is Oct. 26, 2026. The nomination period ran from May 1 to Aug. 21, 2026.

Toronto elects its mayor by first-past-the-post in a single round, so whoever gets the most votes on Oct. 26 wins and there is no runoff. Chow is the incumbent and is seeking her first full term after winning the 2023 by-election.

Israel's defense establishment says it has no information that can confirm or rule out an Iranian connection to the flydubai co-pilot. For now it assesses that he acted alone. Reportedly the Mossad, Shin Bet, IDF and Transportation Ministry all believe he was a lone wolf, not acting on orders from Iran or another terror group.
Israeli sources told CNN the co-pilot accused of trying to hijack the flydubai plane probably acted alone.
Officials said early signs point to the co-pilot acting alone. A senior US official briefed on Israel's investigation told NBC there were no signs that Iran directed or took part in the attack.

Co-pilot Hamam al-Hammami reportedly confessed, saying 'I did it as revenge for Gaza; I wanted to die as a martyr.' He reportedly planned to crash into Ben Gurion Airport and had a backup plan to target a US military base in Jordan. The report says Israeli officials hinted, without confirmation, that he had visited 'enemy countries'.
A joint UAE–Israel investigation is reportedly looking at the co-pilot's radicalisation during a stay in Syria and at a possible link to an Iranian-backed terrorist group.

PM Netanyahu said the co-pilot 'underwent Islamist radical indoctrination' and that 'We'll get to the root of this attacker, whether he had accomplices, whether Iran was behind it. I think we'll find out very soon.' He also told Fox it was 'too early to say' whether Iran was involved.

Netanyahu pointed to Iran and its proxies as intent on stepping up attacks on Israelis abroad, but did not directly attribute the flydubai attack to them. The incident comes ahead of an Israeli election and during a US-Israel war against Iran that began in late February 2026.

US President Trump suggested the co-pilot may be linked to Iran 'based on what I'm hearing' but gave no details. This went further than Netanyahu's statements. Trump is not an Israeli official, so his statement does not count for this question.

National Security Minister Ben Gvir said the alleged attack shows Israel must step up its military campaigns across the region. Ministers called for more military action after the incident (Jerusalem Post), but neither report describes a minister saying Iran or a proxy carried out or directed the attack.

The UAE Attorney General called the attack a 'terrorist act' and said investigators are checking whether al-Hammami, an Omani national born in the UAE to a Syrian mother, acted as a 'lone wolf' or had links to extremist groups. Omani authorities had earlier barred him from flying over concerns about extremist views.
Shin Bet agents have joined UAE authorities in questioning the co-pilot in the UAE, so Israeli findings about any outside links may come out of this joint probe.
Netanyahu ordered a security review of flights to Israel after the flydubai attack.

Flight FZ1073 (Dubai to Tel Aviv, about 172–174 people aboard) dropped more than 17,000 ft in about 2 minutes after the co-pilot attacked the captain with a crash axe. Passengers overpowered him and off-duty pilots landed the plane in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia.

The question closes Oct 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. To count, a statement must explicitly say Iran or a listed proxy ordered, planned, carried out or directly helped the attack. Saying they only inspired or radicalised him does not count.

BLS's August 2026 CPI release shows core CPI (all items less food and energy) up 2.4% over the 12 months to August 2026, not seasonally adjusted. It rose 0.3% in August on a seasonally adjusted basis, after 0.2% in July.

Unrounded, August 2026 core CPI was +0.29% month over month, and the 2.4% year-over-year rate was described as the lowest core rate since March 2021. Core goods were +0.68% y/y and core services +3.01% y/y.
Monthly seasonally adjusted core CPI changes in 2026: Feb 0.2%, Mar 0.4%, Apr 0.2%, May 0.0%, Jun 0.2%, Jul 0.2%, Aug 0.3%.

Year-over-year core CPI in 2026: Jan 2.5%, Feb 2.5%, Mar 2.6%, Apr 2.8%, May 2.9%, Jun 2.6%, Jul 2.5%, Aug 2.4%. Nov and Dec 2025 were 2.6%, and there is no October 2025 reading because of the 2025 lapse in appropriations.

raw_facts.source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (Sept 2025 CPI release archive)
raw_facts.fact: Base effect: the unadjusted core CPI index was 329.970 in August 2025 and 330.804 in September 2025, a non-seasonally-adjusted rise of about 0.25%. To print above 2.4% (2.5% or higher when rounded), September 2026's unadjusted core index must be at least about 338.91 (330.804 × 1.0245).
Core CPI rose 0.2% seasonally adjusted in September 2025, after 0.3% in each of July and August 2025. That September 2025 month drops out of the 12-month window in the September 2026 reading.
In August 2026, shelter rose 0.3% (3.0% y/y), owners' equivalent rent rose 0.19% m/m (about 3.08% y/y) and primary rent rose 0.17% m/m (2.75% y/y). Headline CPI rose 0.4% m/m and 3.4% y/y.

On September 10, 2026 the ECB raised the deposit facility rate by 25 bps to 2.50%, effective September 16. The main refinancing rate went to 2.65% and the marginal lending rate to 2.90%. This was the second hike of 2026.
In 2026 the ECB hiked 25 bps on June 11, which was its first hike in three years, held on July 23 and hiked 25 bps again on September 10. That puts the 2026 pattern so far at hike, pause, hike.

The next ECB Governing Council monetary policy decision is due October 29, 2026, after the October 28–29 meeting. The meeting after that is December 17, 2026, when new staff macroeconomic projections will be published.

Bundesbank President Joachim Nagel said there are 'no clear signs of second-round effects' and no 'inflation feeding through to price and wage setting'. The report took this to mean the ECB has room to wait in October. Nagel also said inflation risks 'remain tilted to the upside', which keeps a December hike open.

Eurostat's flash estimate puts euro area annual HICP inflation at 3.8% in September 2026, up from 3.2% in August and the highest since September 2023. Energy inflation was 18.8% (14.3% in August), services 3.2% (3.0%) and non-energy industrial goods 1.1% (1.2%). Prices rose 0.6% month on month.
September's 3.8% inflation reading came in above the 3.7% Bloomberg consensus.

At a European Parliament hearing, Lagarde said the inflation surge has not yet produced second-round effects and that a 'measured response' remains appropriate. She said 'We do not see evidence at this stage of energy prices feeding into higher wages.' Reuters described this as pushing back on the most aggressive market bets.
At the same hearing Lagarde said risks to growth are tilted to the downside and inflation risks to the upside. She repeated that decisions are taken meeting by meeting.

Executive Board member Isabel Schnabel named three factors for the next move: price expectations, demand, and global borrowing costs. She said 'As long as expectations are firmly anchored... monetary policy can tolerate a more gradual return of inflation to target.' She also noted that rising US yields could dampen growth more than models expect.

A Bloomberg report published right after the September hike was headlined 'ECB Officials Expect Further Rate Hikes with October in Play'. Unnamed officials said more tightening was expected and did not rule out October.
Latvia's Martins Kazaks said 'The case is building up for more tightening.' He would not say whether a hike could come in October, but said the ECB can move 'stepwise' and 'without rush'.

Reuters reported that many economists see the ECB holding at its October 29 meeting and hiking only in December, when new projections come out. It also said euro zone inflation may approach 4% by year-end.
Eurostat will publish the full September 2026 HICP data on October 16, 2026, before the October 29 decision. The October flash estimate is due after the meeting.

In the 2026 tightening cycle the ECB has hiked at 2 of its 3 meetings since June (June and September) and held at the July meeting, which had no new projections. Unverified: October is also a meeting without new projections, and the full-cycle counts here are partly from memory.

35 Senate seats are up in 2026, including specials in Florida and Ohio; 23 of them are held by Republicans. Cook rates 9 Solid D, 2 Likely D, 1 Lean D, 7 Toss-up, 1 Lean R, 2 Likely R and 13 Solid R. The toss-ups are Alaska, Iowa, Maine, Michigan, New Hampshire, Ohio and Texas.

Cook's most recent update moved Georgia from Lean to Likely Democratic, Kansas from Likely to Lean Republican, and South Carolina from Safe to Likely Republican. Separately, Cook moved Iowa from Lean Republican to Toss-up.

raw_facts.fact: Since 1934 the president's party has lost an average of 3.4 Senate seats in midterms and has lost Senate seats about two-thirds of the time. It gained seats in 1934, 1998 and 2002. Unverified: these counts come from a secondary summary.

Recent midterms in which Senate control changed include 1994, 2006 and 2014, all moving against the president's party; in 2002 control moved to the president's party. Big Senate midterm losses include 13 seats in 1958, 12 in 1946, 9 in 2014 and 8 in 1986 and 1994. Unverified: this is not a complete count from one source.

On October 6, 2026 WTI crude was quoted at $89.37/bbl, down 1.93% from the prior close, and Brent at $100.45. To reach $105, WTI would need to rise about 17.5% from this level.

Another tracker put WTI at $86.91 on October 6, 2026, down 3.82% on the day. It said WTI fell from $91.48 to $86.91 over the past 30 days, a 5.0% drop. (Trading Economics showed $87.99 on Oct 6, down 1.61%. Sources disagree on the exact figure.)
On October 5, 2026 WTI traded at $90.62/bbl and Brent at $102.30. Brent had dipped to about $101.59 earlier in the session.

Oil fell after shipping data showed Middle East crude exports above pre-war levels on 4 of the 7 days in the last week of September. G7 nations also plan to release about 100 million barrels of crude and diesel from emergency reserves.

In the week to September 25, WTI's daily opening price went from $101.00 (Mon) to $95.39 (Tue) and a low of $89.89 (Wed), then $92.72 (Thu) and $94.75 (Fri), a weekly fall of $6.25 (about 6.2%). The drop came on renewed US-Iran talks about a phased deal that could reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Brent traded near $105, the widest WTI-Brent spread since May.

Physical supply stayed tight. Crude exports through Hormuz were 33.7 million barrels for the week, roughly unchanged, and freight from the Gulf to Asia on very large crude carriers (VLCCs) added about $20/bbl. Possible US diesel export restrictions were also affecting WTI's discount to Brent.

On September 10, 2026 WTI futures rose 6.7% in one day to settle at $102.48/bbl, the highest settle since May 19, as US-Iran strikes escalated and Iranian forces reported targeting 10 vessels near Hormuz. Brent settled at $107.63 that day.

Earlier in 2026, during the Iran war, WTI went above $105. The June WTI contract settled at $105.88 in one session, and WTI reached an intraday high of $110.93. Brent peaked at $114.70 in April. (Unverified: the exact dates of these peaks were not confirmed.)

In mid-September an attack on a Saudi pipeline briefly disrupted supply. Prices then fell on reports that Saudi Arabia would offer more crude through Hormuz. This shows how sharply prices have swung in both directions on headlines.

The November 2026 WTI contract (CLX26) expires around October 20, 2026, and the December contract (CLZ26) has a last trade date of November 20, 2026. Under the active-month rule, the December contract would become the Active Month about three sessions before the November contract expires, around October 16. Check ICE's own expiry page for the exact dates.

The question resolves Yes if any Pyth 1-minute candle high for the ICE WTI (CLL) Active Month reaches $105.00 or more during an October 2026 trading session. A brief intraday spike counts; a settlement price is not required. Any gap between the November and December contract prices after the roll changes the level the Active Month needs to reach.

Iran's supreme national security council head said the Strait of Hormuz will stay shut until the US meets six conditions, including ending the war against Iran and its allies. No completed US-Iran deal to reopen the strait was reported in the sources reviewed as of early October.

raw_facts.fact: Recent general-election polls for Marshall (R) vs Hamilton (D): YouGov, Sept 24–Oct 4: 45–48. NYT/Siena, Sept 22–30: 45–45. Trafalgar (R), Sept 29–Oct 1: 44–44. Wedgewood, Sept 22–24: 48–50. GSG (D), Sept 13–16: 47–49. co/efficient (R), Sept 8–10: 49–44.

In a Sept 15–16 poll of 750 likely voters (±3.6), Hamilton had 45%, Marshall 43%, Libertarian David Graham 4%, and 8% were undecided. Hamilton led independents 42–27. In the same poll Republican Masterson led the governor's race 51–44, and Trump's approval was 40% approve, 53% disapprove.

The GOP super PAC Senate Leadership Fund paused its spending in North Carolina and moved money into Kansas. According to Ad Impact, its Kansas ad reservations total $8.2 million. The ads attack Hamilton as a 'two-face extremist.'
CNBC reports that stubborn inflation, backlash to White House trade policy, and megachurch pastor Adam Hamilton as a strong challenger have made Kansas an unexpected Senate battleground.
In the Aug 4 primaries, Marshall won the GOP nomination with 79.9% (266,135 votes) over Michael Soetaert. Hamilton won an 11-candidate Democratic primary with about 34.9% (76,105 votes).
After the primary, analysts moved their rating of the Kansas Senate race from Safe R to Likely R. By early October, Cook rated it a Tossup.

As of July 15, 2026, Marshall had raised $6.2M and had $5.4M cash on hand. Hamilton had raised $4.2M and had $1.7M cash on hand. Kansas Reflector reported that total spending on the race may exceed $50M.
It has been reported that Marshall's medical practice sued 700+ patients over unpaid bills, and 81 of those cases led to arrests. The candidates' only debate was held Sept 12 on WIBW.
Democrats have not won a U.S. Senate election in Kansas since 1932, so Republicans have won every Kansas Senate race for more than 90 years. Trump won Kansas by 16 points in 2024.
In 2020, polls showed a close race (PPP in August: Marshall 43–42; NYT/Siena in late October: Marshall 46–42). Marshall won 53.2% and a margin of about R+11.4.

In 2014, independent Greg Orman led or was tied with Republican Pat Roberts in many October polls (Marist early October had Orman ahead; Monmouth had a 46–46 tie). Roberts won 53.15% to 42.53%, a margin of about 10.6 points. Unverified: this is only 2 recent cases where Kansas polls underestimated the Republican.

The US blockade of Iranian ports is still being enforced. CENTCOM has turned back 130 commercial vessels since the blockade restarted in mid-July, most recently on October 5. It says it will 'swiftly act against any vessels trying to run the blockade.'
Over the past 12 weeks, CENTCOM has disabled 3 vessels that refused orders and destroyed 13 ships it linked to blockade violations or the IRGC's 'shadow network'.

State media quoted Iranian President Pezeshkian saying 'negotiations are meaningless' with the US, because it 'breaks its commitments' and has 'attacked us three times after talks.' Iran's legal affairs minister said Iran is still reviewing the US response to Araghchi's seven-day proposal. Trump said the conflict is 'essentially almost over.'

Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf said the Strait of Hormuz stays closed until the US meets seven conditions based on the June memorandum of understanding. Iran rejected US nuclear demands and insists the blockade must be settled first. An Iranian official said the strait could reopen within seven days if the conditions are met.
Iran said it has received the official US response to its latest proposal to end the war, which has lasted about seven months. Araghchi delivered the US proposal to Tehran around September 30.

Araghchi proposed that Iran reopen Hormuz and resume nuclear talks within 7 days if the US lifts the naval blockade, waives oil sanctions and agrees to a ceasefire that includes Lebanon. Trump publicly rejected it ('It is what we would have maybe agreed to a year ago') but told Axios he expected talks to continue. (Date approximate: the weekend after the September 22 UN meeting.)

Unnamed sources said US and Iranian negotiators in New York were discussing a phased deal: Iran reopens Hormuz and the US lifts its blockade. The main obstacle is that neither side wants to give up its leverage first. A deal would mean Trump accepting another temporary fix after the earlier understanding collapsed in July.

At the UN, Araghchi met US envoys Witkoff and Kushner for three hours, the first structured face-to-face US–Iran contact of this conflict. Witkoff called the talks 'promising, constructive.' Qatar is passing messages between the two sides.
Iran loaded no crude onto tankers in September 2026, down from about 250,000 barrels per day in August. It is the first such month since the war began in February.

Precedent: the first blockade began April 13, 2026, and was lifted after Trump and Iran announced an agreement on June 14. The MOU was signed at Versailles on June 17 and CENTCOM removed the blockade on June 18, about 9 weeks after it started. The deal gave both sides 60 days to negotiate.

The June lifting held for less than a month. Trump announced the blockade's return on July 13 and enforcement began July 14. As of October 6 the second blockade has lasted about 12 weeks, with no official announcement ending it.

Only an official, declarative US government announcement of a general end or suspension of the blockade counts; exemptions for specific vessels or ports do not. Reports of talks about a phased deal from unnamed sources do not count. The deadlines are October 15 and October 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET.

A Faktor plus poll of 986 respondents (16–20 Sept 2026) had 'Aleksandar Vučić – Ujedinjena Srbija' (SNS) at 48.6%, the Student List at 37.1%, SPS at 4.9%, Evropska Srbija at 3.6%, Autentična desnica at 2.8% and Mi snaga naroda at 1.2%. It also found 16% of voters undecided and put expected turnout at about 62%.
In the Faktor Plus poll, the Student List was at 37.1%, 5.6 points higher than in that pollster's previous survey. The Vučić-led list was at 48.6%.
A BIRODI poll from around late August or early September 2026 put the Student List at 48.5% and SNS at 38.6%. The publication date is approximate.

A June 2026 survey by CRTA and Stanford researchers had the Student List ahead of SNS among decided voters, 44.9% to 35.7%. The article also said Faktor Plus did not disclose who commissioned its September poll, which showed SNS ahead 48.6% to 37.1%.
Ilija Srdanović, a cardiologist and medical professor from Novi Sad, heads the Student List's 250-candidate slate on the ballot. However, the movement says the list has no figurehead leader.

The election guide names Srdanović as the Student List's list bearer but does not say he, or anyone else, is the list's designated candidate for prime minister. The Student List has often distanced itself from the opposition, though parties including DS, Kreni-Promeni and Dveri back its campaign and People's Serbia withdrew its own list to support it.

Aleksandar Vučić resigned as President of Serbia on 27 September 2026, about eight months before his term ended, to lead SNS's 'United Serbia' list and run for prime minister. Assembly Speaker Ana Brnabić became acting president.
Vučić signed a decree dissolving the National Assembly and calling early parliamentary elections for 25 October 2026. They had originally been due by December 2027.
Sixteen certified electoral lists are running in the 25 October 2026 parliamentary election, with about 6.44 million registered voters. Election day is the same day the question closes.

The 250 Assembly seats are allocated by closed-list proportional representation in one nationwide constituency, using d'Hondt with a 3% threshold that is waived for ethnic-minority lists. A prime minister must be elected by an Assembly majority, so a government is formed after the vote and not on election day.
The current Prime Minister is Đuro Macut, an independent who succeeded Miloš Vučević on 16 April 2025.

SNS has governed Serbia since 2012. UNVERIFIED (from memory): SNS-led lists came first in all 6 parliamentary elections since 2012 (2012, 2014, 2016, 2020, 2022, 2023), and every prime minister since 2014 has been from SNS or backed by it.

At its meeting ending 16 September 2026, the MPC voted 6–3 to keep Bank Rate at 3.75%. Bailey, Breeden, Dhingra, Lombardelli, Ramsden and Taylor voted to hold; Greene, Mann and Pill voted to raise it 25bp to 4.00%.

The September minutes say the Committee 'stands ready to act as necessary' to keep CPI on track for 2%, without explicit guidance on the next move. The MPC projects CPI inflation reaching slightly above 4% in early 2027.

Governor Bailey said: 'the longer this volatility persists, the bigger the impact it will have on inflation, and the more likely it is we will need to raise Bank Rate to ensure that inflation falls back to our 2% target.' CNBC reported the Bank held rates even though the Fed had raised its rate.

ING reported that Bailey described a possible November move as an 'insurance hike' based on risk management rather than incoming data. ING said whether the Bank hikes depends on whether oil and gas prices stay high over the six weeks to November.
The September minutes say the next MPC meeting concludes on 4 November 2026, with the decision and minutes published on 5 November 2026. That matches the market's resolution date.

The minutes say members who voted to hold pointed to weaker-than-expected pass-through of energy costs to other goods, few second-round effects in wages and prices so far, restrictive financial conditions, domestic slack and a soft labour market. One member said policy should respond to 'evidence of propagation rather than mechanically to volatile ticks in headline energy prices.'

Alan Taylor, who voted to hold, said the surge in gas and oil prices has 'clearly increased near-term inflation risks.' He added that higher energy costs 'still appear largely concentrated within the energy complex itself rather than spreading widely through the economy.'

raw_facts.fact: The question resolves on whoever is formally sworn in as PM after the October 27, 2026 election. The economy added 29,000 nonfarm payroll jobs in September 2026, against forecasts of roughly 80,000-100,000. Unemployment rose to 4.2% from 4.1%. August was revised down from 162,000 to 133,000 and July from a gain to a loss of 10,000, for a combined downward revision of 60,000.

On September 2, 2026 the Bank of Canada kept its overnight rate at 2.25%. That was its seventh straight hold since it cut from 2.50% in October 2025. The Bank said upside risks to its inflation forecast had increased because of the Middle East conflict and new US tariffs and Canadian counter-tariffs.

raw_facts.source: StockWireX / Bank of Canada media advisory
raw_facts.fact: In a September 21, 2026 speech to the Halifax Partnership, Governor Macklem warned that waiting too long to raise rates would force steeper and higher hikes. He said inflation is expected to edge up in the coming months and named oil (near US$100/bbl), trade uncertainty and inflation expectations as the factors that could bring the timing of hikes forward.

The summary of Governing Council deliberations for the September 2 decision says members agreed that 'the risk that inflation spreads to other goods and services had risen.' It says policy will be guided by the inflation forecast and the risks around it, and that the economy and inflation evolved broadly as forecast in the July Report.

As of October 1, UBS, Manulife, Oxford Economics and Scotiabank were publicly forecasting a 25bp hike in October. National Bank and Scotiabank were reported as forecasting 2.50% in October and 2.75% by December. TD Economics expected the Bank to hold for the rest of 2026.

CIBC argues that Canada's inflation is narrow and mostly driven by fuel: gasoline adds about 0.8 percentage points of the 3% CPI, and only 38% of 55 major CPI components are above 3%. It suggests a Canadian hike could come in 2027 rather than October.
Canada's August 2026 CPI was 3.0% y/y, unchanged from July. CPI excluding gasoline rose to 2.4% from 2.2%, the BoC's trim and median core measures were around 2.0%, and gasoline was up 22.8% y/y.

Q2 GDP grew 1.2% y/y, and Q3 growth is estimated at 1.4% to 2% annualized. Business investment rose for the first time since Q4 2024. UBS projects September CPI at 3.3%.

September CPI is due around October 19–20, 2026, before the decision. The Bank of Canada announces its rate decision, together with the October Monetary Policy Report, on October 28, 2026 at 9:45 am ET.
The next Bank of Canada rate decision is October 28, 2026 at 9:45 am ET. The September Labour Force Survey, usually released in early October, comes out before that.

At its September 16, 2026 meeting the FOMC voted 12-0 to raise the federal funds target range by 25 bp to 3.75%–4.00%. The current upper bound is therefore exactly 4.00%, so only a hike at the Oct 27–28 meeting would put it above 4.00%.
The September hike was the first rate increase since 2023.

The September dot plot's median shows one more 25 bp hike by end-2026 (to about 4.1%). Sixteen of 18 participants projected at least one more hike this year, and four projected two. Two FOMC meetings remain in 2026: October 27–28 and December.
The September jobs report showed payrolls up only 29,000, against estimates of more than 80,000. Unemployment rose to 4.2% from 4.1%, and wage growth slowed.

NY Fed President John Williams said there is 'no need for urgency' and that 'one further upward adjustment' may be appropriate late this year. Vice Chair Jefferson said future moves should come from 'carefully examining trends in the data.' Minneapolis Fed's Kashkari said he had no strong view on hiking at the end of October. Dallas Fed's Logan called September's hike a 'first step' but did not say when the next one should come.

Yahoo Finance reported that the weak September jobs report is likely to keep the Fed on hold in October, with attention staying on inflation. The August PCE release on Sept 30 came in cooler than expected, though core PCE was still running at about 3%.

Fed officials including Williams, Barr, Hammack and Paulson said further hikes may be needed because inflation has been above 2% for 5.5 years. Governor Cook pointed to inflation pressure from the AI buildout and from oil prices. Diesel was $6.529/gal, up from $3.739 a year earlier.
September CPI comes out October 14, 2026 at 8:30 AM ET. It is the last CPI report before the October 27–28 FOMC meeting. The prior (August) headline CPI was 3.4% year over year.

Graham Platner won the June 9 Democratic primary, then withdrew on July 10 after a sexual assault allegation, which he denies. On July 25, Democratic convention delegates in Bangor picked former state Senate President Troy Jackson as the replacement nominee: Jackson got 566 votes and Sandra Pelletier got 5.

In Marist's Oct 1–4, 2026 poll of 1,505 Maine registered voters (MoE ±3.8), Jackson (D) had 51% and Collins (R) 47%. Jackson led independents 52–45. Asked who will actually win, 57% said Collins and 41% said Jackson. Trump approval in Maine was 40% approve, 59% disapprove.

The CBS/YouGov poll of 1,144 Maine registered voters (Sept 23–Oct 1, MoE ±4.7) found Collins and Jackson tied, and about 10% said they could still change their minds. Collins drew about 1 in 5 voters who disapprove of Trump, and Jackson ran behind Democratic governor nominee Hannah Pingree. Four in ten Democrats and most independents said they wished someone else were the Democratic nominee.
An AARP poll released around Oct 1, 2026 showed Jackson narrowly ahead of incumbent Collins, by a margin AARP called slim.

A late-September UMass Lowell Maine poll had Jackson at 51% and Collins at 47%, which the pollsters described as essentially a tie given the margin of error. Independents split 49% Jackson, 47% Collins.
A search-result summary gave the polling average as Jackson 47.6% and Collins 47.5%, about a tie. I did not read the RCP page itself to confirm this.
A July 2026 UNH poll, taken before Jackson was nominated, had Jackson at 49% and Collins at 46% among likely general election voters.

In 2020, Democrat Sara Gideon led Collins in every independent public poll that year. Collins trailed by 5.5 points in the final RCP average (Emerson had Gideon +6 at the end of October, Quinnipiac +12 in September), yet Collins won by about 9 points. That is a polling miss of roughly 14–15 points, all in Collins's favor.

In 2020, Collins won by about 9 points while Biden also carried Maine by about 9, which shows heavy ticket-splitting in her favor. Collins has won five straight Senate elections (1996, 2002, 2008, 2014, 2020); this count is from memory and was not checked against a source.

In their first debate on Oct 6 (CBS 13/WGME), Collins and Jackson blamed each other for Mainers' economic struggles and called each other corrupt. Jackson attacked Collins for voting with Trump 96% of the time and for her vote to advance the 'One Big Beautiful Bill', which is projected to cut Maine's Medicaid funding.
Three more Collins–Jackson debates are scheduled, on Oct 8, Oct 13 and Oct 15. The general election is Nov 3, 2026.

Maine uses ranked-choice voting for statewide federal races, so if no one wins a first-round majority, lower-ranked choices are redistributed until someone does. An IVN article refers to four Senate candidates sharing a debate stage, but I could not confirm which independent or third-party candidates are on the 2026 general election ballot.

A New York Times/Siena poll of 615 Texas voters, taken Sept. 21–30, 2026, had Democrat James Talarico at 51% and Republican Ken Paxton at 45%, with a margin of error of ±4.5. The same pollster's June 2026 poll had the race tied 47–47.

A Fox News poll of 881 likely voters, taken Sept. 24–28, 2026, had Talarico at 51% and Paxton at 49%, with a margin of error of ±3. Talarico's favorability was 52% favorable to 44% unfavorable; Paxton's was 40% to 58%.

As of Oct. 5, 2026, the RealClearPolitics polling average had Talarico at 48.4% and Paxton at 45.3%, so Talarico was ahead by 3.1 points. About 6% of voters were undecided or backing other candidates.

A recent Texas Southern University poll had Talarico at 47% and Paxton at 46%. A University of Texas/Texas Politics Project poll had Talarico at 42% and Paxton at 39%, leaving a large share undecided. Exact field dates were not confirmed.

AP projected that Attorney General Ken Paxton won the Republican runoff, beating Sen. John Cornyn after President Trump endorsed Paxton the week before. Cornyn had led the March 3 primary but fell short of a majority. Cornyn is the first Republican senator from Texas to lose his party's renomination.

As of early October, ad spending in the race had reached $442 million, making it the second-most expensive non-presidential race in U.S. history. Republicans accounted for $326 million and Democrats for $116 million. In the NYT/Siena poll, 57% disapproved of Trump's job performance, up 5 points from June.

In the Fox News poll, 53% of likely voters said they were concerned Talarico is too liberal and 51% said they were concerned Paxton is too close to Trump. 68% called cost of living extremely important to their vote.

Talarico accepted TV debates on Oct. 6 (WFAA, Dallas) and Oct. 13 (KXAN, Austin). As of late September, Paxton had not committed to any specific debate date, and WFAA reported his campaign had not responded since Aug. 24.

In the same polling cycle, Republican Gov. Greg Abbott led Democrat Gina Hinojosa by 4 points (50–46) in one poll, and another poll showed the governor's race tied. Libertarian Ted Brown also appears in some Senate polls.
Early voting in Texas starts Oct. 19, 2026, and Election Day is Nov. 3, 2026.

In the 2024 Texas Senate race, the final polling average had Ted Cruz up about 3.8 points (49.0 to 45.2), but he won by 8.5 points (53.05% to 44.56%). The polls underestimated the Republican margin by about 4.7 points.

In 2018, final polls mostly had Cruz ahead of Beto O'Rourke by 3 to 6 points (Emerson +3, UT-Tyler +3.6, Quinnipiac +5, Texas Tribune +6). Cruz won by about 2.6 points (51% to 48%), so the Democrat did slightly better than most polls showed.
Texas has not elected a Democrat to any statewide office in about 30 years, since 1994. From memory and unverified: the last Democrat to win a Texas U.S. Senate race was Lloyd Bentsen in 1988.

The question resolves once AP, Fox News and NBC all call the race for the same candidate, and otherwise on official certification. Paxton is the Republican nominee. From memory and unverified: Texas general elections are decided by plurality, with no general-election runoff.

On 10 September 2026 the ECB raised the deposit facility rate by 25 bps, from 2.25% to 2.50%. This was its second hike since the US-Iran war began. From 16 September the key rates are: deposit facility 2.50%, main refinancing operations 2.65%, marginal lending 2.90%.

Governing Council member Joachim Nagel said there are 'no clear signs of second-round effects taking hold just yet', which suggests room to wait before tightening again. He also said inflation risks 'remain tilted to the upside' and the ECB should 'remain flexible and respond to incoming data'. The article describes this as a case for an October pause, with a December hike still possible.

President Lagarde said measured ECB hikes remain appropriate because this year's inflation has not yet produced dangerous second-round effects. She repeated that decisions are made meeting by meeting, with no pre-commitment to a rate path.

The September flash HICP for the euro area was 3.8%, up from 3.2% in August and the highest since September 2023. The rise was mainly energy-driven, and core and services pressures were described as 'broadly contained': German core was unchanged at 2.4% and Italian core rose from 1.4% to 1.6%.

MUFG wrote that the bar for an October ECB hike had risen after Lagarde's more measured tone and a pullback in gas prices. It said a renewed rise in energy markets over the coming weeks would be needed for the hawks to push for an October move.

Commentary on recent policymaker remarks says October 'looks more and more like a pause'. Nordea economists reportedly do not forecast an October hike but keep forecasts for hikes in December and March.

Executive Board member Isabel Schnabel gave a clearly hawkish view of the inflation outlook. Econostream judged that the policy signal at the end of her speech points away from an October hike unless conditions worsen significantly in the coming weeks. In Berlin she called recent moves in energy prices 'quite concerning', citing diesel, reduced refining capacity, low European gas storage and competition with Asia for LNG. The exact date of the speech was not confirmed.
So far in this 2026 hiking cycle the ECB has alternated: +25 bps on 11 June, hold on 23 July, +25 bps on 10 September. That is 2 hikes and 1 hold in the last 3 meetings.

The Governing Council's monetary policy meeting is scheduled for 28-29 October 2026, with the decision announced on 29 October. The euro area flash HICP for October is normally published after that meeting, so the September 3.8% print is the last full inflation reading available before the decision.
The question resolves on the change in the deposit facility rate, currently 2.50%. The ECB has moved all three key rates in 25 bp steps in 2026, keeping the MRO 15 bps above the deposit rate.

raw_facts.fact: At its September 15–16, 2026 meeting the FOMC voted 12-0 to raise the federal funds target range by 25 bps, from 3.50%–3.75% to 3.75%–4.00%. It was the first increase since 2023.

In the September dot plot, 16 of 18 participants projected at least one more hike in 2026. The median 2026 year-end rate was 4.1%, which equals one more 25 bp hike at either the October or December meeting. Some reports say four participants projected two more hikes.

August core PCE rose 0.2% m/m, below the 0.3% forecast. Year-over-year core PCE was 3.0% for August, and July was revised down to 3.0% from 3.3%. Headline PCE was 3.4% y/y.
NY Fed President John Williams said the September hike had 'removed any urgency' and that one more increase 'may be appropriate before the end of 2026.'

Vice Chair Philip Jefferson said officials will 'need to come to our own judgment, which may take more time.' On the hawkish side, Boston Fed President Susan Collins said inflation has been 'too high for too long,' and KC Fed President Jeff Schmid said 'we just haven't fulfilled our promise on the inflation side.'
A White House economist said, citing the weak September jobs report, that Fed rate hikes may be over for 2026.
Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said 'inflation is too high' and described the September hike as removing a 'dose of accommodation.' He said the Fed wants a 'timelier' approach to curbing inflation.

In his Jackson Hole speech, Warsh cited 12-month PCE inflation of 3.7% and a six-month annualized rate of 4.1%. He said underlying inflation 'has not meaningfully improved.' Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack said 'it is time for the Fed to act with rate hikes.' (Exact date unverified.)
September CPI is due October 14, 2026, which is the main inflation release left before the October 28 decision. The September PCE report is due October 29, one day after the decision.

The outcomes are mutually exclusive. If the FOMC leaves the 3.75%–4.00% range unchanged on October 28, or the meeting is canceled, 'Fed maintains rate' resolves Yes. A 25 bp increase to 4.00%–4.25% resolves 'Hike 25bps' Yes, and a 50 bp hike resolves both of these No.

In CRTA's poll, fielded 13–27 September 2026, 44% of citizens backed the Student List and 32% backed the Vučić-led bloc (United Serbia). These shares appear to be of the whole sample, not only of decided voters.

raw_facts.fact: NSPM's poll, fielded in the first ten days of September 2026, had the Student List at 44.4% and United Serbia at 41.7%. Its previous poll had them at 39.6% and 37.5%.

Faktor Plus polled 986 people on 16–20 September 2026. Results: 'Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia' 48.6%, Student List 37.1%, SPS 4.9%, European Serbia 3.6%, Authentic Right 2.8%, Mi snaga naroda 1.2%, others/minorities 1.8%. Expected turnout was about 62%.

In Faktor Plus's September poll, the Student List rose 5.6 points from the previous poll and United Serbia rose 1.4 points. Faktor Plus's director said the opposition vote had consolidated because the People's Movement of Serbia, Ecological Uprising and New Face of Serbia had withdrawn from the race.
Faktor Plus's previous poll had SNS/United Serbia at 47.2% and the Student List at 31.5%.

An earlier CRTA/Stanford Democracy Action Lab face-to-face poll of 2,324 adults, fielded from 10 June, found 44.9% of decided voters (about 70% of the sample) for the Student List, 35.7% for SNS and 3.8% for SPS, with all others below the threshold. The article date is unconfirmed. Vučić publicly rejected CRTA's findings as propaganda.

The main lists on the ballot are: 1 'Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia' (SNS-led); 2 'Ivica Dačić – Factor of Stability' (SPS, JS, SDPS, Zeleni); 3 'Student List – Students Are Winning' (ballot carrier Ilija Srdanović); 8 'Authentic Right – Dr. Miloš Jovanović' (NADA); 9 'European Serbia' (SSP and SRCE, led by Tepić and Ponoš). Wikipedia says polls are split, with some putting SNS first and others putting the Student List first.

DS, Green–Left Front, PSG (which left the Platform for European Serbia), New Face of Serbia and Ecological Uprising endorsed the Student List. SSP/SRCE (European Serbia) and NADA are running their own lists, so the opposition vote is split across several lists.
Vučić said he would resign as president on 27 September to campaign as the head of the United Serbia list. SNS nominated him as its candidate for prime minister.

All 250 seats are elected by closed-list proportional representation in one nationwide constituency, allocated by the D'Hondt method. There is a 3% threshold, which does not apply to ethnic-minority lists, and 126 seats is a majority. Because seats closely follow vote share among lists that pass the threshold, the list with the most votes would almost certainly also win the most seats.
16 lists are officially registered for the 25 October election: 17 were submitted, 1 was withdrawn and 1 was cancelled by the Republic Electoral Commission (RIK). Five of the 16 have minority status.

The early election was called on 9 September 2026 and will be held on 25 October 2026. The OSCE/ODIHR and CeSID will observe it, and TV debates are running on N1, RTS, Nova and Insajder through late September and October.

CRTA accused Vučić of trying to discredit it as an election observer and as a witness to possible fraud. The article date is unconfirmed. Separately, monitors report that Student List leader Ilija Srdanović has had no live appearances on national-coverage TV channels since 15 September.

Unverified, partly from memory: an SNS-led list won the most seats in each Serbian parliamentary election from 2012 to 2023 (2012, 2014, 2016, 2020, 2022, 2023, so 6 of 6). In December 2023 it won about 46.7% against about 23.6% for Serbia Against Violence.

An unnamed Israeli official familiar with the matter said 'there is no information that can rule out or confirm an Iranian connection to or involvement with the co-pilot.' The defense establishment's current assessment is that Omani co-pilot Hamam al-Hammami acted alone. The article names no Israeli minister who has claimed Iran was behind it.

The Mossad is in direct contact with its UAE and Saudi counterparts. Israel says it is still building a final profile of Hammami to decide whether he was a lone wolf, belonged to an organization, or was sent directly by Iran. Information passed to Israel so far has not settled this.

Asked about Iranian involvement, PM Netanyahu said it was 'too early to say' and added: 'We'll get to the root of this attacker, whether he had accomplices, whether Iran was behind it. I think we'll find out very soon.'

Netanyahu said the attacker 'underwent Islamist radicalization' and that investigators were 'examining whether he was sent, and whoever sent him will pay a very heavy price.' Two Israeli officials told Reuters that no evidence of Iranian involvement had been found so far and that the attacker appeared to have acted independently.

According to The Wall Street Journal, Omani authorities had earlier grounded the co-pilot over concerns that he had become radicalized. It is unclear whether Oman shared those concerns with other governments or airlines.

US President Trump said of possible Iranian involvement: 'I would say the answer, based on what I'm hearing, is yes, but we're working on it right now.' He later said 'I do. I personally do' believe Iran was responsible. He gave no evidence. Statements by US officials do not count toward resolution, which requires an Israeli government statement.

Shin Bet agents are taking part in the UAE interrogation of the co-pilot. He told interrogators he planned to crash a plane full of Israelis before flydubai hired him, chose the airline because it flies to Tel Aviv, and wanted revenge for what he called the 'genocide in Gaza.'
Israel has made no official suggestion of Iranian involvement. Defense Minister Katz called the co-pilot a terrorist who aimed to crash the plane but did not attribute the attack to Iran.

The UAE described the September 30 FZ1073 incident as an attempted 'terrorist operation.' It said the co-pilot attacked Captain Smit Machchhar with an emergency axe. The plane, carrying 174 people, landed in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia.

The question resolves Yes only if the Israeli government (e.g. the PM or a cabinet minister) explicitly says Iran or a listed proxy ordered, carried out, planned, or directly aided the attack by October 31, 2026. Saying he was radicalized or inspired by Islamist or Hamas ideas does not count. Netanyahu's 'radical Islamist indoctrination' remark is that kind of inspiration-only statement.
