The film's own Rotten Tomatoes page shows a 68% Tomatometer from 50 reviews, which is about 34 fresh and 16 rotten. The Popcornmeter shows 0 verified ratings, and the page lists a release date of October 9, 2026.

Earlier on October 7, outlets reported a 70% critics score from 43 reviews, about 30 fresh and 13 rotten. That means the 7 reviews added since then split roughly 4 fresh and 3 rotten, and the score drifted down from 70% to 68%.

From 34 fresh out of 50: two rotten reviews in a row would make it 34/52, or 65.4%, shown as 65%, which does not count as above 65. Seven rotten reviews in a row would make it 34/57, or 59.6%, shown as 60%, which does not count as above 60. Fresh reviews added along the way would mean more rotten ones are needed.

The questions resolve on the Tomatometer at 10:00 AM ET on Monday, October 12, 2026, the Monday after the October 9 wide release. The score must be strictly above the strike, so 65 resolves 'Above 65' as No.

Critics are divided. They praise Sorkin's dialogue but call the directing 'mundane and too dense,' and say the film lacks the sharpness and stakes of The Social Network (96%). Jeremy Strong's Zuckerberg is called 'robotic' by some critics and captivating by others.
At 70%, Screen Rant ranked it Sorkin's third-lowest-rated film. Only Malice (54%) and Being the Ricardos (68%) were lower. On the RT page, Molly's Game, which Sorkin directed, is listed at 82%.

Pull quotes on the page include harsh rotten ones: 'a pale and pathetic facsimile of a prestige drama' and a jab at whether Sorkin 'knows what the word reckoning means'. A positive review notes Sorkin's 'passion for the subject is unmistakable'.
As of October 1, the film was in a slow rollout to critics. Early reactions online were described as 'rather mid', and the film had 0 Tomatometer reviews in late September.

The US theatrical release is Friday, October 9, 2026. The film skipped the fall festivals and held an early screening on September 17 with Kara Swisher, so more reviews are likely to arrive through release weekend before the October 12 check.

The Vermont Public/Braun Research poll released Sept 28, 2026 has Republican Gov. Phil Scott at 42% and Democrat Amanda Janoo at 32%. Among likely voters it is Scott 44%, Janoo 34%, with 16% undecided or no opinion. Scott's job approval is 45%, down 15 points from Vermont Public's 2022 poll.

The UNH Green Mountain State Poll (835 likely voters, online, Sept 17–21, 2026, margin of error ±3.4) has Janoo at 49% and Scott at 43%, with 6% undecided and 2% for another candidate. The pollsters called it a statistical tie.

In UNH's July poll Scott led Janoo by 15 points, so its September poll is a 21-point swing toward Janoo. In UNH polling, Scott's approval fell from 61% (October 2025) to 52% (July 2026) to 47% (September 2026).
Scott was still rated the most popular governor in the country in Morning Consult's July 2026 data. His campaign says public polling has always undercounted his support.

Scott has won his last three reelection bids by at least 40 points each, including 73% of the vote in 2024. He has won five straight governor's races since 2016, and Vermont Public calls 2026 his tightest race since he was first elected.

Scott won the Republican primary with 98.5% (21,466 votes), facing only write-ins, and is the Republican nominee. Janoo won the Democratic primary with 49.1% (39,614 votes) to Aly Richards' 46.6% (37,570). Democratic primary turnout was about 80,700, compared with about 21,800 on the Republican side.

Three minor candidates are also on the general election ballot: June Goodband (Green Mountain Peace and Justice), Brian Judd (independent) and Dean Roy (Freedom and Unity). Bernie Sanders, the Vermont Democratic Party and 2022 nominee Brendan Brendan... [see correction]

Janoo outraised Scott in September, $291,000 to $223,000. Cycle totals are $706,000 raised for Janoo and $414,000 for Scott; cash on hand is $280,000 for Janoo and $296,000 for Scott. Scott spent about $137,000 on TV ads in September and Janoo about $60,000.
Scott said Democratic enthusiasm is the toughest reelection headwind he has faced since 2016. He defended unpopular decisions such as calling state employees back to the office.

In July 2026, after Scott's approval hit a four-year low in UNH polling, a UNH pollster said this could be the year Democrats unseat him. Coverage links part of his decline to his vetoes of progressive bills.
Two debates remain: Vermont Public on Oct 21, 2026 at 7 p.m. and WCAX on Oct 28, 2026 at 7 p.m. Scott has turned down earlier candidate forums. Election day is Nov 3, 2026.

Vermont elects its governor to a two-year term, and Scott is running for a sixth. If no candidate gets a majority of the vote, the Vermont General Assembly picks the governor from the top three, so a plurality win alone may not settle the race.

In the August 2026 CPI, core CPI (all items less food and energy) rose 0.3% from July, slightly above forecasts. The 12-month core rate edged down to 2.4%, and the three-month annualized pace was 2.0%.
12-month core CPI rates for 2026: Jan 2.5%, Feb 2.5%, Mar 2.6%, Apr 2.8%, May 2.9%, Jun 2.6%, Jul 2.5%, Aug 2.4%. The rate has fallen in each of the last three releases.

For the 12 months ending September 2025, the core rate was 3.0%. September 2026 drops the September 2025 monthly core change out of the 12-month window and replaces it with the September 2026 change. BLS reported the September 2025 change as about 0.2% seasonally adjusted (recalled from memory, unverified). So a September 2026 monthly core change above about 0.2% would tend to push the 12-month rate up from 2.4%. The question needs the published one-decimal figure to be 2.5% or higher.
BLS published no October 2025 CPI data because of the 2025 lapse in appropriations (government shutdown). The 12-month core rate was 2.6% in November and December 2025.

Within August core, non-housing core services rose 0.6% from July: airfares +2.7%, hotels +2.4%, wireless services +5.9%. Core goods rose 0.1%. Headline CPI rose 0.4% on the month and held at 3.4% year over year, with gasoline up 3.9%.
TD described August core as ending a three-month run of softer readings. Oil prices were near $100 a barrel, which TD said was keeping headline inflation high.
BLS releases the September 2026 CPI on Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at 8:30 AM ET, the same day the question closes (12:25 UTC). September PPI follows on October 15 and September PCE on October 29.
The September CPI is the last inflation report before the Federal Reserve meeting on October 27–28, 2026.

Quaest runoff poll (Oct 2–3, n=3,702, ±2 pts, taken before the first round), total votes: Flávio 44% (up from 42%), Lula 42% (unchanged), blank/null/won't vote 13%, undecided 1%.

The runoff between Flávio Bolsonaro and Lula is on October 25, 2026. The question closes 2026-10-26 03:59 UTC. To resolve Yes, Flávio must win by 4–8 points of valid votes, and a margin exactly on a bracket edge goes to the higher bracket.

Democrats have not won a Florida U.S. Senate race since 2012. Republicans won the 2016, 2018, 2022 and 2024 races.
The special general election is November 3, 2026. The winner serves the rest of Rubio's term, through 2028. Florida has no general-election runoff, so the plurality winner takes the seat.

Daily WTI front-month highs so far in October 2026 were: Oct 1 93.68, Oct 2 93.51, Oct 5 91.88, Oct 6 90.05, and Oct 7 90.98 (intraday, possibly incomplete). The highest October print so far is 93.68, which is $6.32 below $100. These are NYMEX-style figures, not the Pyth/ICE CLL feed the market resolves on.

WTI traded above $100 in mid-September 2026: highs were 104.04 (Sep 10), 104.46 (Sep 11), 100.03 (Sep 14), 101.69 (Sep 15), 105.63 (Sep 16) and 102.47 (Sep 17). From Sep 18 to Oct 7 the highest daily high was 98.01 (Sep 18), and no day after Sep 24 (96.78) had a high above 96.54.

Recent WTI daily ranges have been wide, often $3–6 from high to low (for example, Oct 2: 88.06–93.51; Sep 29: 88.78–94.74; Sep 10: 95.37–104.04). On Sep 10, WTI closed up about $6.4 (96.05 to 102.48) in a single session.
On Oct 1, 2026, Brent rose more than 4% to $102.31 and WTI nearly 3% to $92.87 after reports that the US was sending a third aircraft carrier to the Middle East. US diesel was $6.40/gal.

Prices fell for five straight days (about 17% in total) after Sep 17, when Saudi crude was reportedly routed through Hormuz after a pipeline loss. WTI's Sep 17 close of $101.91 was the period high, and WTI recovered to $92.16 on Sep 23 after Iran's president said the country would not surrender.

Escalating US-Iran fighting pushed Brent above $100 (closing at $101.21) on Sep 9, 2026, with WTI at $96.05, both the highest closes since May. In August, prices swung on Hormuz reopening hopes, the US blockade of the strait, and new sanctions on Iran, with WTI between about $78 and $87.

In the 12 months to August 2026, the CPI-U all-items index rose 3.4% (not seasonally adjusted), the same rate as for the 12 months to July. The NSA index was 334.980 in August 2026, up 0.3% from July before seasonal adjustment. On a seasonally adjusted basis it rose 0.4%.

The September 2025 CPI-U NSA index was 324.800, and August 2025 was 323.976, so September 2025 rose about 0.25% NSA month over month. My own calculation: a published 12-month rate above 3.6% (3.7% or higher after rounding, i.e. at least 3.65%) needs a September 2026 index of about 336.66 or more. That is roughly a +0.50% NSA rise from August's 334.980. A rise of about +0.40% NSA (index about 336.33) would round to 3.6%.

Since WWII, the president's party has lost an average of about 4 Senate seats in midterms. Across 22 midterms from 1934 to 2018, it gained Senate seats only 6 times.

A 2006 editorial counted 3 midterms since WWII in which the president's party lost the Senate: 1946, 1954 and 1986. This count is unverified and looks incomplete, since 1994 is not listed and 2006 came after the editorial. Adding those makes about 5 of the 20 midterms from 1946 to 2022.

raw_facts.source: Wikipedia (2026 United States Senate election in Alaska)
raw_facts.fact: The polling average the page cites, as of 2026-10-03, is Peltola 48.7% and Sullivan 45.8%. In polls that ran the ranked-choice rounds, Peltola wins the final round 52–48 (ASR, Sep 10–12) and 53–47 (AARP, Sep 8–11).
In a new Alaska Survey Research poll of likely voters, Peltola leads Sullivan 51% to 49% after the third round of ranked-choice tabulation.
The RealClearPolitics average has Peltola at 48.5% and Sullivan at 47.3%, a Peltola lead of about 1.2 points.

In the Aug 18, 2026 top-four primary, Peltola (D) won 82,244 votes (49.5%) and incumbent Dan S. Sullivan (R) won 68,726 (41.4%). Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. took 2.5%, David Leslie (D) 1.1% and Gerald Heikes (R) 1.1%. Leslie withdrew under pressure from Democratic leadership, so the November ballot is Peltola, Dan S. Sullivan, Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. and Heikes. The two minor candidates are both registered Republicans.

A same-name candidate, Dan J. Sullivan of Petersburg, will appear on the November ballot with no party label. Republicans accuse him of being a Democratic plant meant to draw votes away from the incumbent. In polls he takes about 1–7% of first choices.

Since mid-July, outside groups backing Sullivan have spent about $15.5–20 million on ads and groups backing Peltola about $15.4 million. The Senate Leadership Fund has spent more than $8 million and Trump's super PAC about $3.6 million since early September.

Peltola's campaign raised $6.9 million in Q2 2026 to Sullivan's $2 million, and raised a record of about $8.9 million in Q1. Sullivan had more cash on hand: $8.3 million versus her $6.1 million. Q3 reports are due in mid-October.

raw_facts.source: Nate Silver (FiveThirtyEight) via Goodreads blog repost; Washington Monthly
raw_facts.fact: A 2014 analysis found that Alaska polling misses have almost always overestimated Democrats. In 2014 Ivan Moore (ASR) had Begich ahead 48–42 in late October, but Sullivan won by about 2 points (48–46).

raw_facts.source: Alaska's News Source / NYT-Siena (result from recall, unverified)
raw_facts.fact: In 2020, NYT/Siena's October poll had Sullivan leading Al Gross 45–37. Sullivan won by roughly 12–13 points (about 53.9–41.2, recalled and unverified), so the polls understated him.

In 2024 Peltola lost the at-large House seat to Begich: 46.4% to 48.4% on first choices and 48.7% to 51.3% after ranked-choice tabulation. ASR's final 2024 presidential poll had Trump at 55–45, and Trump won Alaska by about 13.
Democrats have not won a U.S. Senate election in Alaska since 2008, when Begich won. Sullivan won the seat in 2014 and 2020.

The general election is November 3, 2026, under ranked-choice voting with four candidates. If no one has a majority of first choices, Alaska runs the ranked-choice tabulation after absentee ballots arrive, typically about two weeks after election day. That means calls by AP, Fox and NBC may come after the question closes on Nov 4.
The question resolves when AP, Fox News and NBC have all called the race for the same candidate; otherwise it resolves on official certification. The results include the ranked-choice rounds.

The latest release covers August 2026. Seasonally adjusted CPI-U rose 0.4% in August after 0.1% in July. Core rose 0.3%, energy 2.1% and gasoline 3.9% seasonally adjusted (2.5% not seasonally adjusted). CPI was up 3.4% over 12 months.

Seasonally adjusted monthly headline CPI in 2026, with gasoline's seasonally adjusted change in brackets: Feb 0.3 (0.8), Mar 0.9 (21.2), Apr 0.6 (5.4), May 0.5 (7.0), Jun -0.4 (-9.7), Jul 0.1 (-2.9), Aug 0.4 (3.9). Only 1 of these 7 months (March) came in above 0.6%; April was exactly 0.6.

Core CPI ran 0.2, 0.2, 0.4, 0.2, 0.0, 0.2 and 0.3 from February to August 2026. In April, a 5.4% gasoline rise plus 0.4% core produced a 0.6% headline. In May, a 7.0% gasoline rise plus 0.2% core produced 0.5%.

AAA said the national average for regular gasoline was $4.33 for September 2026, a record for September, 50 cents above the previous record of $3.83 set in 2023. The October 1 average was $4.41, down nearly 7 cents from the week before.

Citing EIA, LendingTree reported that regular gasoline averaged $4.36 a gallon in September 2026, up from $4.06 in August and $3.93 in July. That is about a 7.4% rise from August to September before seasonal adjustment.

AAA weekly national averages rose through September: $4.14 on Sep 3, $4.27 on Sep 10, $4.43 on Sep 17 and $4.48 on Sep 24, the highest ever for that time of year. AAA attributed the rise to volatility in the Strait of Hormuz and high crude prices.
EIA's weekly U.S. regular gasoline price was $4.071 for the week of Aug 31, $4.157 for Sep 7 and $4.319 for Sep 14, 2026. A third-party aggregator of EIA data put the week of Sep 28 at $4.47.

The resolution value is the seasonally adjusted monthly change in all-items CPI-U, published to one decimal. A value of 0.6% resolves No; at least 0.7% is needed for Yes.

The latest Channel 13 poll, published October 7, gives Netanyahu's bloc 55 of 120 seats, the Eisenkot-led Zionist opposition bloc 50 and the Arab parties about 15. Neither side reaches the 61 seats needed for a majority without the Arab parties.

The October 5 Channel 12 poll had Eisenkot's bloc at 54 seats, unchanged from the previous poll, and Netanyahu's bloc at 49. Ofer Winter's far-right People of Israel party again fell below the threshold, which is counted against Netanyahu's bloc. A poll-aggregator listing for October 5 shows Yashar 23 and Likud 21.

The Maariv/Lazar poll of October 2 projected Netanyahu's bloc at 51 seats, the opposition at 53 and the Arab parties at 12. It put Likud at 19, Otzma Yehudit at 9, Eisenkot's Yashar at 21 and Bennett's Together at 13.

The Jerusalem Post averaged five late-September polls (Channel 14, i24NEWS, Maariv, N12 and Channel 13). The averages were coalition bloc 54.6 seats, Zionist opposition 50.6 and Arab parties 12.4, with Likud at 23 and Yashar at 22.2. Individual polls varied widely: the coalition ranged from 49 seats (Maariv) to 63 for the right-wing bloc (Channel 14), and Likud ranged from 18 to 32.

A Times of Israel poll had Netanyahu's bloc at 51 seats and the opposition at a combined 55, after Winter's People of Israel party fell below the 3.25% threshold. Bloc totals in many polls depend on whether People of Israel and the Hendel–Zelekha Reservists/New Economic list cross the threshold.

Because the opposition refuses to rely on the Arab parties, a Channel 13 poll on September 30 put Netanyahu's bloc at 54 seats, two more than the opposition's Jewish parties. Yashar was the largest party at 21 seats and Likud had 19.

Eisenkot has said Yashar would work with junior partners such as RZP or Likud if Netanyahu is no longer prime minister. Benny Gantz has ruled out supporting a Netanyahu-led government and is pursuing a 'third bloc' that favors a unity government. Ra'am presents itself as a pragmatic partner seeking to replace the Netanyahu government, and five opposition leaders signed a pledge not to attack each other.

Eisenkot has said he would make no deals with the Arab parties. Netanyahu's campaign slogan is 'Eisenkot has no government without the Arab parties.' Gantz's Blue and White polled below the threshold, at 0.7% in one late-September Channel 12 poll.

Lists running include Together (Bennett 2026 plus Yesh Atid, headed by Bennett), the Joint List (Hadash, Ta'al and Balad), and Ra'am separately. Unity dropped out on September 4, and Hili Tropper joined Yashar. Surplus-vote pairings are Together with Yisrael Beiteinu, Yashar with the Democrats, the Joint List with Ra'am, and Likud with RZP–Zehut.

The election is on October 27, 2026, with diaspora voting on October 20. Surplus-vote agreements are due October 16, and official results are due to be confirmed on November 4. The 25th Knesset dissolved on July 17, 2026, after serving its full term.

The question resolves to the first person formally sworn in as prime minister after the 2026 election. A caretaker or interim prime minister does not count, so Netanyahu staying on as caretaker during a deadlock would not count. If nobody is sworn in by December 31, 2027, it resolves 'Other'. The forming government needs Knesset confidence, which in practice means 61 of 120 seats or abstentions.

In November 2022, final pre-election polls put Netanyahu's bloc at about 59–60 seats and exit polls at 61–62, but the official count gave it 64. Part of the gap came from about 290,000 votes for Meretz and Balad that were wasted when both fell below the threshold, and from higher turnout in right-leaning cities.

Unverified, from memory: of the 5 elections from April 2019 to November 2022, 2 (April and September 2019) produced no government and led to repeat elections. After March 2020 Netanyahu was sworn in on May 17, 2020; after March 2021 Bennett was sworn in on June 13, 2021; and after November 2022 Netanyahu was sworn in on December 29, 2022.

At its September 15-16, 2026 meeting the FOMC voted 12-0 to raise the federal funds target range by 25 bps to 3.75%-4.00%, its first increase since 2023. This is the level the October change will be measured from (upper bound 4.00%).

The September minutes, released October 7, said 'most participants assessed that another increase in the target range for the federal funds rate would likely be appropriate by year end,' but gave no indication of timing. They added that decisions depend on incoming information. The remaining 2026 decisions are October 28 and December 9.

New York Fed President and FOMC Vice Chair John Williams said there is no urgency in deciding when to raise rates again, and Fed Vice Chair Philip Jefferson echoed that view. Reuters reported that investors who had expected hikes in both October and December changed their view after these comments, and that the Fed now seems set to hold in October.

Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan believes at least two more quarter-point hikes will be needed to control inflation. Chair Kevin Warsh has not spoken publicly since his September 16 press conference, in line with his pledge to give less policy guidance.

September payrolls rose by only 29,000, against a Dow Jones consensus of 84,000. Unemployment rose to 4.2% from 4.1%. Revisions cut July/August by a combined 60,000 (July is now -10,000), and average hourly earnings rose 0.1% m/m and 3% y/y.
In the September Summary of Economic Projections, 16 of 18 participants projected one more rate hike in 2026, without saying at which meeting. Warsh did not submit a projection.

Fed staff estimated PCE inflation at 3.8% y/y for August. Reuters noted that August inflation rose less than expected. The minutes said some participants saw the September hike as a risk-management 'insurance' move, while others saw it as necessary to curb inflation.
At the July 2026 meeting the Fed held rates, and three FOMC members dissented in favor of a quarter-point hike.
September 2026 CPI is scheduled for October 14, 2026 at 8:30 a.m. ET. This is the main inflation release before the October 27-28 FOMC meeting, and the Fed can also estimate September PCE from it.

The FOMC meets October 27-28, 2026, with the statement due at 2:00 p.m. ET on October 28, less than a week before the U.S. midterm congressional elections. The next meeting after that is December 8-9.
Coverage of the minutes reported that after the weak September jobs data, investors were positioned for the Fed to keep rates unchanged at the October 27-28 meeting.

Since the 1994 shock tightening, the Fed has generally prepared markets before acting rather than surprising them. Unverified: no cited count was found of FOMC decisions that went against market expectations on the eve of the meeting.

On September 2, 2026 the Bank of Canada held its target for the overnight rate at 2.25%, with the Bank Rate at 2.5% and the deposit rate at 2.20%. Coverage of the decision said the upside risks to inflation had increased and that the Bank is prepared to adjust policy as needed.
The September 2, 2026 hold was the Bank of Canada's seventh straight decision with no change. The policy rate has been 2.25% since the October 29, 2025 cut.

The summary of Governing Council deliberations for September 2 says the economy and inflation evolved broadly in line with the July forecast and the economy is still in excess supply. Members agreed that if higher energy prices spread to other CPI components, this 'could require a monetary policy response'. The summary does not say a hike was seriously considered. The date shown is approximate; these summaries are usually published about two weeks after the decision.

In a September 21 speech, Governor Tiff Macklem said a hike is possible if inflation proves persistent but made no commitment. He said the Bank doesn't want to restrain growth unnecessarily if inflation pressures are contained, nor wait too long if they become persistent.

Headline CPI rose 3.0% year over year in August 2026, the same as in July. Excluding gasoline it was 2.4%, up from 2.2%. The Bank's preferred core measures averaged 2.0%: CPI-trim 1.9% and CPI-median 2.0%.

TD noted that the 2-year Government of Canada yield had risen more than 40 bp over the previous month as markets moved toward rate hikes. TD said the August CPI report did not support that degree of tightening.
Real GDP was essentially unchanged in July 2026. June growth was revised up to 0.4% from 0.3%. Second-quarter growth had come in stronger than expected.
Canada lost 41,700 jobs in August 2026 and the unemployment rate held at 6.4%. U.S. Section 338 tariffs took effect August 22.

Capital Economics' base case is no hike in October, though it calls the decision close. It forecasts two quarter-point hikes starting in 2027. Two other economists quoted by BNN Bloomberg expect the Bank to hold for the rest of 2026 and hike in Q1 2027.

Senior Deputy Governor Carolyn Rogers said the policy rate is too blunt a tool for housing affordability. According to The Hub, the Bank so far sees little sign that higher gasoline prices are spreading across the wider consumer basket. Economists expect any tightening to be capped at about 50 bp.

After the September decision, both TD Economics and RBC said they expect the Bank of Canada to hold at 2.25% for the rest of 2026. RBC's Claire Fan said oil prices are the main factor behind market pricing of the October meeting.

Unverified, recalled count: the Bank of Canada's last few tightening cycles began with 25 bp hikes (June 2010, July 2017, March 2022). Each followed explicit hawkish guidance in the preceding statements. The September 2026 statement said the Bank is 'prepared to adjust monetary policy as needed'.

At its September 15–16, 2026 meeting the Fed raised the federal funds target range by 25 basis points to 3.75%–4.00%, on a 12–0 vote. It was the Fed's first increase since 2023. The upper bound is now exactly 4.00%, so a Yes requires another hike on October 28.

Bab el-Mandeb had 290 transits by cargo vessels over 10,000 dwt in 21–27 September (preliminary), up from 264 the week before. The four-week average was 280 a week, against 316 in June and 257 in January. This is Lloyd's own monitor, not PortWatch.

Lloyd's says the Houthi blockade on Saudi Arabia has dampened traffic growth but their threats have not stopped ships returning to the Red Sea. Owners are carrying out plans to return to the route. The EU says ships are queuing for Operation Aspides escorts because there are too few warships.
Windward counted 23 inbound and 19 outbound Bab el-Mandeb crossings on 4 October 2026, up from 18 inbound and 13 outbound on 3 October.

Unverified: a commenter who said they checked PortWatch's chokepoint dataset reported that the Bab el-Mandeb 7-day moving average had never fallen below 20, on 0 of 953 days since January 2024. The market description gives the 7-day average on 16 August 2026 as 29, and says the strait historically handled 60–80 transits a day.
Clarksons said Bab el-Mandeb transits averaged 31 a day over 25–26 July 2026, right after the Houthi blockade on Saudi shipping was declared. That was about a 50% fall from the second quarter.

In September the Houthis seized Mocha and Perim Island (11 Sept). In late September and early October, Saudi-backed Yemeni forces counterattacked, said they had retaken Mocha, and said they had secured the strait. The Houthi blockade declared in July targets Saudi shipping and exempts non-Saudi vessels. Trump said in late September that the Houthis are letting most ships pass.
On 4 October 2026 a tanker, reportedly the Chrystal Sky, reported multiple explosions about 60 nm south of Mokha. It was undamaged and continued its voyage, and no one claimed the attack.
Fighting near the Bab el-Mandeb continues. The Saudi-backed government says it has retaken Mocha and other territory near the strait, and the Houthis deny losing ground.

The Houthis reportedly took control of Yemen's Red Sea coast and Perim Island at the narrowest point of the strait. The strait has become more important to Saudi exports because the US–Iran war has disrupted the Strait of Hormuz.

JMIC rates the threat in the Bab el-Mandeb and southern Red Sea as SUBSTANTIAL, and says Al-Mokha port is closed after more than 25 missile impacts. In August a cargo ship hit about 40 nm southeast of Al Mukha was declared a constructive total loss.

PortWatch counts transit calls from satellite AIS data and covers all vessel types. Its daily counts are higher than the Lloyd's List figures, which only include cargo ships over 10,000 dwt. The question resolves Yes only if the published 7-day average is 10 or less on some date before 31 October.

Lloyd's Red Sea Brief is moving to every other week, so the next issue is due around 15 October 2026. The question covers data through 31 October, and the resolution allows 14 days after that for PortWatch to publish.

Post-election reviews found that first-round polls underestimated Flávio Bolsonaro. According to Bahia Notícias, only 4 of 11 polling firms had Flávio winning the first round. Final Datafolha valid-vote numbers were Lula 45%, Flávio 42%, and AtlasIntel (27 Sep–2 Oct) had Lula 47.0%, Flávio 44.1%. The actual result was Flávio 47.03%, Lula 45.16%.

Euro-area flash HICP inflation rose to 3.8% in September 2026 from 3.2% in August, a three-year high, above the 3.6% Reuters poll. Energy inflation was 18.8% (up from 14.3%), and core inflation edged up to 2.5% from 2.4%.

On 28 September Lagarde said a 'measured' policy response is still appropriate and that oil and gas prices from the US-Iran conflict are the main driver of inflation: 'We see higher inflation ahead but no signs yet that it is becoming embedded.' She pushed back on aggressive market bets.

Bundesbank President Nagel said inflation risks are tilted to the upside but there are no clear signs of second-round effects, noting an absence of 'inflation feeding through to price and wage setting'. The outlet reported this as leaving room for an October pause, with December kept in play.

Slovenia's Primož Dolenc said persistently high inflation and unresolved conflicts support 'moving policy rates towards a more restrictive territory', but that 'when and by how much we will determine on a meeting-by-meeting basis'.

Reuters reported that markets read the ECB's 'measured' language as hikes spaced out and possibly timed with the quarterly projections. It also said financial-stability concerns (rising borrowing costs, wider French debt spreads) may weigh on the next decision.

In early October, financial-market stress led markets to scale back expected ECB rate hikes. ECB chief economist Lane has argued that 'demand destruction' from energy costs and higher long-term rates could limit how far rates need to rise.

Greek central bank governor Stournaras said an October move cannot be ruled out if energy costs or inflation surge, but warned against acting hastily. Schnabel has recently said higher bond yields could dampen price pressures.
Eurostat releases the full September 2026 HICP data on 16 October 2026, before the 28–29 October meeting. The October flash estimate comes after the meeting.

raw_facts.source: Wikipedia – Opinion polling for the 2026 Serbian parliamentary election
raw_facts.fact: The page lists 7 regular polls in 2026. Faktor Plus has the SNS-led list ahead in all four of its polls: 46.4% vs 28.7% (30 Apr), 47.1% vs 30.7% (26 Jun), 47.2% vs 31.5% (4 Sep) and 48.6% vs 37.1% (21 Sep). The other three, from CRTA and NSPM, put the Student List ahead: 44.9% vs 35.7% (CRTA, 15 Jul), 39.6% vs 37.5% (NSPM, 30 Jul) and 44.4% vs 41.7% (NSPM, published 30 Sep, fieldwork early Sept).

In the Faktor Plus poll fielded 16–20 Sep 2026 (n=986), the Vučić-led list was at 48.6% and the Student List at 37.1%, a gain of 5.6 points for the Student List since the previous poll. balk.hu describes Faktor Plus as close to the ruling SNS, and its director denies any manipulation.

raw_facts.source: Wikipedia – Opinion polling for the 2026 Serbian parliamentary election
raw_facts.fact: Opposition and independent media accuse Ipsos and Faktor Plus of pro-government bias. A Bureau for Social Research study found that most Serbian pollsters do not disclose weighting or funding. CRTA's July poll left out 12.2% undecided, and an April NSPM scenario poll left out 21% undecided.

RIK accepted 18 lists and 1 was withdrawn. List #1 is 'Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia' (SNS, PUPS, SRS, ZS and others; 209,130 signatures). List #3 is 'Student List – Students Are Winning', headed by Ilija Srdanović (69,099 signatures). SPS–JS (Dačić) is running separately as list #2.

Vučić resigned as president on 27 Sep 2026 to lead the SNS list as its prime ministerial candidate. The snap election was announced on 8–9 Sep and set for 25 Oct, more than a year before the regular vote due in late 2027.

Several opposition groups consolidated behind the Student List. The People's Serbia coalition (NPS, NLS, EU) withdrew its list on 22 Sep to back it, after NLS and EU had endorsed it on 15 Sep. PSG left the PES coalition in late September to support the Student List. PES (SSP/SRCE, Tepić/Ponoš) is still running separately as list #9 but has said it will cooperate with the Student List.

In late September, pro-government tabloids ran campaigns against Student List leader Srdanović, which fact-checkers said used AI-manipulated photos. Televised debates are scheduled on RTS, N1, Nova and Radio Belgrade from 29 Sep to 8 Oct.

Vreme reports that polls are dominated by two blocs, 'Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia' and the Student List. A September NSPM survey suggested that Dačić's SPS may struggle to clear the 3% threshold.

The CRTA / Stanford Democracy Action Lab survey (June fieldwork, n=2,324) put the Student List at 44.9% and SNS at 35.7% among decided voters. It was the first published poll to show the Student List ahead.
No Ipsos, CRTA or other poll fielded in October 2026 turned up. The most recent published polls are Faktor Plus (21 Sep) and NSPM (30 Sep, fieldwork early September).

In the December 2023 snap election, preliminary results gave the SNS list 47.95% and Serbia Against Violence 24.32%, with SPS at 6.75%. Ipsos/CeSID exit polls (about 47% vs 23%) were close to the count. Unverified recollection: an SNS-led list has won the most seats in every parliamentary election since 2012 (2012, 2014, 2016, 2020, 2022, 2023), 6 of 6.

CRTA observers said irregularities in the 2023 vote (bussed-in voters, identity documents issued for non-residents, family voting) may have affected the outcome, especially in Belgrade. Turnout was 59.1%.

All 250 seats are elected by nationwide proportional representation with a 3% threshold. Minority lists, including #4, 5, 6, 10, 14, 15, 17 and 18, are exempt from the threshold. The question resolves on seats won by the ballot-named list, with ties broken by votes.
Election day is 25 Oct 2026, the same day the question closes. RIK (rik.parlament.gov.rs) publishes the preliminary and final results.

raw_facts.source: Desk calculation from Rotten Tomatoes figures
raw_facts.fact: Assuming standard rounding, 61% of 88 reviews means 54 fresh and 34 rotten (54/88 = 61.4%; 53/88 would show 60%). The resolution page reads a 59% Tomatometer from 104 reviews. No verified audience score is posted yet, and the page lists the theatrical release as October 9, 2026. 59% of 104 works out to about 61 fresh and 43 rotten, since 61/104 = 58.7%.

From about 61 fresh out of 104, six rotten reviews in a row would take the score to 55% (61/110), which is not above 55. For the 60 strike, the displayed score must reach 61%: five fresh reviews in a row would give 66/109 = 60.6%. Across 200 total reviews, the score needs at least 112 fresh to show 56%+ and roughly 121 fresh to show 61%. That means about 51 of the next 96 new reviews (53%) for the first case and about 60 of 96 (62.5%) for the second.
Shortly after the review embargo lifted, the film stood at 70% with 42 reviews counted and an average rating of 6.4/10. Its Metacritic score was 52/100.
In a separate early reading, the film had a 67% Tomatometer from 39 reviews.
On October 7, the film held 70% from 60 reviews. Critics were reported as saying it looks flat and lacks energy.
A later reading put it at 63% fresh from 73 reviews, down from the 67–70% readings at 39–60 reviews earlier that day.

raw_facts.source: Derived from dated readings (Dark Horizons, Yahoo, Rotten Tomatoes)
raw_facts.fact: The score has been falling: 70% (42 reviews), then 63% (73), then 59% (104). Reviews added between 42 and 104 were about 52% fresh (roughly 32 of 62). Those added between 73 and 104 were about 48% fresh (roughly 15 of 31).
Showbiz411 reported that the film opened at 68% on Rotten Tomatoes. ScreenPulse had logged 69% at 13:09 UTC on Oct 7, and Film Updates logged 70% at 14:50 UTC.
At that point the score made the film Aaron Sorkin's third-lowest on Rotten Tomatoes among the films he has worked on. The Social Network holds 96%.

Top-outlet reviews are mixed to positive. Peter Bradshaw (Guardian) gave it 3/5, David Rooney (THR) called it 'sharp entertainment' and Nikki Baughan (Screen International) called it 'incisive'. Several U.S. officials briefed on the investigation and a former Israeli security official said early signs are that the co-pilot acted alone, not for a larger organization or a foreign government. A senior U.S. official briefed on Israel's investigation said there were no signs that Iran directed or took part in the attack. Officials stressed the investigation is still at an early stage.
Headline: 'Co-pilot accused of trying to hijack Flydubai plane probably acted alone, Israeli sources say.' Only the headline was available to us, not the article text.
Israeli sources told CBS that an early Israeli investigation suggests the co-pilot was probably not directed by a terrorist group or a nation and that this was likely a lone-wolf attack.

raw_facts.source: Al Jazeera / CBS News (via search summary)
raw_facts.fact: In a written statement, Netanyahu said the attacker 'underwent Islamist radicalization' and 'came to crash the plane with its passengers', adding: 'We are investigating whether he was dispatched, and whoever sent him will pay a very heavy price.' The statement did not name Iran. The quote comes from search-result summaries; we could not see which page carried the original text.

Netanyahu said it was too early to say whether Iran was involved and that he did not yet have information to attribute the incident to Tehran. He said Israel would join the probe and that this would be settled 'one way or another in a matter of days'.

On Fox News, Netanyahu said 'We know that he underwent Islamist radical indoctrination', citing personal information gathered during questioning. He also said the co-pilot was suicidal. He did not attribute the attack to Iran.

While admitting it was too early to establish a motive, Netanyahu pointed generally to Iran and its proxies as intent on stepping up attacks on Israelis abroad. Al Jazeera framed this as security messaging ahead of an Israeli election. We did not confirm the election date.

Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz called the incident 'an attempted jihadist terror attack' and called the co-pilot a 'terrorist'. He did not attribute it to Iran or any named group. Our sourcing for this quote is a search summary, so treat the exact page as unconfirmed.

raw_facts.source: South China Morning Post / Outlook India
raw_facts.fact: Asked whether he had been briefed on links between the co-pilot and Tehran, Trump said: 'I would say the answer, based on what I'm hearing, is yes, but we're working on it right now.' He vowed to hit Iran 'very hard' if it was involved. Outlook India later reported he said he 'personally' believed Iran was behind it. VP JD Vance said there was 'nothing conclusive'. These are U.S. statements, not Israeli ones, so they do not count toward resolution.

AP sources named the co-pilot as Omani national Hamam al-Hammami, who had been barred from flying by Omani authorities over extremism concerns. The UAE Attorney General called the attack a 'terrorist act' with a crash axe. Abu Dhabi leads the investigation and has not publicly given a motive or said whether he acted alone.

Reports say a joint UAE-Israel investigation is looking at the co-pilot's radicalisation in Syria and a possible link to an Iranian-backed terrorist group. AP reported that investigators had found no connection to a militant group so far.

Citing Channel 12 and Israel Hayom, NPR and Fox reported that the co-pilot told investigators he meant to crash the plane into Ben Gurion Airport. An Israeli investigative team has joined the UAE investigation.

The investigation is ongoing and final results on whether an organization or state was behind the attack are still pending. The UAE leads the probe, and an Israeli team is taking part. No date for findings has been announced.

The market resolves Yes only if the Israeli government (statements by the PM or a cabinet minister count) explicitly says Iran or a listed proxy ordered, carried out, planned, or directly aided or coordinated the incident. Statements about inspiration or 'Islamist indoctrination' alone do not qualify.

The Oct 9 00:00 UTC hourly candle (still open) showed open 109.62, high 109.69, low 109.25, last 109.42. The previous hour (Oct 8 23:00 UTC) went from 110.34 to 109.62, after SOL traded above 110 from 21:00 to 23:00 UTC (high 110.87, 21:00 close 110.65).

Binance daily candles: Oct 8 opened 116.30, high 116.81, low 105.71, close 109.62 (-5.7%, a range of about 9.6%). Oct 7 opened 120.70 and closed 116.30 (low 115.26).

Daily high-low ranges from Sep 25 to Oct 7 were mostly about 1.3%–6% (for example Oct 3: 118.52–120.09; Oct 2: 117.11–123.76), then widened to about 9.6% on Oct 8. Recent hourly candles often moved 0.5%–1% or more, which is about the size of the current gap to the strike.

On Truth Social on October 8, Trump said the US would not attack Iran before the November 3 midterms, citing 'productive discussions' with Tehran. Search summaries of the coverage report he also said the blockade 'will remain in full force and effect'; the full articles could not be opened to confirm the exact wording.

On October 5, CENTCOM said it had redirected 130 ships since enforcement resumed on July 14 and had disabled 3 vessels and destroyed 13 over 12 weeks. Vice Adm. Brad Cooper said the mission continues.

Coverage summarized in search results says Treasury sanctioned 17 more vessels and said this effectively neutralizes most of Iran's remaining shadow fleet. A White House official said Trump has all options available. Earlier reports said the White House had told the Pentagon to prepare strikes before the election.

Iran's parliament speaker Ghalibaf said the Strait of Hormuz will not reopen until seven conditions based on the Islamabad memorandum are met. The report says the UN-sidelines talks produced no breakthrough, and a Tehran source said Iran's assessment is that the war is resuming.

Trump said he rejected Iran's proposal from indirect talks in New York (Witkoff and Kushner with FM Araghchi, with Qatar mediating). Iran had offered to reopen Hormuz and resume nuclear talks within a week if the US lifted the blockade, removed oil sanctions and restored a region-wide ceasefire.
Trump told Axios he expected more negotiations that week. Gaps remained wide: Iran wants talks focused on Hormuz and the blockade, while the US wants nuclear concessions.

Iranian hardliners filed a request in parliament to impeach FM Araghchi after his New York meetings with Witkoff. They reportedly objected that the talks were not coordinated with the Supreme National Security Council.

The first phase of the blockade ran from April 13 to June 18, 2026, about 9.5 weeks. CENTCOM announced its end on X along with a 60-day US–Iran memorandum of understanding. This is the one previous official lifting.

In early August, Axios reported the US was close to a Hormuz deal (a 60-day Oman–Iran arrangement) and was aiming to announce it that Wednesday. No lifting of the blockade followed; it remained in force through August and September.

raw_facts.source: Wikipedia (2026 United States naval blockade of Iran)
raw_facts.fact: Trump announced the reinstatement on July 13, and enforcement began July 14. In the timeline through mid-September there was no announcement of lifting. Iran's central bank governor said on August 19 that oil exports had effectively ceased, and redirected vessels passed 100 by September 12.
During the first phase, Trump repeatedly said the blockade would stay until an agreement was signed. In that phase, the lifting came only with a signed MOU, announced by CENTCOM.
The US midterm elections are on November 3, 2026, after both question deadlines (October 15 and October 31). No date has been publicly set for the next US–Iran negotiating round.

On release day, The Social Reckoning's Rotten Tomatoes page shows a Tomatometer of 60% from 131 reviews. A score of exactly 60 counts as No under the 'Above 60' rule. The Popcornmeter has fewer than 50 verified ratings, so no audience score is shown.
The film opened in theaters on October 9, 2026, so the market settles Monday, October 12, 2026, at 10:00 AM ET. The Tomatometer must be strictly above 60, so it needs to show 61% or more.

raw_facts.source: Desk arithmetic from Rotten Tomatoes figures
raw_facts.fact: 60% of 131 reviews is about 78–79 positive and 52–53 negative. If the split is 79/52 (60.3%), one or two more positive reviews with no new negatives would lift it to about 60.6%, which shows as 61%. Each new negative review pulls the score toward 59%, below Fresh. This depends on Rotten Tomatoes' rounding method, which is unverified.
Kalshi News reported the film at 61% with critics on Rotten Tomatoes as of Thursday afternoon, October 8.
Collider, writing at 8:15 PM EDT on October 8, reported a 60% critics' score but did not give a review count. Its own review rated the film 7/10 and called it a 'downgrade' from The Social Network.
Around the review embargo lift on October 7, outlets reported 67% from 39 reviews, 70% from 43 reviews and 70% from 60 reviews. The score has since slid to 60% as the count grew to 131.
Showbiz411 reported the film opening at 68% on Rotten Tomatoes on October 7.
An early report put the film at 52/100 on Metacritic, weaker than its Rotten Tomatoes score. Critics generally praised Sorkin's script and the cast but faulted the direction.

Recent reviews on the page are mixed. The Daily Telegraph gave it 2/5, calling it a 'doggedly conventional and old-fashioned journalistic procedural', while the Irish Times gave it 3/5 and called the script 'lively'.
Screen Rant reported the score makes The Social Reckoning Aaron Sorkin's third-lowest-rated film on Rotten Tomatoes. The 2010 film The Social Network holds a Certified Fresh 96%.

BEA plans to release the advance estimate of Q3 2026 GDP on Thursday, October 29, 2026, at 8:30 AM ET. This is the release that settles the market, and the market closes at 8:29 AM that day.

BEA's third estimate put Q2 2026 real GDP growth at a 2.2% annual rate, revised up 0.7 points from the 1.5% second estimate. Higher investment, consumer spending and government spending drove the revision. Q1 2026 was revised to 2.5%.

The August 2026 goods and services trade deficit widened to $105.6 billion, from a revised $92.8 billion in July. That is the largest gap since March 2025, and consensus had been $102.0 billion. Imports rose $17.2 billion to a record $420.8 billion, while exports rose $4.5 billion to $315.2 billion.

Capital goods imports hit a record $146.4 billion in August, up 57.9% from a year earlier, led by semiconductors and aircraft. About two-thirds of the rise in industrial supplies imports came from crude oil and nonmonetary gold. The three-month average deficit through August was $89.9 billion.

August 2026 retail sales rose 1.2% month over month to $773.9 billion, against an expected rise of about 0.8%, and were up 6.0% year over year. Sales excluding autos rose 1.4%. TD estimated real sales rose 0.8% and said real Q3 consumer spending was running at about a 3% annualized pace.

BEA reported that August 2026 personal consumption expenditures rose 0.9% and personal income rose 0.2%. The saving rate was 4.1%, and July PCE was shown at +0.1%. The date is approximate: these are figures from the late-September personal income release.

September 2026 nonfarm payrolls rose 29,000, against a forecast of 84,000, and unemployment rose to 4.2%. July was revised to -10,000 and August to +133,000, a combined downward revision of 60,000. Wages were up 3.0% year over year.

In 2025, a government shutdown cancelled the scheduled October 30 Q3 advance release. The first Q3 2025 estimate (4.3%) did not come out until December 23, 2025. This shows the release date can slip. As of October 2, 2026, no shutdown delays to federal data releases had been reported.
Recent first prints: Q3 2025 was first reported at 4.3%, later revised to 4.4%. The Q4 2025 advance estimate was 1.4% (second estimate 0.7%). Q1 and Q2 2026 currently stand at 2.5% and 2.2%.

A 2018 commentary counted 6 of 50 quarters from 2005 to 2018 with growth above 4%. UNVERIFIED, recalled from memory: since 2010, roughly 7 of about 66 advance estimates were above 4.0% (2018Q2 4.1, 2020Q3, 2021Q1, 2021Q2, 2021Q4, 2023Q3 4.9, 2025Q3 4.3). Forum Research polled on Oct. 6, just after Chris Alexander suspended his campaign. Among decided and leaning voters it had Olivia Chow at 46% and Brad Bradford at 42%. Chow led by 11 points in Forum's Sept. 25 poll.
Nanos surveyed 755 Toronto residents from Sept. 30 to Oct. 4, before Alexander withdrew. Among decided voters Chow had 52.4% and Bradford 42.6%. 22% of all respondents said they were undecided.
A Liaison Strategies poll released Oct. 6, before Alexander dropped out, had Chow at 48%, Bradford at 40% and Alexander at 9%. No other candidate had broken through.

Mainstreet's early-October poll had Chow at 38.1%, Bradford at 32.2% and Alexander at 7.2%. Head-to-head, Chow led Bradford 47% to 41%, with 12% undecided. Mainstreet's previous survey was fielded Sept. 14–17.

Former MP Chris Alexander, polling third at about 7–9%, dropped out on Oct. 6, the first day of advance voting. He endorsed no candidate. Bradford invited Alexander's supporters to treat his campaign as their 'home.'
The official withdrawal deadline was Aug. 21, so Alexander's name stays on the Oct. 26 ballot. Analysts warned that some voters may not know he has withdrawn.

Political scientist Myer Siemiatycki said Alexander's supporters are 'up for grabs' and noted that polling shows many Torontonians view Bradford unfavourably. Liaison's David Valentin said Alexander's supporters cannot simply be counted as votes for Bradford or Chow.

On Oct. 6 Chow and Bradford held their fourth debate together, the first head-to-head one, at Toronto Metropolitan University. Chow attacked Bradford's past positions on fare increases and bike lanes. Bradford attacked her record on her pledge of 65,000 rental homes and called her 'fearmongering.' A CBC Toronto debate also covered finances and public safety.
Bradford proposed ending the practice of setting money aside for future capital projects and instead paying for infrastructure over decades by taking on debt. Chow called the plan 'reckless.'
As of Oct. 8, no new endorsements in the mayoral race had been reported. Searches turned up no 2026 endorsement from Premier Doug Ford.

Advance voting opened Oct. 6, and election day is Oct. 26, 2026. Chow, who won the 2023 by-election, is running for her first full term. Bradford, the Ward 19 Beaches–East York councillor, is not seeking re-election to council.

In the 2023 by-election Chow won with 37.2% to Ana Bailão's 32.5%. Mainstreet's final poll had Chow at 36% and Bailão at 30%. Earlier Ipsos and Viewpoints polls had Bailão near 12%, and her late surge came after an endorsement from John Tory. About 21.7% of votes were cast in advance or by mail.

Unverified, recalled from memory: since Toronto's 1997 amalgamation, every incumbent mayor who ran for re-election has won (Lastman 2000, Miller 2006, Tory 2018 and 2022, so 4 of 4). Rob Ford did not run in 2014.
Bradford finished eighth in the June 2023 mayoral by-election that Chow won. 2026 is his second run for mayor.

raw_facts.fact: The general election candidates are incumbent Republican Roger Marshall, Democrat Adam Hamilton (pastor and founder of the Church of the Resurrection) and Libertarian David C. Graham. The page lists these polling averages: 270toWin Marshall +0.2, RealClearPolitics Marshall +0.2, Decision Desk HQ Hamilton +0.9, FiftyPlusOne Hamilton +1.1, and Silver Bulletin Hamilton +1.4. Their combined average is Hamilton 46.0%, Marshall 45.4%.

A YouGov poll of 2,252 likely voters (Sep 24–Oct 4) has Hamilton 48%, Marshall 45%, with a margin of error of ±3.2 points. Two other recent polls show a tie: NYT/Siena (Sep 22–30) at 45–45, and Trafalgar Group (R) (Sep 29–Oct 1) at 44–44.
An Emerson/Nexstar poll (Sep 15–16) had Hamilton 45%, Marshall 43%, Libertarian Graham 4% and 8% undecided. Wedgewood (Sep 22–24) had Hamilton 50–48. Co/efficient (R) (Sep 8–10) had Marshall 49–44.

A GBAO poll released by the Hamilton campaign on Oct 7 shows Hamilton 49%, Marshall 44% head-to-head, and Hamilton 46%, Marshall 41% with Graham included. In the same poll, 42% said recent information made them less favorable toward Marshall, versus 15% more favorable.

On Sept 8, a New York Times investigation reported that Marshall, a former ob-gyn, sued more than 700 patients over unpaid medical bills, and dozens were arrested. Hamilton and outside groups are airing ads about it. Marshall's lawyers sent a cease-and-desist letter calling the ads defamatory.

A group tied to Senate Majority Leader John Thune is spending $14 million on ads in Kansas, partly shifted from North Carolina. Another GOP-aligned super PAC committed nearly $2 million. AdImpact reports the Senate Leadership Fund reserved about $8.2 million to support Marshall.

FOX4 reports that several polls, including its own from September, show Hamilton narrowly ahead but within the margin of error. The Marshall campaign launched an attack ad against Hamilton the weekend before Oct 7, and Hamilton's campaign disputes its claims.

In 2020, the final Kansas Senate polling average showed Marshall 44.5%, Bollier 42.5% (about R+2). NYT/Siena had Marshall +4 and PPP had a tie. Marshall won 53.2% to 41.8% (R+11.4), outperforming his polls by about 9 points.

In 2014, late polls averaged roughly a tie between independent Greg Orman and Sen. Pat Roberts (R), with Orman +0.2 per Insight Kansas as of Oct 23. Roberts won 53.15% to 42.53% (R+10.6). In both 2014 and 2020, the Republican beat the final polls by about 9–10 points.
Kansas has not elected a Democrat to the U.S. Senate since 1932. Republicans have held both seats since Sen. George McGill (D) left office in January 1939, a run of about 86 years.

After results are certified, the president has 7 days for consultations, then gives one MK 28 days to form a government, extendable by up to 14 days. If that fails, the mandate can go to another MK or to the Knesset (which needs 61 MKs backing one candidate), or new elections are triggered.

Jackson led or tied Collins in every listed poll from mid-July to mid-September. Examples: UNH Jul 15–20, Jackson 49–46. Hart (D), Jackson 49–45. UMass/YouGov Aug 28–Sep 14, Jackson 48–43. Rasmussen (R), Sep 8–10, Jackson 46–45. Exceptions: the Abacus registered-voter version had Collins 46–45, and Quantus (Sep 14–15) had Collins 48–47.

In 2020, Democrat Sara Gideon led nearly every public poll and finished 6.5 points ahead in the RealClearPolitics average. Collins still won with just under 51% of the vote, a margin of roughly 8–9 points (about 8.6 by recollection, not verified from the sources). That puts the polling miss at about 15 points in Collins's favor.
Unverified recollection: Collins has won all 5 of her Senate general elections (1996, 2002, 2008, 2014, 2020).
Second debate (WMTW, Oct 8) was testy. Jackson accused Collins and her husband of profiting from the Iran war, without offering specific evidence. The two candidates accused each other of corruption.

First debate (WGME, Oct 6): Jackson tied Collins to Trump and her Kavanaugh vote. Collins said she is 'not exactly' Trump's favorite senator and argued that she is the only pro-choice candidate on the stage.

About a week before Oct 8, ProPublica reported that the FBI sought to investigate bribery claims involving Collins, tied to $150,000 that convicted contractor Martin Kao says he routed to a pro-Collins super PAC. ProPublica says the probe was dropped after Trump returned to office. Collins's campaign calls the allegations recycled and says she was cleared. Jackson called it 'corruption of the highest order.'
As of June 30, 2026, Collins had raised $18.9M and had $11.0M cash on hand. Jackson was not yet a candidate then and shows $0. Trump has not endorsed Collins.
Two more debates are scheduled: Oct 13 (WABI/WAGM) and Oct 15 (News Center Maine/Portland Press Herald/Maine Public). Election day is November 3, 2026.

Maine uses ranked-choice voting for U.S. Senate races. The question resolves once AP, Fox News and NBC all call the race for the same candidate, and otherwise on official certification. Jackson, as the replacement Democratic nominee, counts as the Democrat.

When checked, the official Sprint Qualifying results page showed no results. The sprint-qualifying session was scheduled for Friday, Oct 9 at 20:30 local time. The sprint-qualifying result sets the Sprint grid only, not the Grand Prix grid.

Verstappen won the rain-hit, relocated 'Bahrain GP in Malaysia' at Sepang on Oct 4, 2026. It was his and Red Bull's first win of 2026 and his 72nd career win. Antonelli was 2nd (+2.307s) and Hamilton 3rd (+4.919s). Russell retired late with a power unit failure.
Russell won the Azerbaijan GP and Verstappen finished 2nd, with Hadjar 3rd. Forbes says this was Red Bull's first double podium since China 2024.

After the Sepang race, Antonelli led the championship by 84 points over Russell. The table after Baku had been Antonelli 302, Russell 236, Hamilton 199, Norris 186, Leclerc 179 and Verstappen 163 (6th).

Mercedes has dominated 2026: Russell won Australia and Azerbaijan, and Antonelli won China, Japan and Belgium among others. Norris won Hungary. Verstappen's only 2026 win so far is Sepang on Oct 4. I could not verify the full count of race winners for the season.

Verstappen has never won the Singapore GP. He finished 2nd there in 2025 behind Russell (Mercedes), who won from pole. Verstappen says the Red Bull is better at low speed now but still struggles over bumps and kerbs.

Singapore is a Sprint weekend for the first time: one practice session and Sprint Qualifying on Friday Oct 9, then the Sprint and Grand Prix qualifying on Saturday Oct 10, and the Grand Prix on Sunday Oct 11. It is the sixth and final sprint of 2026.

The question resolves on the driver listed first in the FIA Final Classification of the Sunday Grand Prix, including time penalties. Changes after publication don't count, and a Sprint win does not count.

The question resolves Yes only if Alabama wins by 2 or more points. A 1-point Alabama win, a tie or a Georgia win all resolve No. If the game doesn't start within 48 hours of its scheduled time, it resolves to a fair price.

The Senate is currently 53 Republicans and 47 Democrats (45 Democrats plus 2 independents who caucus with them). 35 seats are up in 2026, including special elections in Florida and Ohio, and 65 are not up.

Republicans hold 23 and Democrats 12 of the 35 seats up in 2026. Democrats need a net gain of 4 seats for a 51-seat majority. Under the resolution rules, a 50-50 split goes to Republicans because the Vice President (JD Vance) is a Republican.

Cook rates 7 Senate races as Toss Up, all of them Republican-held: AK (Sullivan), IA (open), KS (Marshall), ME (Collins), MI (open, Democratic-held), OH (Husted) and TX (open). Note that MI is Democratic-held, so 6 of the 7 are Republican-held. Cook rates NH (open, D) as Lean Democrat and GA (Ossoff) and NC (open, R) as Likely Democrat.

On Oct 6 Cook moved Kansas from Lean Republican to Toss Up, New Hampshire from Toss Up to Lean Democrat and North Carolina from Lean Democrat to Likely Democrat. The analysis is titled 'A Senate Majority is Squarely in Democrats' Sights.'
Inside Elections' Oct 1 changes: Alaska moved from Tilt R to Toss-up, Georgia and North Carolina from Tilt D to Lean D, and Michigan from Toss-up to Tilt R.

RCP polling averages in Republican-held seats: NC Cooper (D) +9.0 over Whatley; ME Jackson (D) +0.7 over Collins; OH Brown (D) +3.2 over Husted; TX Talarico (D) +3.1 over Paxton; IA Turek (D) +0.7 over Hinson; AK Peltola (D) +1.8 over Sullivan.

In the three cycles before 2022, more than half of late battleground-state polls missed by more than 3 points. In 2016 and 2020 almost all of the error ran toward Democrats (Republicans outperformed their polls). Example: in Maine in 2020, no poll showed Collins leading, and she won by 9 points.

Wang estimated that national Senate polling error in midterm years is about five times larger than in presidential years and can run in either direction. Republicans outperformed their polls in the 1994 and 2002 midterms.
Generic ballot (dated): Data for Progress had Democrats +8 in May 2026. A tracker average from spring 2026 was about D+5. No October 2026 generic-ballot reading was found.

Election Day is November 3, 2026, and the question closes Nov 4 at 04:59 UTC. Alaska's ranked-choice count and any runoffs (such as Georgia's, if no one gets 50%) could settle seats after Election Day, and runoffs count under the rules.

Chicago is expected to use Sean Burke in some role, though manager Will Venable has not committed to one. Burke allowed 1 hit and 1 run in 5 1/3 innings of bulk relief in Game 2 and went 2-0 with a 1.04 ERA in three regular-season appearances (two starts) against Cleveland.

Cleveland finished the regular season 85-77 and won its third straight AL Central title, clinching on Sept 26, as the AL's No. 2 seed with a first-round bye. Chicago finished 84-78, one game back, as the No. 6 seed. Cleveland went 24-10 over its last 34 games to pass Chicago.

In the newest Suffolk University poll (Oct 1–4, 500 likely voters, margin of error ±4.4), Democrat Josh Turek led Republican Ashley Hinson 48% to 44%. Libertarian Thomas Laehn had about 2%. Newsweek reported that the RealClearPolling average on Oct 7 had Turek ahead 46.2% to 45.2%.

The Fox News poll (Sept 24–28) had Turek ahead of Hinson 49% to 47% among 1,008 likely voters (±3) and 50% to 46% among 1,204 registered voters (±2.5). Fox said the registered-voter gap had not changed since June.

In 2020, the final Iowa Senate polling average had Ernst ahead by about 0.4 points, but she beat Greenfield 51.8% to 45.2% (R+6.6). The polls underestimated the Republican by about 6 points.

Vučić dissolved the National Assembly and called snap parliamentary elections for 25 October 2026. The vote had been due by December 2027. He cited EXPO 2027 in Belgrade as one of his reasons. The question closes on the same day as the election.

Vučić resigned as president on 27 September, cutting his second term short by more than seven months. He is leading SNS in the election. AP reports that if his party wins a majority of seats, parliament is expected to elect him prime minister. He launched his campaign at a packed Belgrade arena on 3 October.

Vučić heads list no. 1, 'Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia' (SNS-led, 209,130 signatures), as SNS's candidate for Prime Minister. All 250 seats are up and 126 are needed for a majority. Seats are allocated by d'Hondt in one nationwide constituency with a 3% threshold, and minority parties are exempt from the threshold.

Faktor Plus poll, 16–20 Sept, n=986: United Serbia 48.6% (+1.4), Student List 37.1% (+5.6), SPS 4.9%, European Serbia 3.6%, NADA 2.8%. Stated willingness to vote was 62%. Faktor Plus is described as pro-government-leaning. I found no October poll or independent poll.
The page says the SNS–Student List race has tightened. Some polls put SNS first and others put the Student List first. It gives no poll figures in its text.

The People's Serbia coalition withdrew its list on 22 September to back the Student List (list no. 3, ballot carrier Ilija Srdanović). Faktor Plus also said the People's Movement of Serbia, Ecological Uprising and New Face of Serbia had withdrawn, which consolidated the opposition vote.

Other lists: 'Factor of Stability!' led by Ivica Dačić (SPS, JS, SDPS, Zeleni), which is the ruling coalition's traditional partner; European Serbia (Tepić/Ponoš, SSP and SRCE); Authentic Right (NADA). Fifteen other lists, including minority lists, were also submitted.

In the 2024 cycle, parliament had one month to constitute itself after final results, then 90 days to form a government. The president nominates the PM-designate, who presents a programme and cabinet for an Assembly vote. If no government is elected in time, parliament is dissolved and new elections are called.

The question closes on 25 October 2026, election day. Any Assembly vote electing a new prime minister would come after the new parliament's constitutive session, about 30 days after final results, so it would fall after the close date. The resolution window runs to 30 June 2028.
In the December 2023 snap election, the SNS-led list won about 47% and regained a majority, with preliminary projections of about 129 of 250 seats.
In 2022, SNS took about 43% and roughly 120 seats. It stayed the largest party but lost its outright majority (126). It still formed a government with partners.

In 2020, the SNS-led 'For Our Children' coalition won 188 of 250 seats, a two-thirds majority, in a vote boycotted by most opposition parties. In 2016, SNS won 131 seats. SNS-led lists have finished first in every parliamentary election from 2014 to 2023. 2012 is not verified here.

This election follows about two years of student-led protests that began after the November 2024 Novi Sad railway station disaster, with more than 100,000 people protesting at the March 2025 peak. Vučić previously served as Serbia's prime minister from 2014 to 2017, before becoming president.

Tesla's stake in SpaceX is under 1%. It comes from Tesla's roughly $2B investment in xAI Series E preferred stock, which converted into SpaceX equity when SpaceX absorbed xAI. Tesla and SpaceX also have a 'framework agreement' on collaboration and the joint Terafab chip project.
On the July 22 call, Tesla's general counsel described "numerous beneficial transactions" with SpaceX, and the CFO said Q2 net income included a $1B mark-to-market gain on Tesla's SpaceX holdings.

More than 900 million SpaceX shares unlocked on August 6, 2026. Third-party trackers (unverified) list further tranches around October 24 and after SpaceX's Q3 report, with full expiry on December 8, 2026. Musk's shares are locked up until one year after the June 2026 IPO.

In late January 2026, Bloomberg and Reuters reported that Musk was weighing a SpaceX–Tesla tie-up, a SpaceX–xAI merger, or a three-way combination. The SpaceX–xAI deal went ahead and Tesla was not combined. (Recalled, unverified here: the SpaceX–xAI merger was announced in early February 2026, within days of the reports.)

Wedbush's Dan Ives frames any combination as coming in 2027, after the SpaceX IPO. Oppenheimer says a deal is 'plausible' but does not see a near-term merger. Morningstar flags Tesla shareholders' concern about SpaceX's valuation as an obstacle.

Precedent: when Musk proposed taking Tesla private in 2018, the board formed a three-member special committee of independent directors and hired outside counsel. The process ended without a deal. A Musk-related-party transaction would likely require a similar committee process before any definitive agreement.

To resolve Yes, a definitive, binding agreement must be announced through official channels before November 1, 2026. Musk hints, intent statements and reports of talks (like the September 15 and July 22 remarks) do not qualify.
RealClearPolling's average of polls from Sept. 15 to Oct. 6 has Democrat Abdul El-Sayed at 48.1% and Republican Mike Rogers at 44.9%, a lead of 3.2 points for El-Sayed. The page may have been cached.
FiftyPlusOne's Michigan Senate polling average as of Oct. 8 has El-Sayed at 48.0% and Rogers at 44.5%.
Quantus Insights polled 744 likely voters on Oct. 5–6 and found El-Sayed at 48% and Rogers at 47%. A YouGov poll fielded Sept. 28–Oct. 5 had El-Sayed at 49% and Rogers at 48%.

A Mitchell Research poll fielded Oct. 1 has El-Sayed at 45.6% and Rogers at 41.4%, with 6% undecided and a 3.8-point margin of error. Four minor-party candidates (Libertarian, Natural Law, U.S. Taxpayers and Green) each got 3% or less, and 11% of respondents had already voted absentee. Mitchell pointed to Republicans gaining in the final weeks of past Michigan Senate races.
In a Fox News poll, El-Sayed led Rogers 50% to 49% among likely voters and 51% to 48% among registered voters. Fox's Aug. 6–10 poll had Rogers ahead 51% to 47% among registered voters.
A Michigan State University IPPSR poll had El-Sayed ahead of Rogers, 48% to 44%. An earlier poll reported in July had El-Sayed trailing Rogers by double digits while Haley Stevens was tied with him.

El-Sayed won the Aug. 4 Democratic primary with about 48.5% to Rep. Haley Stevens' 47.5%, a margin of about 15,000 votes. Stevens conceded and endorsed him. Rogers had no opponent in the Republican primary, and Mallory McMorrow withdrew from the Democratic race in July. The seat is open because Democratic Sen. Gary Peters is retiring.

El-Sayed and Rogers held a very combative first debate in Grand Rapids on Oct. 8, covering gas prices, the war with Iran and tariffs. El-Sayed called Rogers a Trump loyalist, and Rogers called El-Sayed a 'con man'.

El-Sayed is being outspent nearly 2-to-1 on ads. Groups aligned with Republicans had spent nearly $3 million by mid-September on ads tying El-Sayed to the streamer Hasan Piker, according to AdImpact data. Rogers released an ad calling for an end to the tariff war with Canada.
A second debate, hosted by WXYZ-TV, is scheduled for Oct. 21. The general election is Nov. 3, 2026, and absentee voting in Michigan began Sept. 24.

In 2024, Democrat Elissa Slotkin beat Rogers by about 0.3 points (48.6% to 48.3%, roughly 19,000 votes) even though Trump carried Michigan. Late polls had mostly shown Slotkin ahead by a few points, for example 47% to 42% in an EPIC-MRA poll.
The last time a Republican won a U.S. Senate race in Michigan was 1994. Democrats have won every Michigan Senate race since then, including 2024.

In a Faktor Plus poll (fieldwork 16–20 Sept 2026, n=986), Vučić's 'United Serbia' list had 48.6% (+1.4) and 'Student List – Students Win' had 37.1% (+5.6). SPS had 4.9%, European Serbia 3.6% and Authentic Right 2.8%, with projected turnout of 62%.

An NSPM poll with fieldwork in the first ten days of September 2026 put the Student List at about 44.3–44.4% of decided respondents and Vučić's list at 41.7%. The previous NSPM round had 39.6% vs 37.5%. No sample size was published, and the fieldwork came before the election was called and before several parties withdrew in favour of the Student List.

raw_facts.source: Wikipedia, Opinion polling for the 2026 Serbian parliamentary election
raw_facts.fact: An earlier Faktor Plus poll (about 4 Sept 2026, n=1,200) had the SNS-led list at 47.2% and the Student List at 31.5%. About one in three voters was undecided. Opposition and independent media accuse Faktor Plus and Ipsos of pro-government bias.

raw_facts.source: bne IntelliNews (CRTA / Stanford Democracy Action Lab)
raw_facts.fact: A CRTA/Stanford DAL poll (June 2026 fieldwork) found 44.9% of decided voters backing the Student List versus 35.7% for SNS. It was reported as the first regular national poll since July 2010 to place a party other than SNS first.

Searches as of early October 2026 found no poll with October fieldwork. The latest published figures are still the late-September Faktor Plus and NSPM releases, and Vukadinović said a new NSPM poll could come out in early or mid-October.

All 250 seats are elected by closed-list PR in a single nationwide constituency using D'Hondt. The threshold is 3% of votes cast, and minority lists are exempt. On the ballot, list 1 is 'Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia' (SNS, PUPS, SPS-excluded allies, SRS and others) and list 3 is 'Student List – Students Are Winning'. SPS runs separately as list 2 ('Ivica Dačić – Factor of Stability!').

DS, the Green–Left Front, PSG (which left European Serbia), POKS, SPO, Kreni-Promeni, SDS, LSV, Dveri and Enough is Enough are not running their own lists and are backing the Student List. The People's Serbia coalition (NPS, NLS, EU) withdrew its list on 22 Sept to back the Student List.

The opposition vote is still split among several separate lists: European Serbia (SSP, SRCE, Solidarity), Authentic Right/NADA (NDSS, Monarchists), and Alternative for Serbia. NADA said NDSS would join a Student List-led government if it crosses the threshold.

Vučić dissolved the Assembly on 9 Sept 2026 and resigned the presidency on 27 Sept to head the SNS list as its prime ministerial candidate. The Student List is led by Ilija Srdanović, a Novi Sad cardiologist.

The list 'Izbor naroda' withdrew after endorsing the Student List. Vreme reported that Nestorović's list, which Vukadinović said could have passed the threshold, also exited. RIK had to publish the final summary list by 9 October.

Election day is 25 Oct 2026, with polls open 07:00–20:00 and campaign silence starting two days before. Televised debates ran from 24 Sept to 9 Oct. The Student List has called on citizens to take to the streets after polls close.

raw_facts.source: Wikipedia, Opinion polling for the 2023 Serbian parliamentary election
raw_facts.fact: In the December 2023 election, the SNS list got about 46.7–48.0% (129 seats) and the opposition SPN got about 23.6–24.3% (65 seats). The final NSPM poll (12 Dec, 39.8 vs 25.6) and OFID poll (38.7 vs 27.1) underestimated SNS by roughly 8–9 points. Ipsos (44.6 vs 23.6) was closest.

SNS-led lists have won the most seats in every Serbian parliamentary election since 2012: 2012, 2014, 2016, 2020, 2022 and 2023, which is 6 of 6 (count recalled, unverified per election). The 2023 vote was marred by monitor-reported irregularities.

Observers describe Serbian elections as run under unfair conditions, including media dominance by the ruling party. Separately, pro-government tabloids have run campaigns against Srdanović using AI-manipulated photos, according to fact-checkers.
An earlier CRTA telephone poll (13–27 Sept 2025, n=2,020) found 44% support for a student list versus 32% for Vučić's bloc. This is older trend context from before the 2026 lists were formed.

Israeli sources told CNN the co-pilot probably acted alone. Another Israeli source said Israel knows of no link to any group or government so far, though the investigation is at an early stage.
Asked whether Iran was involved, Netanyahu said it was too early to say. Mossad and Shin Bet were investigating, and an initial assessment suggested the co-pilot was likely acting alone.

President Trump said the attacker could be linked to Iran 'based on what I'm hearing' and later said he personally thinks Iran was behind it. Investigators have not confirmed any Iran link, and Israel has not officially suggested one.

According to an unconfirmed Channel 12 report, the co-pilot told investigators 'I did it as revenge for Gaza' and wanted to die a martyr. No official conclusion has linked Iran or any terrorist organization to planning the attack. Shin Bet has joined the UAE investigation.

A LinkedIn profile linked to al-Hammami posted images of Israeli aircraft and al-Qaida figures (Sunni jihadist, not on the market's list of Iran affiliates) about nine hours after the attack. Who wrote the posts is unclear. According to the UAE, his radicalization began in 2017.

The WSJ reported that Omani authorities had barred al-Hammami from flying over concerns about extremist views. The UAE attorney general called the attack a terrorist act. The article mentions no links to Iran, Hamas or Hezbollah.
Two Israeli officials said the co-pilot told UAE interrogators he planned the attack before flydubai hired him. An Israeli official said the inquiry suggests he acted alone.
No formal charges have been announced, and the UAE and Israeli investigations into possible accomplices are still open. Flydubai flights to Israel are suspended until further notice.

Netanyahu's 'Islamist radical indoctrination' remarks would count only as inspiration or ideological influence, which does not qualify. To resolve Yes, an official Israeli statement must say Iran or a listed proxy ordered, planned, carried out or directly coordinated the attack.

raw_facts.fact: Lindsey Graham won the June 9 GOP primary but died on July 11, 2026. Gov. McMaster appointed his sister Darline Graham on July 13, with backing from Trump and Thune. She was sworn in July 14 and is now the Republican nominee. Democrat Annie Andrews won her primary with 61.5% over Brandon Brown.
The Aug 11 special GOP primary produced no majority winner. In the Aug 25 runoff, Darline Graham beat Rep. Ralph Norman with 52.5% of the vote.

Recent polls: InsiderAdvantage (Sept 28–29, 1,200 likely voters, ±2.83) Graham 46%, Andrews 45%; Trafalgar (Sept 23–25, 1,087 LV, ±2.9) Graham 43%, Andrews 42%, with about 8.5% undecided; InsiderAdvantage (Sept 8–9) Graham 45%, Andrews 43%.
A Rasmussen poll from about mid-September (exact date unverified) had Graham 48%, Andrews 43% among likely voters, with 9% not sure.

In 2020, final polls showed Lindsey Graham ahead of Jaime Harrison by 2–3 points (Data for Progress 49–46; Morning Consult 46–44), but Graham won by about 10. The polls understated the Republican margin by about 7–8 points.

The last Democrat elected to the US Senate from South Carolina was Ernest Hollings in 1998, and the last Democrat to carry the state for president was Carter in 1976. Republican presidential margins were Trump +18 (2024), about +12 (2020), +14 (2016), Romney +10 (2012) and McCain +9 (2008).
