Seasonally adjusted CPI-U rose 0.4% in August 2026, after 0.1% in July. Before seasonal adjustment it was up 3.4% over 12 months. Core CPI rose 0.3% on the month and 2.4% on the year.
Recent seasonally adjusted monthly headline CPI changes were: Mar 2026 +0.9%, Apr +0.6%, May +0.5%, Jun -0.4%, Jul +0.1%, Aug +0.4%. Two of the last six months were above 0.5%.

In August 2026 the gasoline index rose 3.9% (after -2.9% in July), making up over a third of the all-items increase. Energy rose 2.1%, shelter 0.3% and food 0.1%. Energy was up 16.3% and gasoline 27.4% over 12 months.

EIA data put the September 2026 average US gasoline price at $4.36 a gallon, up from $4.06 in August and $3.93 in July. That is roughly a 7.3–7.4% rise from August to September before seasonal adjustment ($4.355 vs $4.058 per EIA weekly survey averages).
EIA weekly US regular gasoline retail prices were $4.478 on 2026-09-21, $4.465 on 2026-09-28 and $4.354 on 2026-10-05.

The AAA national average rose from $4.14 (Sept 3) to $4.27 (Sept 10), $4.43 (Sept 17) and a peak of $4.48. AAA's September 2026 monthly average was $4.33, 50 cents above the previous September record of $3.83 (2023). By Oct 1 the average had fallen to $4.41.
AAA said crude oil ran near $100 a barrel earlier in September before dipping back into the $90s, and named volatility in the Strait of Hormuz as a key factor.

September seasonal factors assume pump prices normally ease that month. So a rise in unadjusted gasoline prices in September becomes a larger rise once seasonally adjusted, and the adjusted CPI is the figure the question uses.

The September 2026 CPI is scheduled for Wednesday, October 14, 2026 at 8:30 a.m. ET. The question closes at 8:25 a.m. ET that day and resolves on the published single-decimal seasonally adjusted monthly change, so 0.6% or higher means Yes.
BLS headline monthly CPI-U changes are seasonally adjusted and rounded to one decimal. A published 0.5% does not count as 'more than 0.5%'.
In September 2025 the gasoline index rose 4.1% and was the largest factor in the monthly increase, but headline seasonally adjusted CPI rose only 0.3%.

In 2024, Brown lost his Ohio Senate seat to Bernie Moreno 46.5% to 50.1% (Moreno +3.6). The final RCP average (Oct 23 to Nov 4) was Moreno +1.7, and a 270toWin six-poll average had Brown 47.3 to Moreno 47.0. Republicans beat the polls by about 2 to 4 points. In early October 2024, Marist and the Washington Post had shown Brown up by about 2.

In 2022, JD Vance beat Tim Ryan 53.0% to 46.9% (R +6.1). The final 270toWin six-poll average was Vance 52.0 to Ryan 44.2 (about R +7.8), and RCP's final listing was Vance +6.5. That year the polls overstated the Republican margin by roughly 0.4 to 1.7 points.
A late-June 2026 New York Times/Siena poll had Husted ahead 50% to 47%. A September 2025 Emerson poll had Husted +6. Husted led in early polling before Brown moved ahead in later surveys.

AdImpact puts ad spending in the race at $298M, the most of any 2026 Senate race. Republican-aligned super PACs put about $14M into Ohio ads in the week before Sept 18, and Trump-linked No Going Back PAC has spent more than $13.4M there. Senate Leadership Fund has pledged $79M for Husted and Senate Majority PAC $64M for Brown.
Brown raised more than $17.1M in Q2 2026 to Husted's $7.7M, outraising him for a fourth straight quarter. Through June 30, Brown had raised about $38.6M in total and Husted about $14.3M.
Q3 2026 campaign finance reports are due October 15, 2026, and Election Day is November 3, 2026. The race is a special election for the rest of JD Vance's term, which runs through January 2029.

As of about early August 2026, neither campaign had agreed to a Senate debate. A Husted spokesperson pointed out that Brown skipped a debate with Moreno in 2024. These searches found no scheduled Brown-Husted debate.

The nominees are Husted (R, appointed by Gov. DeWine in January 2025, unopposed in the primary) and Brown (D, won the primary with 89.4%). Also running are Libertarian Bill Redpath and independent Greg Levy (PSL). This is Ohio's first U.S. Senate special election since 1954.

Day 1 ended early because of bad light, then light drizzle led officials to call off play for the day. That left about 24.4 of the scheduled 90 overs unbowled.
Day 2 was due to start at 9:30 AM SAST, with the middle session extended to 12:10–2:40 PM to recover lost time. The match is scheduled to run until Oct 13, three days before the question closes.
As of this research, no Day 2 score had been indexed. The latest confirmed score is still Australia 187/6 at the Day 1 close.
Australia slumped to 124/6 before the Cummins–Renshaw fightback, with returning fast bowler Nortje and Jansen among the wicket-takers.

The pitch gave seam movement and occasional sharp bounce, and spin is expected to matter more as it wears. Australia were without Cameron Green (abdominal strain) and Josh Inglis (fractured finger). South Africa were without Kagiso Rabada (hamstring).

Forecasts showed Day 2 (Oct 10) cloudy with about a 10% chance of rain. Day 3 (Oct 11) was flagged as the most likely day to lose play to rain. Days 4–5 (Oct 12–13) looked partly sunny to cloudy with limited rain chance.

In South Africa's 10 Durban Tests before March 2022, they won 2 and lost 7. That implies about 1 draw in 10, but it is inferred and unverified.

raw_facts.fact: On October 8, 2026, Trump posted on Truth Social that the US will not attack Iran before the November 3 midterms. In the same post he said the naval blockade of Iranian ports 'will remain in full force and effect.' He said Steve Witkoff is 'doing very well' in negotiations with Iran.

Iranian FM Abbas Araghchi said on October 8 that Tehran is 'reviewing the views of the Americans' and will reply to the latest US proposal 'within the next few days.' Messages are passing through mediators. He pointed again to Iran's 'Seven-Day Plan,' under which Hormuz would reopen once US conditions, including lifting the blockade, are met.
CENTCOM said on October 5 that it had redirected its 130th commercial vessel since the blockade resumed on July 14. Over the past 12 weeks it has disabled 3 ships and destroyed 13.

The US blockade of Iranian ports is still in place, and Iranian leaders admit it is crippling the economy. Iran's oil exports remain blocked, and Oil Minister Paknejad resigned as oil available for export ran out. Trump said 'either Iran signs the deal, or it won't exist any longer,' and senior officials met at Camp David the previous Friday.

Before Trump's October 8 post, Axios reported that the Pentagon had been told to prepare possible fresh strikes on Iran, with no set date. Trump had not made a final decision on resuming major combat operations.

Trump called 'unacceptable' Iran's seven-day proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and resume nuclear talks if the US lifted the naval blockade and waived oil sanctions. Mediators kept working after the rejection.

Axios reported that Trump was willing to ease sanctions and unfreeze Iranian assets in return for concrete Iranian nuclear steps. A US official said there would be no deal 'unless the nuclear issues are addressed' and that the sides remained apart on sequencing. BLS's unadjusted core CPI index (all items less food and energy) was 338.041 in August 2026 and 329.970 in August 2025. BLS reported the 12-month change as 2.4%. Computed from these index levels, the unrounded change is about 2.445%, just under the 2.45% that would round to 2.5%.
Core CPI rose 0.3% in August 2026 (seasonally adjusted), and its 12-month rate was 2.4%, down from 2.5% in July. It was the lowest core rate since March 2021. Headline CPI was 3.4% year over year.

Seasonally adjusted monthly core CPI changes in 2026: Feb 0.2%, Mar 0.2%, Apr 0.4%, May 0.2%, Jun 0.0%, Jul 0.2%, Aug 0.3%. Shelter rose 0.3% in August after two months of 0.1%, and shelter's 12-month rate was 3.0%, down from 3.2% in July.

raw_facts.source: Ball State CBER (BLS data); BLS September 2025 CPI release
raw_facts.fact: The base month dropping out of the comparison is September 2025, when the unadjusted core index was 330.54 (two decimals; the three-decimal value 330.542 is unverified). Core rose 0.2% m/m seasonally adjusted that month and 3.0% year over year. Computed: the unadjusted index rose about 0.17% from August to September 2025.

For the published one-decimal 12-month rate to be 2.5% or higher, the unadjusted September 2026 core index needs to reach about 338.64 (330.54 × 1.0245). That is a rise of about 0.18% or more from August's 338.041. If the rise matches September 2025's roughly 0.17%, the rate stays near 2.44–2.45%.
BLS is scheduled to release the September 2026 CPI on Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. ET. The question closes at 12:25 UTC that day.
August 2026 core CPI came in 0.1 percentage point above the consensus on a monthly basis (0.3% vs 0.2%). The annual rate of 2.4% matched the consensus. Gasoline was up 27.4% year over year.
In September 2025, core CPI rose 0.2% m/m seasonally adjusted, after 0.3% in both July and August 2025. Shelter rose 0.2% m/m, and owners' equivalent rent rose 0.13% (Goldman Sachs breakdown).
